Groet van liefde in de gezegende naam van onze Heer en Heiland, Jezus Christus. Veel christenen hebben de afgelopen jaren een tijd van beproeving en beproefdheid doorgemaakt, maar we vertrouwen erop dat ieder met Paulus kan zeggen… Niet dat ik dit zeg omdat ik gebrek lijd; ik heb geleerd in welke toestand ik ook verkeer, tevreden te zijn. —Filippenzen 4:11.

De zomer is hevig bij ons aangebroken, samen met de hitte en de vochtigheid die hier in Ohio bij zomers horen. Het voorjaar, samen met het normale plantseizoen, was extra langgerekt. Maar inmiddels is het meeste van wat lokaal bekendstaat als “het voorjaarswerk” voltooid. De gewassen van de boeren en de kruiden van de tuinders steken hun kopjes door de koele aarde en zoeken naar de warmte en het licht van de zon.

In dit nummer kunt u een wandeling maken op de weg naar Emmaüs en proberen uzelf in de sandalen van Jezus’ discipelen te plaatsen terwijl zij zich verwonderden over de plotselinge wending van gebeurtenissen rond Christus’ dood, begrafenis en vermeende “opstanding”. U kunt proberen uzelf voor te stellen bij Daniël van weleer, terwijl hij ervoor koos zoals gewoonlijk bij zijn open raam te blijven bidden, terwijl hij heel goed wist dat deze eenvoudige handeling zijn leven voorgoed kon veranderen. U kunt samen met de kleine “Ellie” verwonderd zijn over hoe God al voldeed aan “de verlangens van haar hart” nog voordat zij wist dat de zaken niet volgens plan verliepen.

Iets nieuws in dit nummer is het begin van een serie van broeder Donald Brechbill over “discipelschap”. Disciple (leerling) heeft bijna dezelfde spelling als discipline (discipline). Voor velen draagt discipline een negatieve bijklank, wat hopelijk de lezer niet ervan zal weerhouden zich te laten aantrekken door wat broeder Donald te delen heeft. Laten we ons herinneren dat Jezus het persoonlijke voorbeeld gaf van het discipelschapmodel—Hij koos en riep “discipelen” om Hem te volgen en van Hem te leren. Later zond Hij hen twee aan twee uit om te onderwijzen en meer discipelen te maken. En toen Hij de “Grote Opdracht” gaf, was die gericht aan Zijn discipelen van dat moment, en aan alle toekomstige discipelen—de Kerk van Jezus Christus. We vertrouwen dat ieder geïnspireerd kan raken door deze serie.

In komende nummers zijn we van plan een “Lied van het Kwartaal” en een rubriek over verschillende aspecten van de “Kerkgeschiedenis” op te nemen. U kunt voor ons bidden terwijl we doorgaan met het voortzetten van ons werk en ons tijdschrift.

Even een vriendelijke herinnering… We moedigen feedback van onze lezers aan. Als u bijzonder gezegend bent door een bepaald artikel, is terugkoppeling nuttig voor ons als bestuur en bemoedigend voor onze schrijvers. Ook als er iets specifieks is dat iemand graag in toekomstige nummers van het tijdschrift zou zien, verwelkomen wij die input. Dit helpt ons als bestuur ideeën te krijgen bij het kiezen van artikelen en bij het vragen aan auteurs om te schrijven.

In het voorjaar van 2022 hebben we enkele veranderingen doorgevoerd in onze bediening in onze pogingen het werk van The Berean Voice voort te zetten in de toekomst. Personeelswijzigingen:

Broeder Andrew (onze ontwerper) is steeds drukker geworden als jonge vader met een groeiend gezin en als diaken in onze lokale gemeente. Gezien deze uitdaging besloot het bestuur Andrews verlangen te steunen om iemand te vinden die hem (voorlopig) kan helpen met het grootste deel van het ontwerpproces voor elk nummer van ons tijdschrift—The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Daardoor kunnen er in komende nummers enige kleine veranderingen in de “stijl” van het ontwerp optreden.

In het voorjaar van 2022 werd besloten nieuwe bestuursleden te zoeken ter vervanging van enkelen die de afgelopen jaren vanwege persoonlijke verantwoordelijkheden waren gestopt. Na gebed om de wijsheid en leiding des Heren, en na overleg met het leiderschap van onze kerk, werden broeder Joe Mast en broeder Sheldon Bower gekozen om de open plaatsen in het bestuur te vullen. Deze broeders hebben beiden deze roeping vriendelijk aanvaard en laten God al hun geestelijke gaven gebruiken om verschil te maken.

Broeder Joe Tindall is sinds ons begin in juni 2016 bestuurslid van The Berean Voice geweest. Vanwege zijn leeftijd (83) verzocht broeder Joe ontslag als bestuurslid. Tijdens onze maandelijkse bestuursvergadering in mei 2022 heeft het bestuur aan dat verzoek van broeder Joe voldaan. We zullen de stabiliteit van zijn stille wijsheid tijdens onze bestuursvergaderingen en bij onze selectie van artikelen missen. Bid alstublieft met ons voor broeder Joe en zijn gezin nu hij en zijn vrouw het einde van hun leven en alles wat bij die levensfase hoort tegemoetzien—dat zij trouw en moedig mogen blijven.

Moge God ieder zegenen en bewaren.

Curvin L Wenger

Greetings of love in the blessed name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Many Christians have gone through a time of trial and testing during the past several years, yet we trust that each one is able to say with Paul… Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content –Philippians 4:11.

Summer is hard upon us, along with the heat and humidity that goes along with summers here in Ohio. Springtime, along with the normal planting season, was extra long and drawn out. But, by now, most of what is known locally as “the spring work” has been finished. The farmers’ crops and the gardeners’ herbs are pushing through the cool soil and towards the heat and light of the sun.

In this issue you can take a stroll on the road to Emmaus and try to put yourself in the sandals of Jesus’ disciples as they puzzled over the sudden turn of events surrounding Christ’s death, burial, and alleged “resurrection”. You can try to picture yourself with Daniel of old as he chose to keep praying like normal at his open window, while knowing full well that this simple act most likely could change his life forever. You can marvel with little “Ellie” how God met the “desires of her heart” even before she knew things weren’t working out according to plan.

Something new in this issue is the beginning of a series by Brother Donald Brechbill on “discipleship”. Disciple has almost the same spelling as discipline. For many, discipline carries a negative connotation, which hopefully will not interfere with the reader being drawn to what Brother Donald has to share. Let’s remember that Jesus gave personal example of the discipleship model—He chose and called “disciples” to follow and learn from Him. Later He sent them out two by two to teach and make more disciples. And then when He gave the “Great Commission” it was to His disciples at that time, and to all future disciples—the Church of Jesus Christ. We trust that each one can be inspired by this series.

Coming up in future issues, we are planning to have a “Song of the Quarter” and a section on various aspects of “Church History”. You can pray for us as we continue to move forward with our ministry and our magazine.

Just a friendly reminder… We encourage feedback from our readers. If you have been especially blessed by a certain article, feedback is helpful for us as a board, and it is encouraging for our writers. Also, if there is something specific that someone wishes to see included in future magazine issues, we welcome the input. This helps provide ideas for us as a board when choosing articles and when asking authors to write.

In the spring of 2022, we made some changes with our ministry in our endeavors to keep the work of The Berean Voice moving forward into the future. Personnel changes:

Brother Andrew (our designer) has become increasingly busy as a young father with a growing family and as a deacon for our local church congregation. In looking at this challenge, the board decided to support Andrew’s desire to find someone to help him (for now) with the bulk of the design work for each issue of our magazine—The Heartbeat of the Remnant. 愿我们主救主耶稣基督赐人爱的问候。过去数年，许多基督徒都经历了试炼和考验的时期，然而我们相信各人都能与保罗同声说…… 我并不是因缺乏而说这话；我无论在什么景况，都可以知足，这是我已经学会了——腓立比书4:11。

夏天已经来到，伴随着俄亥俄州夏日常有的暑热和湿气。春季和正常的播种季节相比，格外漫长而延宕。但现在，本地人所称的“大多数春季工作”已接近完成。农夫的庄稼和园丁的香草正从凉爽的土壤中破土，朝向太阳的热与光伸展。

在本期，你可以漫步在以马忤斯的路上，设身处地进入耶稣门徒的凉鞋，体会他们如何为基督的死、埋葬以及所谓“复活”的突发转折而困惑。你可以想象自己与旧日的但以理同在，尽管明知在敞开的窗前照常祷告这一简单行为很可能永远改变他的生命，他却仍选择持续祷告。你可以与小“埃莉”一同惊叹，上帝如何在她尚未察觉事情未按计划进行之前，就已回应“她心里的渴望”。

本期的新项之一是唐纳德·布雷奇比尔弟兄开办的“门徒训练”系列。门徒（disciple）与纪律（discipline）的拼写几乎相同。对许多人而言，纪律带有负面意味，但愿这不会妨碍读者被布雷奇比尔弟兄要分享的内容吸引。让我们记得，耶稣亲自作了门徒训练模式的榜样——祂拣选并呼召“门徒”跟随并向祂学习。后来祂差遣他们两个人一组出去教导并造就更多门徒。然后当祂颁布“大使命”时，是对当时的门徒说的，也对所有未来的门徒——耶稣基督的教会。我们相信每一位都能从这一系列中得着激励。

在未来的期刊中，我们计划设立“本季之歌”以及关于“教会历史”各方面的专栏。你可以为我们祷告，求主赐智慧，使我们在事工与杂志的推进上继续前行。

友情提醒……我们欢迎读者的反馈。如果某篇文章特别使你蒙福，反馈对我们董事会有帮助，也能鼓励作者。此外，若有人希望在未来的期刊中看到某些特定内容，我们欢迎提出建议。这有助于董事会在挑选文章与邀请作者撰写时提供思路。

在2022年春，我们为事工做出了一些调整，以求使《悯悯人的心跳》（The Berean Voice）这项工作继续面向未来前进。人事变动如下：

安德鲁弟兄（我们的设计师）作为一位年轻的父亲，家庭逐渐增员，并且在本地教会担任执事，因而日益繁忙。鉴于这一挑战，董事会决定支持安德鲁弟兄找人（暂时）协助承担每期杂志《悯悯人的心跳》的大部分设计工作——因此即将在后续期刊中出现的设计“风格”可能会有些微调整。

在2022年春，董事会决定寻求数位新成员来替代过去数年因个人责任而离任的数位成员。在为主寻求智慧与指引，并与我们教会的领导层咨询之后，乔·马斯特弟兄与谢尔登·鲍尔弟兄被选中填补董事会的空缺位置。这两位弟兄皆欣然接受这一呼召，且已开始让上帝使用他们的属灵恩赐来带来改变。

乔·廷道尔弟兄自2016年6月我们创刊以来一直是《悯悯人的心跳》的董事。因年事已高（83岁），乔弟兄请辞董事职务。在2022年5月的月会中，董事会尊重并准许了乔弟兄的请求。我们将在董事会议与文章甄选过程中怀念他那安静智慧所带来的稳健。请为乔弟兄与他的家人祷告，求主在他们面临生命末期与一切随之而来的处境时，赐他们持守信实与勇气。

愿上帝赐福并保守各位。

Curvin L Wenger

There is coming a day when all will be well.
The things that are bad will all be in hell.
But we must not forget that day has not come.
We are in a battle; we must still overcome.
The enemy rages, his time here is short.
He spreads all his lies, the truth to distort.
Sin in our lives, it is his great goal.
For he knows very well it will cost us our soul.
It need not be big; a small sin will do.
He’ll trick and deceive, each soul to pursue.
The darts of the wicked come from all sides.
When faced with God’s power, that devil—he hides!
When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

有一日将至，一切终将安好。
那些邪恶之事都将入于地狱。
但我们不可忘记，那日尚未来到。
我们正处争战；仍须得胜而行。
敌人咆哮，他在此的日子短促。
他撒布谎言，扭曲真理。
罪在我们生命中，是他的主要目标。
因他深知那将使我们失去灵魂之代价。
并非须为大罪；小罪即可成就。
他将诱骗欺瞒，追逐每一颗心。
恶者的箭矢从四面八方射来。
当面对神的大能，那魔鬼便躲藏不见！
当神与我们同在，他无法前进！
当神与我们同在，罪便无处生存！
因为耶和华的眼目来回巡视，
寻找一人完全，他要显出大能！
让我们远离微小，目光放远向前。
握住神的能力！现今是回应的时辰！

Esparce todas sus mentiras para distorsionar la verdad.
El pecado en nuestras vidas es su gran ambición.
Porque sabe muy bien que nos costará el alma.
No tiene que ser grande; un pecado pequeño bastará.
Engañará y embaucará, buscando cada alma.
Las saetas de los impíos vienen de todos los lados.
Cuando se enfrenta al poder de Dios, ¡ese diablo—se esconde!
¡Cuando Dios está con nosotros, no puede avanzar!
¡Cuando Dios está con nosotros, el pecado no tiene oportunidad ya!
Porque los ojos del Señor escudriñan de un lado a otro,
Para encontrar uno perfecto, ¡su poder Él mostrará con arrojo!
Dejemos lo menor y miremos mucho más allá.
¡Tomemos el poder de Dios! ¡Es hora de responder ya!

It’s been said that in the 1500s, after baptism, the Anabaptists lived an average of only 27 days. They were hunted and killed. They realized one thing—serving Christ would most certainly cost them everything. They forsook the comforts of easy living; they forsook it all. It could also have been a similar situation when Jesus walked on the earth, or shortly after He was killed.

…and he turned, and said unto them, If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple. For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish. Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple –Luke 14:25-33.

Jesus clearly asked His disciples to count the cost. And they must have counted the cost, for they faithfully gave all, including their lives, for Christ’s Kingdom. They realized they could have had the good things in this life; however, they also realized it would cost them the good things in the next.

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution –2 Timothy 3:12. If we look at the promises which Jesus gave us in His Word about persecution, and then compare them with the lives of Jesus’ followers today, we might be confused. And rightfully so.

He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked –1 John 2:6. Jesus says we should walk as He walked, He also tells us that we need to follow Him.

How did He walk? We know that Jesus had no place to lay His head—this was how He wanted it. We know that Jesus could have chosen to live where and how He wanted. He was, in fact, in control of the whole world, yet He was despised and rejected by the world and its system. When He spoke, people wanted to lay their hands on Him; they wanted to kill Him. He was not a popular person; He had few friends. In reality, He didn’t fit in, and He didn’t last long. Three years after His ministry began, He was killed. …He was numbered with the transgressors –Mark 15:28.

What about His followers today? Are they walking how He walked? And if not, why not?

We read about the children of Israel going through the wilderness. They fought and overtook the cities in their paths, killing all in the process. We read many accounts about how God instructed the children of Israel to kill all of the enemy, even the women and children. The following is one such account of many.

So the LORD our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining. And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many. And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city –Deuteronomy 3:3-6.

We read accounts like this in scripture, and it can cause us to cringe. It is almost as if life itself was not important. Even in the New Testament, death doesn’t seem to be that big of a deal. People lived and people died.

The first week after we moved to Haiti, I was driving through the city. Suddenly, right in front of me I saw a man lying in the street. Blood ran down the road and pooled in a low spot—he was dead. I was shocked. But what shocked me the most was that no one seemed to notice. People by the hundreds busily walked around him, not even looking at the man—no one cared.

Over the next six years we saw many dead or dying people—it became a normal scene.

If that was how it was back in the Bible times, and it is still how it is today in many countries of the world, maybe we are the ones that are out of the norm? Maybe we esteem life higher than God does. Maybe we are among those that Jesus spoke of when He said—He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal –John 12:25.

In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:19. We were created out of the dust, and after a few short years, we return to the very same dust.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –James 4:14. The Bible also calls our lives a vapor.

We all know what happens after that—the judgment, then eternity. So why do we care so much about this life? Maybe it is an American problem or a western problem.

It is obvious that Americans are looked upon as ‘more valuable’ than most other nationalities. If you are an American in a developing country, you are heralded as a king. If something happens to an American, it is quickly headline news. I once stood over the bodies of two murdered men. One of their close friends stood by, so I asked him how he was doing. He shrugged and said, “This is life”.

So why does life mean so much to us Americans? The answer is simple. We can obtain almost anything we want; money is easy to get, and we can live how we want. We can live in pleasure every day. We go to the store and buy what we want, when we want—we have it our way. This is just how it is; for most of us it is all we have ever known—the life of plenty. So how does this affect us?

This type of living makes it especially hard to ‘give all’ for Christ. It makes it difficult to obey Jesus’ command to …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15. It makes it difficult to say with the Apostle Paul, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. In reality, it makes it difficult to be a Christian.

When Jesus said… For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25, what did He mean? Could it mean literally just what it says: that when you fall in love with your own life, you cannot effectively follow Christ, so that in the end you will actually lose your life?

Can you go to the lost and forsake the comforts of this life if it’s those comforts that you love and live for? It’s not likely. What we have is “Americanized” Christians that will only go to the mission field if they can take their comforts with them. This produces rich, comfortable missionaries who, despite their best efforts, can’t win the lost, rather they make them jealous. Can we go into the cities and preach the gospel to the lost like so many before us have? Can we take time to teach and disciple the tens of thousands who are seeking? If we love our lives, we probably will not, since there is too much to lose and it’s a waste of good talent and opportunity. God help us.

When we are living to please the flesh and we have our lives figured out, it is hard for God to use us. We are puffed up. We tend to believe that God has blessed us because of all our possessions and our status in life; but isn’t this the prosperity gospel? What if that changed? Would we still consider ourselves to be blessed? Is it God or our own doing that causes us to be joyful? What if we found ourselves in John the Baptist’s shoes? Or the Apostle Paul’s? If we would be sitting in prison for doing nothing wrong, would our joy remain? It should if the Holy Spirit is living and working in our hearts. The Bible says that we can suffer joyfully!

Years ago, a coworker of mine was a happy fellow. He had a nice life. There was one problem—he did not believe there was a God. We would talk day after day. He would constantly tell me how happy he was and that one didn’t need to be a Christian to be happy. He would talk about his nice life, all that he possessed, his good job, his nice family. Interestingly enough, he truly did seem happy.

I would tell him that true happiness didn’t come from the things that we possess or the position that we find ourselves in, but he would just disagree. He also proclaimed that he lived a better life than most Christians that he knew. He also said he didn’t get angry like most Christians and could control himself. I tried to convince him that he was deceived. At times I would think I was getting somewhere with him, then later it would seem I was far from reaching him. One day he soberly admitted that I seemed to be different that most Christians he had known in the past, but that still wasn’t enough.

I left that job and lost contact with him. Recently, I ran into another one of my former coworkers. I quickly thought of my friend and asked how he was doing. He looked at me strangely and then shocked me to my core as he said, “He committed suicide”.

The devil wants us to love our life—it’s that simple. When we love our life, we focus on it, we cherish it. The last thing we want to do is lose our life, even if it is for something eternal.

When I was in the Marines, they would constantly remind us that our lives were not number one; our country was. There are many young men who put their country first. Many have gone and given their all; many have died.

In World War 2, the Japanese would try to sneak up to a fox hole housing soldiers and throw in a grenade. Many times, it didn’t end like the Japanese wanted, because someone would jump on the grenade, absorbing the explosion. Thousands gave their lives to save their friends and defend their country. But be sure, if their priorities were not in order (of country first before themselves), they would not have done so.

If someone today, in America, would risk their life for the sake of the gospel, he would be labeled as foolish, reckless, and immature. But what do we say about so many before us—the ones that gave their lives while standing for the same things that we say we believe today? And what about the thousands today who are putting their lives on the line in other countries—are they foolish? Let’s look at a very obvious example in Acts.

And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus. And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem. Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. –Acts 21:10-13.

What would we think of Paul’s actions today? Paul went to Jerusalem and was quickly taken, beaten, and put in prison. It was the beginning of the end for our dear brother. He was moved from prison to prison and eventually ended up in Rome where he was beheaded. What do you think the ones that tried to persuade him to not go to Jerusalem thought? Do you think they called him a fool? Did they shake their heads and say, “I told him not to go!”?

We cannot know for sure. However, I am sure that Paul was simply putting the kingdom of Christ first; his life did not matter. He was obeying God, and God had told him to go.

When we love our lives, it is very difficult to be an effective disciple of the Lord Jesus. We end up forsaking God’s calling and then we are stuck trying to live the Christian life alone, and without God—no spiritual help from above, causing us to fall way short of the mark.

It’s ironic that only when we forsake all, including our lives, will we find true peace and purpose for our lives. And when we love our lives, that is when we will lose them.

Rise up, O saints of God!
Have done with lesser things.
Give heart and soul and mind and strength
To serve the King of kings.

Rise up, O saints of God!
The kingdom tarries long.
Bring in the day of Christlike love
And end the night of wrong.

Lift high the cross of Christ!
Tread where His feet have trod.
Led onward by the Son of Man,
Rise up, O saints of God!

Let us rise up, as God’s people, and begin to be done with lesser things, with our gaze on things above, not on the things of this earth. Yes, we will stand out; we will be labeled fools and many other things. However, we will once again catch God’s attention and the fires of revival will once again burn!

Er wordt gezegd dat in de 1500‑er jaren de wederdopers na de doop gemiddeld slechts 27 dagen leefden. Ze werden opgejaagd en gedood. Ze realiseerden zich één ding—Christus dienen zou hen ongetwijfeld alles kosten. Ze lieten het gemak van een gemakkelijk leven achter; ze lieten alles achter. Het had ook een vergelijkbare situatie kunnen zijn toen Jezus op aarde rondliep, of kort nadat Hij werd gedood.

…en Hij keerde Zich om, en zei tot hen: Indien iemand tot Mij komt, en haat niet zijn vader en moeder, en vrouw en kinderen, en broeders en zusters, ja ook zijn eigen leven, die kan niet Mijn discipel zijn. En wie zijn kruis niet op zich neemt en Mij volgt, die kan niet Mijn discipel zijn. Wie van u, die een toren wil bouwen, gaat niet eerst zitten en berekent de kosten, of hij voldoende heeft om het te volbrengen? Opdat het niet gebeuren zal, dat nadat hij de grondslag gelegd heeft, en het niet kan voltooien, allen die het zien, beginnen hem te bespotten, zeggende: Deze man is begonnen te bouwen en kon het niet voltooien. Of welke koning, die tegen een andere koning ten strijde trekt, gaat niet eerst zitten en beraadslaagt of hij met tienduizend tegen hem opgewassen is die met twintigduizend komt? Anders, terwijl de ander nog ver weg is, zendt hij een gezantschap en vraagt voorwaarden van vrede. Zo ook, wie van u niet al zijn goederen verlaat, die kan niet Mijn discipel zijn – Lukas 14:25-33.

Jezus vroeg Zijn discipelen duidelijk de kosten te berekenen. En zij moeten de kosten berekend hebben, want zij gaven trouw alles, inclusief hun leven, voor het Koninkrijk van Christus. Zij realiseerden zich dat ze de goede dingen in dit leven hadden kunnen krijgen; echter, zij realiseerden zich ook dat het hen de goede dingen in het volgende leven zou kosten.

Ja, en allen die godzalig willen leven in Christus Jezus zullen vervolging lijden –2 Timotheüs 3:12. Als we kijken naar de beloften die Jezus ons in Zijn Woord gaf over vervolging, en die vervolgens vergelijken met het leven van Jezus’ volgelingen vandaag, kunnen we in verwarring raken. En terecht.

Wie zegt dat hij in Hem blijft, die behoort zelf ook alzo te wandelen, gelijk Hij gewandeld heeft –1 Johannes 2:6. Jezus zegt dat wij moeten wandelen zoals Hij wandelde, Hij vertelt ons ook dat we Hem moeten volgen.

Hoe wandelde Hij? We weten dat Jezus geen plaats had om Zijn hoofd neer te leggen—dit was hoe Hij het wilde. We weten dat Jezus had kunnen kiezen waar en hoe Hij wilde leven. Hij had feitelijk de hele wereld in Zijn macht, toch werd Hij veracht en verworpen door de wereld en haar systeem. Als Hij sprak, wilden mensen Hem grijpen; ze wilden Hem doden. Hij was geen populair persoon; Hij had weinig vrienden. In werkelijkheid paste Hij niet, en hield Hij het niet lang vol. Drie jaar nadat Zijn bediening begon, werd Hij gedood. …Hij werd geteld onder de overtreders –Marcus 15:28.

Wat met Zijn volgelingen vandaag? Wandelen zij zoals Hij wandelde? En zo niet, waarom niet?

We lezen over de kinderen van Israël die door de woestijn trokken. Ze vochten en veroverden de steden op hun pad, waarbij ze allen in het proces doodden. We lezen vele verslagen over hoe God de kinderen van Israël opdroeg alle vijanden te doden, zelfs de vrouwen en kinderen. Het volgende is een van zulke vele verslagen.

Toen gaf de HEER, onze God, ook Og, koning van Basan, en al zijn volk in onze hand; en wij sloegen hem, totdat er geen overblijfsel overbleef. En wij veroverden al zijn steden toen, er was geen stad die wij niet van hen namen, zestig steden, heel het gebied van Argob, het koninkrijk van Og in Basan. Al deze steden waren versterkt met hoge muren, poorten en grendels; daarbij vele niet‑ommuurde stadjes. En wij verdelgden hen volkomen, zoals wij Sihon, de koning van Hesbon, verdelgden, en doden, vrouwen en kinderen, uit elke stad –Deuteronomium 3:3-6.

We lezen zulke verslagen in de Schrift, en het kan ons laten huiveren. Het is bijna alsof het leven zelf niet belangrijk was. Zelfs in het Nieuwe Testament lijkt de dood geen al te grote aangelegenheid. Mensen leefden en mensen stierven.

De eerste week nadat we naar Haïti verhuisden, reed ik door de stad. Plots zag ik vlak voor me een man op straat liggen. Bloed stroomde over de weg en verzamelde zich in een laagte—hij was dood. Ik was geschokt. Maar wat mij het meest schokte was dat niemand het leek op te merken. Honderden mensen liepen druk om hem heen, keken niet eens naar de man—niemand gaf erom.

In de volgende zes jaar zagen we veel doden of stervenden—het werd een normaal beeld.

Als dat zo was in de bijbelse tijden, en het is nog steeds zo in veel landen van de wereld, misschien zijn wij degenen die buiten de norm staan? Misschien hechten wij meer waarde aan het leven dan God doet. Misschien behoren wij tot degenen over wie Jezus sprak toen Hij zei—Wie zijn leven liefheeft, zal het verliezen; en wie zijn leven haat in deze wereld, zal het bewaren tot het eeuwige leven –Johannes 12:25.

In zweet zult gij uw brood eten, totdat gij wederkeert tot de aarde; want daarvan zijt gij genomen; stof zijt gij en tot stof zult gij wederkeren –Genesis 3:19. Wij zijn uit stof geschapen, en na een paar korte jaren keren wij terug tot hetzelfde stof.

Gij weet niet wat er van morgen zijn zal; want wat is uw leven? Het is als een damp, die kortstondig verschijnt en dan verdwijnt –Jakobus 4:14. De Bijbel noemt ons leven ook een damp.

We weten allemaal wat daarna gebeurt—het oordeel, daarna de eeuwigheid. Dus waarom geven we zoveel om dit leven? Misschien is het een Amerikaans probleem of een westers probleem.

Het is duidelijk dat Amerikanen worden gezien als ‘meer waardevol’ dan de meeste andere nationaliteiten. Als je een Amerikaan bent in een ontwikkelingsland, word je als een koning onthaald. Als er iets met een Amerikaan gebeurt, is het snel het hoofdnieuws. Ik stond ooit boven de lichamen van twee vermoorde mannen. Een van hun goede vrienden stond ernaast, dus vroeg ik hem hoe het met hem ging. Hij haalde zijn schouders op en zei: “Dit is het leven”.

Dus waarom betekent het leven zoveel voor ons Amerikanen? Het antwoord is simpel. We kunnen bijna alles verkrijgen wat we willen; geld is gemakkelijk te krijgen, en we kunnen leven hoe we willen. We kunnen elke dag in genot leven. We gaan naar de winkel en kopen wat we willen, wanneer we willen—wij krijgen het op onze manier. Zo is het nu eenmaal; voor de meesten van ons is het alles wat we ooit gekend hebben—het leven van overvloed. Dus hoe beïnvloedt dit ons?

Dit soort leven maakt het bijzonder moeilijk om ‘alles te geven’ voor Christus. Het maakt het moeilijk om Jezus’ bevel te gehoorzamen: …Ga in heel de wereld uit en predik het evangelie aan alle schepselen –Marcus 16:15. Het maakt het moeilijk om met de apostel Paulus te zeggen: Want mij is leven Christus, en sterven winst –Filippenzen 1:21. In werkelijkheid maakt het het moeilijk om Christen te zijn.

Toen Jezus zei… Want wie zijn leven zal behouden, die zal het verliezen; en wie zijn leven om Mijn wil zal verliezen, die zal het vinden –Mattheüs 16:25, wat bedoelde Hij dan? Kon het letterlijk betekenen wat er staat: dat wanneer je verliefd wordt op je eigen leven, je Christus niet effectief kunt volgen, zodat je uiteindelijk werkelijk je leven zult verliezen?

Kun je naar de verlorenen gaan en de gemakken van dit leven opgeven als het juist die gemakken zijn die je liefhebt en voor wie je leeft? Dat is onwaarschijnlijk. Wat we hebben zijn “geamerikaande” christenen die alleen het zendingsveld opgaan als ze hun gemakken mee kunnen nemen. Dit produceert rijke, comfortabele zendingswerkers die, ondanks hun beste inspanningen, de verloren zielen niet kunnen winnen, maar hen eerder jaloers maken. Kunnen wij de steden ingaan en het evangelie prediken aan de verlorenen zoals velen voor ons deden? Kunnen wij tijd nemen om de tienduizenden die zoeken te onderwijzen en te discipelen? Als we ons leven liefhebben, zullen we dat waarschijnlijk niet doen, omdat er te veel te verliezen is en het zonde is van goed talent en gelegenheid. God help ons.

Als we leven om het vlees te behagen en we hebben ons leven uitgeplozen, is het moeilijk voor God om ons te gebruiken. We zijn opgeblazen. We zijn geneigd te geloven dat God ons gezegend heeft vanwege al onze bezittingen en onze status in het leven; maar is dat niet het welvaartsevangelie? Wat als dat veranderde? Zouden we ons nog steeds gezegend achten? Is het God of onze eigen doen dat ons vreugde geeft? Wat als we ons in de schoenen van Johannes de Doper zouden bevinden? Of van de apostel Paulus? Als we in de gevangenis zouden zitten zonder iets verkeerds te hebben gedaan, zou onze vreugde blijven? Dat zou moeten als de Heilige Geest leeft en werkt in ons hart. De Bijbel zegt dat we vreugdevol kunnen lijden!

Jaren geleden was een collega van mij een vrolijke kerel. Hij had een prettig leven. Er was één probleem—hij geloofde niet dat er een God was. We praatten dag na dag. Hij vertelde me voortdurend hoe blij hij was en dat men niet christen hoefde te zijn om gelukkig te zijn. Hij sprak over zijn mooie leven, al wat hij bezat, zijn goede baan, zijn fijne gezin. Interessant genoeg leek hij werkelijk gelukkig.

Ik vertelde hem dat ware geluk niet kwam van de dingen die we bezitten of de positie waarin we ons bevinden, maar hij bleef het oneens zijn. Hij beweerde ook dat hij een beter leven leidde dan de meeste christenen die hij kende. Hij zei ook dat hij niet zo snel boos werd als de meeste christenen en dat hij zichzelf kon beheersen. Ik probeerde hem te overtuigen dat hij misleid was. Soms dacht ik dat ik ergens kwam met hem, en later leek het alsof ik ver van hem af stond. Op een dag gaf hij nuchter toe dat ik anders scheen dan de meeste christenen die hij vroeger had gekend, maar dat was nog steeds niet genoeg.

Ik verliet die baan en verloor contact met hem. Onlangs kwam ik een andere vroegere collega tegen. Ik dacht snel aan mijn vriend en vroeg hoe het met hem ging. Hij keek me vreemd aan en schokte me tot in het diepst van mijn zijn toen hij zei: “Hij heeft zelfmoord gepleegd”.

De duivel wil dat wij ons leven liefhebben—het is zo simpel. Wanneer wij ons leven liefhebben, richten we ons erop, koesteren we het. Het laatste wat we willen doen is ons leven verliezen, zelfs als het voor iets eeuwigs is.

Toen ik bij de Mariniers zat, herinnerden ze ons voortdurend eraan dat ons leven niet op de eerste plaats stond; ons land stond op de eerste plaats. Er zijn veel jonge mannen die hun land eerst zetten. Velen zijn gegaan en hebben alles gegeven; velen zijn gestorven.

Tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog probeerden de Japanners soms naar een loopgraaf te sluipen waar soldaten zaten en een granaat naar binnen te gooien. Vaak liep het niet zoals de Japanners wilden, omdat iemand op de granaat sprong en de explosie opving. Duizenden gaven hun leven om hun vrienden te redden en hun land te verdedigen. Maar wees zeker, als hun prioriteiten niet in orde waren geweest (land eerst, zichzelf daarna), zouden ze dat niet hebben gedaan.

Als iemand vandaag, in Amerika, zijn leven voor het evangelie zou riskeren, zou hij als dwaas, roekeloos en onvolwassen worden bestempeld. Maar wat zeggen we over zoveel voorgangers vóór ons—zij die hun leven gaven terwijl ze streden voor dezelfde dingen die wij zeggen te geloven vandaag? En wat te denken van de duizenden vandaag die hun leven op het spel zetten in andere landen—zijn zij dwaas? Laten we naar een heel duidelijk voorbeeld in Handelingen kijken.

En terwijl wij daar vele dagen verbleven, kwam er uit Judea een profeet, met name Agabus. En hij kwam bij ons en nam de gordel van Paulus, en bond zijn eigen handen en voeten, en zei: Zo zegt de Heilige Geest: Zo zullen de Joden te Jeruzalem binden degene die deze gordel bezit, en hem uitleveren aan de heidenen. En als wij dit hoorden, smeekten zowel wij als die ter plaatse hem niet op te gaan naar Jeruzalem. Maar Paulus antwoordde: Wat bedoelt gij dat gij huilt en mijn hart verbreekt? Want ik ben gereed niet alleen gebonden te worden, maar ook te sterven te Jeruzalem om de naam van de Heere Jezus –Handelingen 21:10-13.

Wat zouden wij vandaag van Paulus’ daden denken? Paulus ging naar Jeruzalem en werd spoedig opgepakt, geslagen en in de gevangenis gezet. Het was het begin van het einde voor onze dierbare broeder. Hij werd van gevangenis naar gevangenis gebracht en eindigde uiteindelijk in Rome, waar hij onthoofd werd. Wat denkt u dat de mensen die probeerden hem te overtuigen niet naar Jeruzalem te gaan, dachten? Dachten ze dat ze hem een dwaas noemden? Schudden ze hun hoofden en zeiden: “Ik zei hem toch dat hij niet moest gaan!”?

We kunnen het niet met zekerheid weten. Echter, ik weet zeker dat Paulus eenvoudigweg het Koninkrijk van Christus eerst plaatste; zijn leven deed er niet toe. Hij gehoorzaamde God, en God had hem gezegd te gaan.

Als wij ons leven liefhebben, is het heel moeilijk een effectieve discipel van de Heere Jezus te zijn. We laten Gods roeping varen en blijven dan vastzitten en proberen het christelijke leven alleen te leven, zonder God—geen geestelijke hulp van boven, waardoor we ver achter het doel blijven.

Het is ironisch dat alleen wanneer wij alles achterlaten, inclusief ons leven, wij ware vrede en doel voor ons leven vinden. En wanneer wij ons leven liefhebben, is dat wanneer wij het zullen verliezen.

Sta op, o heiligen van God!
Geef het op voor minder belangrijke dingen.
Geef hart en ziel en verstand en kracht
Om de Koning der koningen te dienen.

Sta op, o heiligen van God!
Het Koninkrijk treuzelt lang.
Breng de dag van Christus‑achtige liefde
En beëindig de nacht van het onrecht.

Hef hoog het kruis van Christus!
Betreed waar Zijn voeten hebben getreden.
Geleid door de Zoon des mensen,
Sta op, o heiligen van God!

Laten wij opstaan, als Gods volk, en ophouden met minder belangrijke dingen, met onze blik op de hemelse dingen, niet op de dingen van deze aarde. Ja, wij zullen opvallen; wij zullen dwazen en vele andere namen worden genoemd. Echter, wij zullen opnieuw Gods aandacht trekken en de vlammen van opwekking zullen opnieuw branden!

Greetings of love in the blessed name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Many Christians have gone through a time of trial and testing during the past several years, yet we trust that each one is able to say with Paul… Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content –Philippians 4:11.

Summer is hard upon us, along with the heat and humidity that goes along with summers here in Ohio. Springtime, along with the normal planting season, was extra long and drawn out. But, by now, most of what is known locally as “the spring work” has been finished. The farmers’ crops and the gardeners’ herbs are pushing through the cool soil and towards the heat and light of the sun.

In this issue you can take a stroll on the road to Emmaus and try to put yourself in the sandals of Jesus’ disciples as they puzzled over the sudden turn of events surrounding Christ’s death, burial, and alleged “resurrection”. You can try to picture yourself with Daniel of old as he chose to keep praying like normal at his open window, while knowing full well that this simple act most likely could change his life forever. You can marvel with little “Ellie” how God met the “desires of her heart” even before she knew things weren’t working out according to plan.

Something new in this issue is the beginning of a series by Brother Donald Brechbill on “discipleship”. Disciple has almost the same spelling as discipline. For many, discipline carries a negative connotation, which hopefully will not interfere with the reader being drawn to what Brother Donald has to share. Let’s remember that Jesus gave personal example of the discipleship model—He chose and called “disciples” to follow and learn from Him. Later He sent them out two by two to teach and make more disciples. And then when He gave the “Great Commission” it was to His disciples at that time, and to all future disciples—the Church of Jesus Christ. We trust that each one can be inspired by this series.

Coming up in future issues, we are planning to have a “Song of the Quarter” and a section on various aspects of “Church History”. You can pray for us as we continue to move forward with our ministry and our magazine.

Just a friendly reminder… We encourage feedback from our readers. If you have been especially blessed by a certain article, feedback is helpful for us as a board, and it is encouraging for our writers. Also, if there is something specific that someone wishes to see included in future magazine issues, we welcome the input. This helps provide ideas for us as a board when choosing articles and when asking authors to write.

In the spring of 2022, we made some changes with our ministry in our endeavors to keep the work of The Berean Voice moving forward into the future. Personnel changes:

Brother Andrew (our designer) has become increasingly busy as a young father with a growing family and as a deacon for our local church congregation. In looking at this challenge, the board decided to support Andrew’s desire to find someone to help him (for now) with the bulk of the design work for each issue of our magazine—The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Thus, there may be some slight changes in the “style” of design in upcoming issues.

In the spring of 2022, there was a decision to seek several new board members to replace several others who had quit over the last number of years due to personal responsibilities. After praying for the Lord’s wisdom and direction, and after consultation with the leadership of our church, Brother Joe Mast and Brother Sheldon Bower were chosen to fill the empty slots on the board. These brothers have both graciously accepted this calling and are already allowing God to use their spiritual gifts to make a difference

Brother Joe Tindall has been a board member for The Berean Voice since our beginning in June of 2016. Due to his age (83) Brother Joe asked to be relieved of his duties as a board member. At our monthly board meeting in May of 2022, the board honored Brother Joe’s request. We will miss the stability of his quiet wisdom in our board meetings and during our article selection process. Please join us in prayer for Brother Joe and his family as he and his wife face the end of their lives and all that goes along with that season of life—that they might remain faithful and courageous.

May God bless and keep each one.

Curvin L Wenger

ברכות של אהבה בשם המבורך של אדוננו ומושיענו, ישוע המשיח. מאמינים רבים עברו זמן של נסיון ומבחן בשנים האחרונות, אך אנו בוטחים כי כל אחד יכול לומר ביחד עם פאולוס… אֵינִי מְדַבֵּר מִפְּנֵי חֲסַר; כִּי לָמַדְתִּי, בְּכָל מַעֲמַד שֶׁאֲנִי בוֹ, לָשֵׂבַע. — איגרת אל הפיליפים 4:11.

הקיץ כבר עלינו לטובה, יחד עם החום והלחות שאופייניים לקייצים כאן באוהיו. האביב, יחד עם עונת השתילה הרגילה, היה ארוך וממושך. אך כעת, רוב מה שמכונה מקומית "עבודת האביב" הושלם. יבולי החקלאים ועשבי הגננים דוחפים מבעד לאדמה הקרירה אל החום ואור השמש.

בגיליון זה תוכלו לטייל בדרך לעמאוס ולנסות להעמיד את עצמכם בסנדליהם של תלמידי ישוע כשהם תוהים בפני המהפך הפתאומי שהיה סביב מותו של המשיח, קבורתו ו"תחייתו" המוצהרת. תוכלו לדמיין את עצמכם לצד דניאל הקדום כאשר בחר להמשיך ולהתפלל כהרגלו בחלון הפתוח, כאשר ידע היטב שמעשה פשוט זה עלול לשנות את חייו לנצח. תוכלו להתפעל יחד עם הקטנה "אלי" כיצד אלוהים ענה על "רצון לבה" אפילו לפני שהיא ידעה שהדברים לא הסתדרו כמתוכנן.

משהו חדש בגיליון זה הוא תחילתה של סדרה מאת האח דונלד ברכביל על "תלמידות". המילה "תלמיד" כמעט זהה באיותה למילה "משמעת". עבור רבים, מושג המשמעת נושא קונוטציה שלילית, ובתקווה הדבר לא יפריע לקורא להתקרב למה שיש לאח דונלד לחלוק. נזכור שישוע נתן דוגמה אישית למודל התלמידות—הוא בחר וקרא ל"תלמידים" ללכת אחריו וללמוד ממנו. לאחר מכן שלח אותם בזוגות ללמד ולעשות תלמידים נוספים. וכשהעניק את "המשלוח הגדול" זה היה לתלמידיו באותו זמן, ולכל התלמידים העתידיים—לכנסיית ישוע המשיח. אנו מקווים שכל אחד מהם יוכל להיחשף להשראה מסדרה זו.

בגיליונות עתידיים אנו מתכננים לכלול "שיר הרבע" וקטע על היבטים שונים של "תולדות הכנסייה". תוכלו להתפלל בעדינו כאשר אנו ממשיכים לקדם את שירותנו ואת המגזין.

רק תזכורת ידידותית… אנו מעודדים משוב מהקוראים שלנו. אם התברכתם באופן מיוחד על ידי מאמר מסוים, משוב כזה מועיל לנו כחברי הוועד, והוא מעודד את כותבינו. אם יש משהו מסוים שמישהו מבקש לראות בגיליונות עתידיים של המגזין, נשמח לקבל את ההצעות. זה מסייע לנו כחברי הוועד בבחירת מאמרים ובהזמת כותבים לבקשת כתיבה.

באביב 2022 ביצענו כמה שינויים בשירותנו במאמצים לשמור על המשך פעולתו של קול הביריאני לעתיד. שינויים בכוח האדם:

האח אנדרו (המעצב שלנו) הפך להיות עסוק יותר ויותר כאב צעיר עם משפחה גדלה וכדיאקון בכנסייתנו המקומית. בהתמודדות עם אתגר זה החליט הוועד לתמוך ברצונו של אנדרו למצוא מישהו שיעזור לו (לעת עתה) ברוב עבודת העיצוב של כל גיליון של המגזין שלנו—דופק השארית. לכן ייתכנו שינויים קלים ב"סגנון" העיצוב בגיליונות הקרובים.

באביב 2022 הוחלט לבקש כמה חברי ועד חדשים כדי להחליף מספר אחרים שהתפטרו במהלך השנים האחרונות בשל אחריות אישית. לאחר תפילה על חכמת ה' והנחיה, ולאחר התייעצות עם הנהגת כנסייתנו, נבחרו האח ג'ו מאסט והאח שלדון באואר למלא את המקומות הפנויים בוועד. האחים הללו קיבלו בחסד את הקריאה הזו וכבר מאפשרים לקב"ה להשתמש במתנות הרוחניות שלהם כדי להביא שינוי.

האח ג'ו טינדל היה חבר ועד של קול הביריאני מאז תחילתנו ביוני 2016. בגלל גילו (83) ביקש האח ג'ו להשתחרר מתפקידיו כחבר ועד. בפגישת הוועד החודשית שלנו במאי 2022, הוועד כיבד את בקשתו של האח ג'ו. יחסר לנו היציבות של חוכמתו השקטה בפגישות הוועד שלנו ובמהלך תהליך בחירת המאמרים. הצטרפו אלינו בתפילה בעד האח ג'ו ובני משפחתו בשעה שהוא ואשתו מתמודדים עם סיום חייהם וכל מה שכרוך בעונה זו של החיים—שיישארו נאמנים ואמיצים.

שיהיה ה' מבורך וישמור את כל אחד ואחת מכם.

קורבין ל. ונגר

Around the world, but particularly in the United States, people seem to value rugged individualism. People who demonstrate this character quality make their own way through life, asking nothing from others and expecting nothing.

I suppose that this idea relates back to the pioneers. These were men and women who trekked across the various new countries looking for a place where they could settle down and call home. There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.

While this may sound like a scenario that demonstrates strength, the truth is somewhat different these days. These days people use technology to deliberately create bubbles of isolation around themselves.

Many older people have found themselves increasingly isolated from friends and family. COVID certainly made this worse, but there were seeds of this seclusion that had been sowed long before COVID was ever heard of.

Isolation is Not a Natural State

Looking back to the Garden of Eden we can see that Adam was created before Eve. While there were lots of animals around, there was no true companionship for Adam. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him … And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him –Genesis 2:18-20.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man –Genesis 2:21-22. Of course, this was the beginning of marriage, but the more important thing to see here is that it is not a normal state for humans to be alone. We desire companionship and not just the companionship of a pet dog or cat.

Isolation can lead to Despair

Perhaps there is no story that demonstrates so clearly the dangers of isolation as the story of Elijah. We know from the biblical book of I Kings, that Elijah was a fiery prophet of God.

He brought word from God to Ahab that there would be no rain and there was terrible drought for the next three and a half years. During that time, Elijah spent time in the wilderness and then with a widow in Zarephath.

The whole time, he was miraculously fed through God’s power, first by ravens and then through God’s provision of flour and oil to a widow, with whom he lived. Through God’s power, he raised the widow’s son to life.

Then came a time when he challenged the prophets of Baal to a match on Mt. Carmel and won a decisive victory for God. Miraculous fire descended from heaven in answer to his prayer. Truly, God was working great things in his life.

Very soon though, Elijah was running for his life into the desert. Jezebel had threatened his life and rather than trusting God, he fled to Mt. Horeb where he heard the voice of God.

When God asked him what he was doing there, Elijah replied, …I have been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away –1 Kings 19:10.

We can see here a big reason for Elijah’s weakness. He felt completely alone. God corrected Elijah’s incorrect assumption when He stated: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him –1 Kings 19:18.

The fact that those men and women existed in Israel did Elijah little good since he didn’t spend time with them. Elijah’s isolation led him to weakness and despair.

The story of Paul comes to mind as well. The Apostle Paul was a man who seemed to have nearly limitless amounts of energy and an unquenchable zeal for the things of God, but his last letter to Timothy from prison revealed a man who felt very alone. Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee… –2 Timothy 4:9-11.

The Apostle was not abandoned. Other than Demas, they had not fled because they were afraid or ashamed of his bonds. He had sent many of his friends away to strengthen the church in various parts of the Roman Empire. Yet, Paul was still feeling isolated and needed the good Christian brothers, Timothy and Mark, to come and encourage him as he faced a martyr’s death.

Isolation is Physically Harmful

Studies have showed that isolation is linked to higher rates of high blood pressure, heart disease, anxiety, and depression. Older people who are isolated often show signs of mental decline and can experience worsening dementia.

Many times, as people age, they experience the deaths of loved ones. The loss of a spouse can lead older people to withdraw from others and to experience loneliness and isolation. This in turn often leads to rapid progression of the aging process.

Science does not fully understand it, but loneliness leads to increased inflammation and poorer immune function. This in turn can lead to lonely people getting worse infections and struggling to recover after such an infection.

While we think of these problems as those that primarily affect elderly people, they can affect younger people as well. In younger people, often loneliness doesn’t lead to memory issues, but it certainly can lead to things like depression, and it can make chronic inflammatory diseases much worse.

The Opposite of Isolation

If asked what the opposite of isolation is most people would probably answer “Companionship” or maybe even “Friendship”. There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.

The Greek word translated fellowship in the New Testament is “Koinonia” and in the Bible it speaks of relationships that are founded on a shared love for God and for the church—a unity of belief and desire. Christian fellowship includes concepts like praying together, encouraging one another, and even suffering together.

I am afraid that many today find themselves in one of two dangerous situations. First, they may not be a member of any church congregation. While this may be unavoidable in certain mission outreach situations, it is not ideal, and most certainly it should not be a normal situation. At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed. We need fellowship, both to encourage us and to keep us accountable.

The second dangerous situation is that many believers, while members of a church, isolate themselves within that church. If you are a member of a large church congregation, it is easy to blend in and not develop relationships with others. This is just as harmful as not being a member of a church body. Too many people feel lonely, even when there are lots of people around.

Scripture makes it clear that we need a church body. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching –Hebrews 10:25.

There are many people who have lives that are full of friends and acquaintances, but if they do not have a place where they receive fellowship, they are missing out.

When I see people in my office who are struggling with depression there are two things I always tell them to do for themselves.

First is to start exercising. There have been several studies that compared exercise to antidepressants and found that it had similar effectiveness to many of the commonly prescribed antidepressant medications. This doesn’t have to be really vigorous exercise, but it does need to be aerobic (enough to raise the heart rate) and consistent.

The second is to become active in a church congregation; it is not enough to just attend church. Having brothers and sisters to pray for someone who is struggling, to listen to the discouraging situations, and to encourage that person to a more vibrant walk with God is really helpful.

Unfortunately, when someone is struggling with depression, the last thing they seem to want to do is make the effort to be around other people, which contrary to their feelings, is counterproductive to changing the problem.

As we consider this, it should move us to reach out to those who we know are struggling with isolation.

When someone loses a spouse, they often have a lot of encouragement for the first several weeks, but we need to make certain that they continue to have an active presence in their lives in the months that follow.

For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:5, should not give us excuse to not obey God’s command to Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2. The family of God is given no time limit on bearing burdens. There is only a mandate that as we see our brother or sister struggling, we are to help them, as we are able.

The blessing is that someday, when we are struggling, we will have men and women of faith around us to encourage us and to pray for us. We cannot carry these burdens alone. Together, we will reach the Celestial City.

Isolation comes for many reasons. Sometimes it seems to be a chosen way of life, as is the natural tendency of introverted people. Sometimes it is foisted upon a person due to deaths of loved ones or other significant losses. Either way, it is not a healthy place to live.

As we find ourselves in these situations, we need to reach out for fellowship. The family of God is there for us if we only reach out.

As we see others who are struggling, we need to extend to them the right arm of fellowship. As we do so, we may, through our small efforts, help someone emotionally, physically, and spiritually, simply by being a friend in a time of isolation.

전 세계적으로, 그러나 특히 미국에서는 거친 개인주의를 중시하는 경향이 있는 것 같습니다. 이런 성품을 보이는 사람들은 남에게 아무것도 요구하지도 기대하지도 않고 스스로 삶을 개척합니다.

이 생각은 개척자들에서 유래한 것일지도 모릅니다. 이들은 정착할 수 있는 땅을 찾아 여러 신생 국토를 가로질러 여행한 남녀들이었습니다. 일반 상점도 드물었고 가능한 한 자급자족하며 살았습니다.

이러한 상황이 강인함을 보여주는 것처럼 들리지만, 오늘날의 현실은 다소 다릅니다. 요즘 사람들은 기술을 이용해 의도적으로 자신을 둘러싼 고립의 거품을 만들어냅니다.

많은 노인들이 점점 더 친구와 가족으로부터 격리되어 있음을 발견합니다. COVID가 이를 악화시켰음은 분명하지만, COVID가 알려지기 훨씬 이전부터 이러한 고립의 씨앗이 뿌려져 있었습니다.

고립은 자연스러운 상태가 아니다

에덴 동산을 돌아보면 아담이 이브보다 먼저 창조되었음을 알 수 있습니다. 많은 동물들이 있었지만 아담에게 진정한 동반자는 없었습니다. 여호와 하나님이 이르시되 사람이 혼자 사는 것이 좋지 아니하니 내가 그를 위하여 돕는 배필을 지으리라 … 아담이 모든 가축과 공중의 모든 새와 들의 모든 짐승에게 이름을 주었으나 아담을 위하여 돕는 배필이 없었더라 –창세기 2:18-20.

여호와 하나님이 아담에게 깊은 잠을 내리시니 그가 잠들매 그가 그의 갈비 하나를 취하시고 그 자리를 살로 메우시고; 여호와 하나님이 취하신 그 갈비로 여자를 지으사 그를 아담에게 이끌어 오셨더라 –창세기 2:21-22. 물론 이것은 결혼의 시작이지만, 여기서 더 중요한 것은 인간이 혼자인 상태가 정상적이지 않다는 점입니다. 우리는 반려견이나 반려묘 같은 동물의 동반이 아닌, 진정한 교제를 갈망합니다.

고립은 절망으로 이어질 수 있다

아마 고립의 위험을 가장 분명히 보여주는 이야기는 엘리야의 이야기일 것입니다. 열왕기상에서 우리는 엘리야가 하나님의 불같은 선지자였음을 압니다.

그는 하나님으로부터 비가 오지 않을 것이라는 말을 아합에게 전했고 그로 인해 다음 삼년 반 동안 심한 가뭄이 있었습니다. 그 기간 동안 엘리야는 광야에 있다가 사렙다의 한 과부와 함께 시간을 보냈습니다.

그동안 그는 처음에는 까마귀를 통해, 그다음에는 그가 함께 살던 과부에게 기름과 밀가루를 공급하심으로써 하나님의 능력으로 기적적으로 먹음을 입었습니다. 하나님의 능력으로 그는 과부의 아들을 다시 살렸습니다.

그러다가 그가 갈멜산에서 바알의 선지자들과 대결하여 하나님을 위하여 결정적인 승리를 거둘 때가 왔습니다. 그의 기도에 응답하여 하늘에서 기적의 불이 내렸습니다. 참으로 하나님은 그의 삶 가운데 큰 일을 행하고 계셨습니다.

그러나 곧 엘리야는 생명을 피하여 광야로 도망쳤습니다. 이세벨이 그의 목숨을 노렸고, 그는 하나님을 신뢰하기보다 호렙산으로 달아나 거기서 하나님의 음성을 들었습니다.

하나님이 그에게 거기서 무엇을 하느냐고 물으시자 엘리야는 대답했습니다. …나는 열왕의 군사 여호와인 주의 열심으로 매우 성내었나이다 이스라엘 자손이 주의 언약을 버리고 주의 제단을 무너뜨리며 주의 선지자들을 칼로 죽였고 나만 남아 주의 눈에 보기에도 나 하나뿐이고 그들이 내 생명을 구하여 빼앗으려 하나이다 –열왕기상 19:10.

여기서 우리는 엘리야의 약함의 큰 원인을 볼 수 있습니다. 그는 완전히 혼자라고 느꼈습니다. 하나님은 엘리야의 잘못된 가정을 정정하시며 말씀하셨습니다. 그러나 내가 이스라엘 중에 칠천명을 남겼으니 곧 바알에게 무릎을 꿇지 아니한 자와 바알에게 입술을 대지 아니한 자라 –열왕기상 19:18.

이스라엘에 그런 남녀들이 존재했다는 사실은 엘리야에게 거의 도움이 되지 않았습니다. 그는 그들과 시간을 보내지 않았기 때문입니다. 엘리야의 고립은 그를 약하고 절망에 빠지게 했습니다.

바울의 이야기도 떠오릅니다. 사도 바울은 거의 무한한 에너지와 하나님의 일에 대한 식을 줄 모르는 열정을 가진 사람처럼 보였지만, 감옥에서 보낸 그의 마지막 편지인 디모데후서에는 매우 외로움을 느꼈던 사람이 드러납니다. 네가 속히 내게로 오라 힘쓰라 데마는 이 세상을 사랑하여 나를 버리고 데살로니가로 갔고 가이오는 갈라디아로 갔으며 디도는 달마티아로 갔고 오직 루가만 나와 함께 있도다 마가를 데리고 오라 네게 유익하리라… –디모데후서 4:9-11.

사도는 버림받은 것이 아니었습니다. 데마 외에는 도망하거나 그의 결박을 부끄러워해서 떠난 것이 아니었습니다. 그는 로마 제국의 여러 지역에 있는 교회를 굳게 세우기 위해 많은 친구들을 보냈습니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 바울은 여전히 고립감을 느꼈고, 순교를 앞둔 그가 힘을 얻도록 디모데와 마가 같은 좋은 신자 형제들이 와서 격려해주기를 필요로 했습니다.

고립은 신체적으로 해롭다

연구들은 고립이 고혈압, 심장병, 불안 및 우울증의 높은 비율과 연관되어 있음을 보여주었습니다. 고립된 노인들은 종종 정신적 쇠퇴의 징후를 보이며 치매가 악화될 수 있습니다.

많은 경우 사람들은 나이가 들면서 사랑하는 이를 잃습니다. 배우자의 상실은 노인들이 다른 사람들로부터 물러나 외로움과 고립을 경험하게 할 수 있습니다. 이는 종종 노화 과정이 급속히 진행되는 결과를 낳습니다.

과학은 이를 완전히 이해하지 못하지만, 외로움은 염증 증가와 면역 기능 저하로 이어집니다. 이는 외로운 사람들이 더 심한 감염에 걸리고 그런 감염 후 회복에 어려움을 겪게 할 수 있습니다.

우리는 이러한 문제들이 주로 노인에게 영향을 미친다고 생각하지만, 젊은이들에게도 영향을 줄 수 있습니다. 젊은 사람들에서는 종종 외로움이 기억력 문제로 이어지지는 않지만, 분명히 우울증과 같은 것들로 이어질 수 있고 만성 염증성 질환을 훨씬 악화시킬 수 있습니다.

고립의 반대

고립의 반대가 무엇이냐고 묻는다면 대부분의 사람들은 아마 “동반자 관계” 또는 “우정”이라고 답할 것입니다. 기독교적 함의를 지닌 다른 단어가 있는데 그것이 더 적절합니다. 그 단어는 교제입니다.

신약에서 교제로 번역된 그리스어 단어는 ‘코이노니아(koinonia)’이며, 성경에서는 하나님과 교회를 향한 공동의 사랑—신앙과 소망의 일치에 기초한 관계들을 말합니다. 그리스도인의 교제에는 함께 기도하기, 서로 격려하기, 심지어 함께 고난을 겪는 것과 같은 개념들이 포함됩니다.

오늘날 많은 이들이 두 가지 위험한 상황 중 하나에 놓여 있다고 걱정됩니다. 첫째, 어떤 이들은 어떤 교회 공동체의 구성원이 아닐 수 있습니다. 선교적 상황에서는 불가피할 수 있지만, 이는 이상적이지 않으며 결코 정상적인 상황이 되어서는 안 됩니다. 적어도 이는 고립감을 만들 수 있고, 최악의 경우 성경의 ‘서로 하라’는 많은 구절들을 따르는 데 장애가 됩니다. 우리는 격려받고 책임지워지기 위해 교제가 필요합니다.

둘째 위험한 상황은 많은 신자들이 교회의 구성원임에도 불구하고 그 교회 안에서 스스로 고립되는 것입니다. 큰 교회 공동체의 일원이라면 쉽게 섞여들어 다른 사람들과 관계를 발전시키지 않을 수 있습니다. 이것은 교회 구성원이 아닌 것만큼 해롭습니다. 주변에 사람이 많은데도 외로움을 느끼는 사람이 너무 많습니다.

성경은 우리가 교회 공동체가 필요함을 분명히 합니다. 모이기를 폐하는 어떤 사람들의 습관과 같이 하지 말고 오직 권면하고 서로 격려하되 이 날이 가까운 것을 보고 더욱 그리하자 –히브리서 10:25.

친구와 지인으로 가득한 삶을 사는 이들이 많이 있지만, 만약 그들이 교제를 받는 장소가 없다면 그들은 많은 것을 놓치고 있는 것입니다.

우울증으로 고통받는 사람들을 진료실에서 볼 때 나는 그들에게 항상 두 가지를 스스로 하라고 권합니다.

첫째는 운동을 시작하는 것입니다. 여러 연구가 운동을 항우울제와 비교하여 운동이 일반적으로 처방되는 많은 항우울제들과 유사한 효과를 보였다고 밝혔습니다. 이는 굳이 격렬한 운동일 필요는 없지만 심박수를 올릴 정도의 유산소 운동이어야 하고 꾸준히 해야 합니다.

둘째는 교회 공동체에 적극적으로 참여하는 것입니다; 단순히 예배에 참석하는 것만으로는 충분하지 않습니다. 고난당하는 사람을 위해 기도해주고 낙담한 상황을 들어주며 그 사람이 하나님과 더 활기찬 동행을 하도록 격려해 줄 형제자매들이 있는 것은 정말로 도움이 됩니다.

안타깝게도 누군가 우울증으로 고통받을 때 그들이 가장 하기 싫어하는 일은 다른 사람들 주변에 있으려 노력하는 것입니다. 그러나 그들의 감정과 달리 그것은 문제를 바꾸는 데 비생산적이지 않고 오히려 도움이 됩니다.

이 점을 고려할 때 우리는 고립으로 고통받고 있는 이들에게 손을 내밀어야 합니다.

누군가 배우자를 잃으면 처음 몇 주 동안은 많은 격려를 받는 경우가 많지만, 우리는 그들이 이후 몇 달 동안도 삶에서 계속 활발한 존재감을 유지하도록 확실히 해야 합니다.

각각 자기의 짐을 질 것이라 –갈라디아서 6:5,은 우리가 서로의 짐을 지라 이로써 그리스도의 법을 성취하라 –갈라디아서 6:2.는 하나님의 명령을 순종하지 않는 변명이 되어서는 안 됩니다. 하나님의 가족은 짐을 지는 데 시간 제한이 없습니다. 우리가 형제자매가 힘들어하는 것을 보거든 능력이 닿는 대로 도와야 할 명령만 있을 뿐입니다.

그 축복은 언젠가 우리가 힘들 때, 우리를 격려하고 위해 기도해줄 믿음의 남녀들이 우리 곁에 있을 것이라는 점입니다. 우리는 이 짐들을 혼자 지고 갈 수 없습니다. 함께라면 우리는 천국의 도성에 이를 것입니다.

고립은 여러 이유로 찾아옵니다. 때로는 내향적인 사람들의 자연스러운 성향처럼 선택된 생활 방식인 것처럼 보입니다. 때로는 사랑하는 이의 죽음이나 다른 중대한 상실로 인해 누군가에게 강요되기도 합니다. 어느 쪽이든 그것은 건강하게 살 수 있는 장소가 아닙니다.

우리가 이런 상황에 처했을 때, 우리는 교제를 위해 손을 내밀어야 합니다. 하나님의 가족은 우리가 손만 내밀면 거기 있습니다.

고군분투하는 다른 이들을 볼 때 우리는 그들에게 교제의 오른팔을 내밀어야 합니다. 그렇게 함으로써 우리의 작은 노력이 고립의 때에 누군가에게 단지 친구가 되어 줌으로써 정서적·신체적·영적 도움을 줄 수 있습니다.

Ellie edged her chair closer to the grown-ups who were visiting in the kitchen. Grandpa, Grandma, and Aunt Lily had stopped by for a visit, and although she didn’t always understand the conversation, she loved to listen. She found that she learned a lot of things that way.

The topic this evening was about something related to church and that got her mind to thinking about singing during Sunday morning worship services. Although Ellie was only five years old, she very much loved to sing. She thought about the fact that her dear Grandpa was a song leader in their church and how much she liked when he led a song.

At Ellie’s church the song leaders all sat around a table near the center of the church. They took turns choosing a song and then leading it for the congregation. Ellie didn’t always know the songs that were chosen. They sang out of a little black hymnbook that had lots of songs with hard words and tunes she didn’t recognize. However, in the back of this little songbook was a section called “The Appendix” and here were hymns that were familiar to her and she was always pleased when a song was announced from that part of the book. Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight. When that particular song number was announced on a Sunday morning, she always felt a twinge of excitement. She would be able to help along with this song!

I wish we would sing that song again, thought Ellie. It’s been a long time since we have.

Then a sudden thought struck her. Why couldn’t she ask Grandpa to choose that song next Sunday?

Yes, I will ask him and see what he says about that idea, she smiled to herself. She decided to wait until her grandparents were ready to leave. She followed Grandpa out the door and as he walked across the porch, she quickly stepped up next to him. “Grandpa,” she asked. “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!” She felt suddenly shy at having asked such a question, and she ducked back toward the doorway of the house.

Grandpa smiled down at her. “I think I can do that. Is that a song you like?” His eyes twinkled at Ellie. “I’ll be happy to lead that one just for you.”

Ellie could scarcely wait for church the following Sunday. She would get to sing “her” song. Grandpa said he would choose it and she had no doubt he would do as he said.

Sunday morning, she waited eagerly for the song service to begin. The first and second songs were ones that were not familiar to her. Then came time for the third one. “Let’s sing number 8 in the Appendix,” announced the song leader. Ellie’s heart sang. They were going to sing her favorite song. Her grandpa had honored her request. Her eyes shone as she joined in the singing of the beautiful song. It was a lovely hymn that spoke of Jesus’ care as a Shepherd and a Friend, and how He would always keep His children close to Himself.

Later, after church was over and they were on their way home, Ellie remarked to her mother, “Grandpa chose that one song, just like I asked him to!”

Ellie’s mom looked a bit startled. “You asked him to lead a song today? When did you ask him?”

“Yes, I did. The other evening when they visited, I asked him if he could lead it today and he said he would. And he did!” Ellie said with delight.

Mom had a strange look on her face, and she was quiet for a moment.

“Did you know that Grandpas weren’t there today? At the last minute they decided to visit elsewhere this morning for church.” Mom smiled tenderly at her little daughter. “It seems that God knew what a little girl’s heart was desiring and He led another brother to choose the song you like so much. That’s so amazing, isn’t it?” Ellie nodded. To think that Grandpa wasn’t even at church today, and still they sang her favorite song anyway! It gave her such a special feeling to know that Jesus cared for her that much.

Today, Ellie is a grown-up woman and now has children of her own. Whenever she thinks about how Jesus cares for all His children, she especially remembers how God cared about one little, five-year-old girl and the song she loved so much. As her mother said, and still does, “Of course God cares. He loves all the little children of the world!”

Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us

Savior, like a Shepherd lead us,
Much we need Thy tender care.
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
For our use Thy folds prepare:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

We are Thine, do Thou befriend us,
Be the guardian of our way.
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
Seek us when we go astray:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

Thou hast promised to receive us,
Poor and sinful though we be.
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
Grace to cleanse, and pow’r to free:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Early let us turn to Thee.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Early let us turn to Thee.

Early let us seek Thy favor,
Early let us do Thy will.
Blessed Lord and only Savior,
With Thy love our bosoms fill:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

Dorothy Ann Thrupp

엘리는 부엌에서 방문객들과 함께 앉아 있는 어른들 쪽으로 의자를 조금 더 옮겼다. 할아버지, 할머니, 그리고 릴리 이모가 들르셨고, 그녀는 대화 내용을 항상 다 이해하지는 못했지만 듣는 것을 좋아했다. 그렇게 하면서 많은 것을 배운다는 것을 알게 되었다.

그날 저녁 화제는 교회와 관련된 어떤 일이었고, 그로 인해 그녀는 주일 예배 때의 찬양에 대해 생각하기 시작했다. 엘리는 겨우 다섯 살이었지만 노래하는 것을 매우 좋아했다. 그녀는 사랑하는 할아버지가 교회에서 찬양 인도자라는 사실과 할아버지가 찬양을 인도할 때 얼마나 좋아하는지를 떠올렸다.

엘리의 교회에서는 찬양 인도자들이 교회 중앙 근처의 탁자에 둘러앉아 있었다. 그들은 돌아가며 곡을 골라 회중을 위해 인도했다. 엘리는 늘 선택된 곡들을 다 알지는 못했다. 그들은 생소한 가사와 멜로디가 많은 작은 검은 찬송가에서 불렀다. 그러나 이 작은 찬송가의 뒤쪽에는 ‘부록’이라는 부분이 있었고, 거기에는 그녀가 익숙한 찬송들이 있어 그 책의 그 부분에서 곡이 발표되면 항상 기뻤다. 그녀가 가장 좋아하는 찬송은 ‘구주여, 목자처럼 우리를 인도하소서’였고, 그녀는 아직 글을 읽지 못했음에도 그것이 8번이라는 것을 알고 있었다. 주일 아침에 그 특정 번호가 발표되면 그녀는 항상 설렘을 느꼈다. 이번엔 이 노래를 도울 수 있을 거야!

그 노래를 다시 불렀으면 좋겠어, 엘리는 생각했다. 오랜만이야.

그러다 문득 한 생각이 떠올랐다. 다음 주에 할아버지께 그 노래를 골라 달라고 요청하면 어떨까?

그래, 꼭 물어볼 거야. 그분이 뭐라고 하실지 보자,라고 그녀는 혼자 미소 지었다. 그녀는 조부모님이 떠날 준비가 될 때까지 기다리기로 했다. 할아버지가 마당을 건너 나가실 때 그녀는 재빨리 그의 옆으로 다가갔다. “할아버지,” 그녀가 물었다. “다음 주일에 ‘구주여, 목자처럼 우리를 인도하소서’라는 찬송을 인도해 주실 수 있어요? 다시 부르고 싶어요!” 그런 질문을 한 자신이 갑자기 수줍어져 집의 문간 쪽으로 몸을 웅크렸다.

할아버지는 그녀를 내려다보며 미소지었다. “그럴 수 있을 것 같구나. 그 노래를 좋아하니?” 그의 눈이 엘리에게 반짝였다. “그 노래는 기꺼이 네 것을 위해 인도해 주겠구나.”

엘리는 다음 주일을 거의 기다릴 수 없었다. 그녀는 ‘자기’ 노래를 부를 수 있었다. 할아버지가 그 노래를 골라 주겠다고 하셨고, 그녀는 그가 말한 대로 해 주실 것을 의심하지 않았다.

주일 아침, 그녀는 찬송 시간이 시작되기를 간절히 기다렸다. 첫 번째와 두 번째 곡은 그녀에게 익숙하지 않은 곡들이었다. 그리고 세 번째 곡 시간이 되었다. “부록의 8번을 부르겠습니다.” 찬양 인도자가 알렸다. 엘리의 마음은 노래했다. 그들은 그녀가 가장 좋아하는 노래를 부를 것이었다. 할아버지는 그녀의 부탁을 들어 주셨다. 그녀는 아름다운 노래를 함께 부르며 눈을 반짝였다. 그 찬송은 예수님의 목자이자 친구로서의 돌보심과 그분이 항상 자녀들을 가까이 지키시리라는 내용을 말해 주는 사랑스러운 곡이었다.

나중에 예배가 끝나고 집으로 돌아오는 길에 엘리는 엄마에게 말했다. “할아버지가 제가 부탁한 대로 그 노래를 골라 주셨어요!”

엘리의 엄마는 다소 놀란 표정이었다. “오늘 할아버지께 그 노래 인도를 부탁했었니? 언제 물어봤니?”

“네, 그랬어요. 그들이 방문하던 그 날 저녁에 오늘 인도해 주실 수 있느냐고 물어봤더니 그러시겠대요. 그리고 정말 하셨어요!” 엘리는 기쁘게 말했다.

엄마의 얼굴에는 이상한 표정이 스쳐 갔고, 잠시 조용해졌다.

“오늘은 할아버지네가 교회에 안 오셨다는 거 알고 있었니? 막판에 교회에 다른 곳을 방문하기로 하셨거든.” 엄마는 딸에게 다정하게 미소 지었다. “하나님께서 한 어린 소녀의 마음이 원하는 것을 아시고, 다른 형제를 인도하여 네가 그렇게 좋아하는 노래를 골라 불러 주셨던 것 같구나. 참 놀랍지 않니?” 엘리는 고개를 끄덕였다. 오늘 할아버지가 교회에 안 계셨는데도 그들이 여전히 그녀가 가장 좋아하는 노래를 불렀다는 사실을 생각하니! 예수님께서 자신을 그만큼이나 돌보신다는 것을 아는 것이 그녀에게 특별한 느낌을 주었다.

오늘날 엘리는 어른이 되어 자신도 자녀가 있다. 예수님께서 모든 자녀들을 어떻게 돌보시는지 생각할 때마다 그녀는 특히 다섯 살짜리 한 어린 소녀와 그녀가 그렇게 사랑하던 노래를 하나님께서 어떻게 보살펴 주셨는지를 기억한다. 그녀의 어머니가 말씀하셨듯, 그리고 지금도 말씀하시듯, “물론 하나님께서는 돌보신다. 그는 세상의 모든 어린이들을 사랑하신단다!”

구주여, 목자처럼 우리를 인도하소서

구주여, 목자처럼 우리를 인도하소서,
우리는 주의 다정한 보살핌이 매우 필요하나이다.
주의 즐거운 목초지에서 우리를 먹이시고,
우리의 유익을 위해 주의 양우리들을 준비하소서:
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
주께서 우리를 사셨으니, 우리는 주의 것입니다.
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
주께서 우리를 사셨으니, 우리는 주의 것입니다.

우리는 주의 것이니 주께서 친구가 되어 주소서,
우리의 길의 지키는 자가 되소서.
우리 양 떼를 지키사, 죄에서 보호하소서,
우리가 길을 잃을 때 찾아 주소서:
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
우리가 기도할 때 들으시고 응답하소서.
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
우리가 기도할 때 들으시고 응답하소서.

주께서 우리를 영접하시겠다고 약속하셨나이다,
비록 우리가 가난하고 죄인일지라도.
주께서는 우리를 도우실 자비가 있으시며,
깨끗케 하실 은혜와 자유케 하실 능력이 있으시니:
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
이른 시일에 우리가 주께 돌아가게 하소서.
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
이른 시일에 우리가 주께 돌아가게 하소서.

이른 시일에 주의 은총을 구하게 하소서,
이른 시일에 주의 뜻을 행하게 하소서.
복되신 주님, 오직 구주이신 예수님,
주의 사랑으로 우리의 마음을 채우소서:
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
주께서 우리를 사랑하셨사오니, 계속 사랑하소서.
복되신 예수님! 복되신 예수님!
주께서 우리를 사랑하셨사오니, 계속 사랑하소서.

Dorothy Ann Thrupp

There is coming a day when all will be well.
The things that are bad will all be in hell.
But we must not forget that day has not come.
We are in a battle; we must still overcome.
The enemy rages, his time here is short.
He spreads all his lies, the truth to distort.

It need not be big; a small sin will do.
He’ll trick and deceive, each soul to pursue.
The darts of the wicked come from all sides.
When faced with God’s power, that devil—he hides!
When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

Настанет день, когда всё будет хорошо.
Плохое уйдёт — и в ад пойдёт прочь.
Но не забудем: этот день ещё не пришёл.
Мы в сражении; нам всё ещё нужно одержать победу.
Враг бушует, его время здесь мало.
Он лжёт и кроит правду на свой лад.
Грех в наших жизнях — вот его цель большая.
Он знает: душу нашу это дорого стоит — не случайно.
Не обязательно большой — хватит и малого греха.
Он обманом заманит, преследуя каждую душу.
Стрелы нечестивых летят со всех сторон.
Когда перед лицом Божьим — тот дьявол прячется вплоть до дрожи!
С Богом с нами, он не сможет продвинуться вперёд!
С Богом с нами греху не будет шансов вовсе!
Ибо очи Господни вглядываются везде,
Чтобы найти одного совершенного — и показать Силу Свою везде!
Оставим малое и взглянем далеко вперёд.
Возьмём силу Божью! Пора откликнуться!

Ellie edged her chair closer to the grown-ups who were visiting in the kitchen. Grandpa, Grandma, and Aunt Lily had stopped by for a visit, and although she didn’t always understand the conversation, she loved to listen. She found that she learned a lot of things that way.

The topic this evening was about something related to church and that got her mind to thinking about singing during Sunday morning worship services. Although Ellie was only five years old, she very much loved to sing. She thought about the fact that her dear Grandpa was a song leader in their church and how much she liked when he led a song.

At Ellie’s church the song leaders all sat around a table near the center of the church. They took turns choosing a song and then leading it for the congregation. Ellie didn’t always know the songs that were chosen. They sang out of a little black hymnbook that had lots of songs with hard words and tunes she didn’t recognize. However, in the back of this little songbook was a section called “The Appendix” and here were hymns that were familiar to her and she was always pleased when a song was announced from that part of the book. Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight. When that particular song number was announced on a Sunday morning, she always felt a twinge of excitement. She would be able to help along with this song!

I wish we would sing that song again, thought Ellie. It’s been a long time since we have.

Then a sudden thought struck her. Why couldn’t she ask Grandpa to choose that song next Sunday?

Yes, I will ask him and see what he says about that idea, she smiled to herself. She decided to wait until her grandparents were ready to leave. She followed Grandpa out the door and as he walked across the porch, she quickly stepped up next to him. “Grandpa,” she asked. “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!” She felt suddenly shy at having asked such a question, and she ducked back toward the doorway of the house.

Grandpa smiled down at her. “I think I can do that. Is that a song you like?” His eyes twinkled at Ellie. “I’ll be happy to lead that one just for you.”

Ellie could scarcely wait for church the following Sunday. She would get to sing “her” song. Grandpa said he would choose it and she had no doubt he would do as he said.

Sunday morning, she waited eagerly for the song service to begin. The first and second songs were ones that were not familiar to her. Then came time for the third one. “Let’s sing number 8 in the Appendix,” announced the song leader. Ellie’s heart sang. They were going to sing her favorite song. Her grandpa had honored her request. Her eyes shone as she joined in the singing of the beautiful song. It was a lovely hymn that spoke of Jesus’ care as a Shepherd and a Friend, and how He would always keep His children close to Himself.

Later, after church was over and they were on their way home, Ellie remarked to her mother, “Grandpa chose that one song, just like I asked him to!”

Ellie’s mom looked a bit startled. “You asked him to lead a song today? When did you ask him?”

“Yes, I did. The other evening when they visited, I asked him if he could lead it today and he said he would. And he did!” Ellie said with delight.

Mom had a strange look on her face, and she was quiet for a moment.

“Did you know that Grandpas weren’t there today? At the last minute they decided to visit elsewhere this morning for church.” Mom smiled tenderly at her little daughter. “It seems that God knew what a little girl’s heart was desiring and He led another brother to choose the song you like so much. That’s so amazing, isn’t it?” Ellie nodded. To think that Grandpa wasn’t even at church today, and still they sang her favorite song anyway! It gave her such a special feeling to know that Jesus cared for her that much.

Today, Ellie is a grown-up woman and now has children of her own. Whenever she thinks about how Jesus cares for all His children, she especially remembers how God cared about one little, five-year-old girl and the song she loved so much. As her mother said, and still does, “Of course God cares. He loves all the little children of the world!”

Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us

Savior, like a Shepherd lead us,
Much we need Thy tender care.
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
For our use Thy folds prepare:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

We are Thine, do Thou befriend us,
Be the guardian of our way.
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
Seek us when we go astray:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

Thou hast promised to receive us,
Poor and sinful though we be.
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
Grace to cleanse, and pow’r to free:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Early let us turn to Thee.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Early let us turn to Thee.

Early let us seek Thy favor,
Early let us do Thy will.
Blessed Lord and only Savior,
With Thy love our bosoms fill:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

Dorothy Ann Thrupp
