Ellie skuif haar stoel nader aan die volwassenes wat in die kombuis te besoek was. Oupa, Ouma en Tannie Lily het vir 'n draai gekom, en al het sy nie altyd die gesprek verstaan nie, het sy daarvan gehou om te luister. Sy het gevind dat sy op dié wyse baie dinge leer.

Die onderwerp vanaand was iets wat met die kerk te doen gehad het en dit het haar gedagtes laat kring oor die sangtyd tydens die Sondagoggenddiens. Al was Ellie eers vyf jaar oud, het sy baie daarvan gehou om te sing. Sy het gedink aan die feit dat haar liewe Oupa 'n sangleier in hul kerk was en hoe baie sy daarvan gehou het wanneer hy 'n lied gelei het.

By Ellie se kerk het die sangleiers almal om 'n tafel naby die middel van die kerk gesit. Hulle het om beurten 'n lied gekies en dit toe vir die gemeente gelei. Ellie het nie altyd die gekose liedjies geken nie. Hulle het uit 'n klein swart psalmbundel gesing wat baie liedere met moeilike woorde en wysies bevat het wat sy nie herken het nie. In die agterkant van daardie klein liedboek was daar egter 'n afdeling met die naam "Die Byvoeging" en daar was liedere wat vir haar bekend was, en sy was altyd bly wanneer 'n lied uit daardie deel van die boek aangekondig is. Haar gunstelinglied was "Verlosser, soos 'n Herder lei ons" en al kon sy nog nie lees nie, het sy geweet dit was nommer agt. Wanneer daardie spesifieke liednommer op 'n Sondagoggend aangekondig is, het sy altyd 'n rilling van opwinding gevoel. Ek sal hiermee kan help sing!

O, as ons daardie lied maar weer sou sing, het Ellie gedink. Dit is lanklaas wat ons dit gesing het.

Toe tref 'n skielike gedagte haar. Hoekom kan ek nie Oupa vra om daardie lied volgende Sondag te kies nie?

Ja, ek sal hom vra en sien wat hy daarvan dink, het sy vir haarself geglimlag. Sy het besluit om te wag totdat haar grootouers gereed was om te gaan. Sy het Oupa uit die deur gevolg en toe hy oor die stoep stap, het sy vinnig langs hom opgestap. “Oupa,” het sy gevra. “Dink jy jy kan die lied ‘Verlosser, soos 'n Herder lei ons’ hierdie komende Sondag lei? Ek sal dit regtig graag weer wil sing!” Sy het skielik skaam gevoel oor die vraag en sy het teruggeduik na die deur van die huis.

Oupa het na haar afgebuig en geglimlag. “Ek dink ek kan dit doen. Is dit 'n lied wat jy graag het?” Sy oë het geskitter toe hy na Ellie kyk. “Ek sal bly wees om daardie een net vir jou te lei.”

Ellie kon amper nie wag vir die kerk die volgende Sondag nie. Sy sou “haar” lied kon sing. Oupa het gesê hy sou dit kies en sy het geen twyfel gehad dat hy sou doen soos hy gesê het nie.

Sondagoggend het sy gretig gewag vir die sanglede om te begin. Die eerste en tweede lied was een wat sy nie geken het nie. Toe kom die tyd vir die derde lied. “Kom ons sing nommer 8 in die Byvoeging,” het die sangleier aangekondig. Ellie se hart het gesing. Hulle sou haar gunstelinglied sing. Haar oupa het haar versoek eer gedoen. Haar oë het gestraal toe sy by die singing van die pragtige lied aangesluit het. Dit was 'n lieflike psalm wat van Jesus se sorg as 'n Herder en 'n Vriend praat, en hoe Hy altyd Sy kinders naby Hom self sou hou.

Later, nadat die kerk verby was en hulle oppad huis toe was, het Ellie vir haar ma gesê: “Oupa het daardie een lied gekies, net soos ek hom gevra het!”

Ellie se ma het effens verbaas gelyk. “Jy het hom vandag gevra om te lei? Wanneer het jy hom gevra?”

“Ja, het ek. Die ander aand toe hulle op besoek was, het ek hom gevra of hy dit vandag kon lei en hy het gesê hy sal. En hy het!” het Ellie bly gesê.

Ma het 'n vreemde uitdrukking op haar gesig gehad en sy het vir 'n oomblik stilgebly.

“Het jy geweet dat Oupa vandag nie daar was nie? Op die laaste oomblik het hulle besluit om elders vandag vir die kerk te gaan kuier.” Ma het sagkens na haar dogtertjie geglimlag. “Dit lyk asof God geweet het wat 'n klein meisie se hart begeer en Hy het 'n ander broer gelei om die lied te kies wat jy so baie hou. Dit is wonderlik, is dit nie?” Ellie het geknik. Om daaraan te dink dat Oupa nie eens vandag by die kerk was nie, en tog het hulle haar gunstelinglied gesing! Dit het vir haar 'n besondere gevoel gegee om te weet dat Jesus so baie om haar gee.

Vandag is Ellie 'n volwasse vrou en het nou haar eie kinders. Wanneer sy dink aan hoe Jesus vir al Sy kinders sorg, onthou sy veral hoe God omgegee het aan een klein vyfjarige dogtertjie en die lied wat sy so liefgehad het. Soos haar ma gesê het, en steeds sê, “Natuurlik gee God om. Hy het liefde vir al die klein kinders van die wêreld!”

Verlosser, soos 'n Herder lei ons

Verlosser, soos 'n Herder, lei ons,
Hoeveel ons nodig het U liefdevolle sorg.
Voed ons in U lieflike weidings,
Berei vir ons U voue as ons toevlug:
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
U het ons gekoop; ons behoort aan U.
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
U het ons gekoop; ons behoort aan U.

Ons is U; wees U dan ons vriend,
Wees die waghond oor ons pad.
Bewaar U kudde, verdedig ons teen sonde,
Soek ons, wanneer ons afdwaal:
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
Hoor, O hoor ons wanneer ons bid.
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
Hoor, O hoor ons wanneer ons bid.

U het belowe om ons te ontvang,
Arm en sondig al is ons.
U het ontferming om ons te verlig,
Genade om te reinig, en krag om vry te maak:
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
Laat ons vroeg na U omkeer.
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
Laat ons vroeg na U omkeer.

Vroeg laat ons U guns soek,
Vroeg laat ons U wil doen.
Geseënde Here en enigste Verlosser,
Vul ons bors met U liefde:
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
U het ons liefgehad, bly lief vir ons steeds.
Geseënde Jesus! geseënde Jesus!
U het ons liefgehad, bly lief vir ons steeds.

Dorothy Ann Thrupp

This is the first of a series of articles on “Discipleship.” Today, Jesus is continuing to call men and women to respond to the simple call, “Follow Me.” Jesus is calling each of us to personally “Follow Me.” In this series, we will explore the depth of this simple command of Jesus. Like the disciples, you will find yourself drawn to follow Jesus.

You may experience both exhilaration and apprehension. Exhilaration, as your journey of faith takes you to heights of love that you have never known. Apprehension, as your faith is tested in new and difficult ways.

There is an emptiness in every human heart that only Jesus can fill. There is a purity and beauty in the life of Jesus that resonates with those heart longings. As we walk with Jesus, we find ourselves being transformed. Old things pass away. All things become new. His life becomes our life. His desires become our desires.

Discipleship is incumbent on the believer. Believing in Jesus, repenting of our sins, and receiving the Lord Jesus into our heart are the first steps into a lifelong journey of faith. Discipleship is not an alternate means of salvation. Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free. Following Jesus is not a carnal attempt to merit eternal life. It is the love response of one who has discovered the source of life.

If you join us on this journey, you will discover that following Jesus will lead us into the valley of decision where we will find ourselves compelled to choose between a life of total surrender to Christ or a life of sin and pleasing self.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagine yourself in a ship with one of these brethren. The sun was rising on the eastern horizon. Anticipating another day of fishing the blue waters of the Galilee, you busy yourself with the daily tasks. Fishing has been your life. You are as much at home on the sea as you are in your cottage.

Another day, another catch of fish, and you should be able to keep the creditors at bay for another week. It’s the only life you have ever known. Your father was a fisherman. Your grandfather was a fisherman. It’s a comfortable life. It’s a familiar life.

This morning, as the waves are gently lapping the sandy shoreline, a man approaches. He’s not a total stranger. Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son. He astounds the local rabbi with his knowledge of the scriptures. His character is flawless; He is the friend of all and a stranger to none.

This man, Jesus (that is his name) is drawing near to your ship. As He draws near, He calls out in a rather cheerful voice, “Follow me.”

James looks at John, and together they look to their father Zebedee. His approving nod was all that they needed. Zebedee had worked with his two sons for many years. Perhaps he was hoping that time with the Nazarene would soften the temper of their abrasive characters.

“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” That’s what He called out to Peter and Andrew. They left their little boat full of nets, perhaps tethered to a stump by the shore. What was it about this Man that He could draw disciples after Him with a simple “Follow Me”? Maybe it was a deep longing in the heart of these disciples—a “hope” that following Jesus might fulfill.

Generations of Jewish men had been looking for The Messiah—The Promised One; He who would break the Roman yoke and restore Israel to her former freedom and glory. Jesus was the most promising revolutionary prospect of the day. He would need a following. He would need their help. Little did they realize that day as they dropped their nets and followed Jesus where that journey would lead them. Little did they know that if they followed this Man, they would never be the same.

As Peter, Andrew, James, and John joined with eight others to follow Jesus, they were walking away from the familiar, secure life of the fisherman. They may have thought that following Jesus would be an adventure. They may have thought that after a term of service to the Nazarene, they could return to their fishing boats. As a matter of fact, that is what they did.

After Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection, He made several appearances to His disciples. They had not yet received the Holy Spirit, and, in the midst of this great uncertainty, they could not resist the allure of the familiar. They decided to go fishing, but much to their consternation they had lost the touch. They fished all night and caught nothing. In the morning Jesus was standing on the shore. He told them to cast on the right side of the ship. They cast and were not able to pull in the nets due to the multitude of fish.

Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No. And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes –John 21:3-6.

Have you ever found yourself in a position where you have tried and tried and all your efforts are met with failure? You know what it is to “reach the end of my hoarded resources”. If that is where you find yourself, you are in a position to experience a miracle. God shows himself strong to those who acknowledge their weakness.

When you decide to follow Jesus, He will draw you into such an utter dependence upon Him that you will finally no longer trust in yourself. To become truly like Jesus is to realize with Paul …that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing…. Paul then continues the verse …for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not –Romans 7:18.

Discipleship will lead us into a total abandonment of ourselves to Christ. Just as the disciples could not have fathomed where following Jesus would lead them, neither can we. We make a faith choice. We choose to follow. We commit the details to our Master.

If you want to be like Jesus, you cannot look back. Jesus said: …No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62. Peter looked back. He said, “I go a fishing”. Disillusioned following the crucifixion and glorious resurrection, Peter chose to return to the lifestyle that was familiar to him. He went back to fishing and James and John went with him.

When Jesus appeared on the shore after their long night of fruitless toil, He prepared a fish fry for the weary disciples. As Peter sat munching on a charbroiled fish, Jesus turned to him and said, “Peter, do you love Me more than these?” How gently piercing are the words of Jesus.

Peter responded, “Yes Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.” We do not know how much time passed, but Jesus turned to him again, “Peter…” (actually He called him Simon) “Do you love Me?” Peter gave the same staid response. “Yes Lord, you know that I love you”. It was the right answer, but Jesus was interested in more than just a right answer, so He said to him again, “Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me?”

Peter finally began to feel that Jesus was asking for something more of him—something that pierced his soul through and through. He had begun following Jesus with the desire to receive from Him. Now Jesus is asking him to reciprocate that love.

Scenes of Caiaphas’ house came before him. He saw Jesus being brutally handled, falsely accused, and spat upon. He heard the angry shouting of the Sanhedrin as they called for Jesus’ death. And then there was that persistent young damsel that challenged him that he was one of Jesus’ disciples. He said to her, “I am not”. Three times he had denied knowing Jesus and now three times Jesus has challenged his love.

In anguish of heart Peter cried out, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee”. Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep”. From that day, Peter was a man with a calling, not only to know Christ for the purpose of receiving from him, but also to emulate him. Discipleship is more than merely knowing about Jesus. Discipleship is walking in his footsteps and identifying with Jesus in his ministry and in his sufferings—truly knowing Him.

Jesus is asking you today, “Do you love me?” We all know the right answer, “Yes, of course, I love Jesus.” Then “Love your neighbor” – “Serve the needy” – “Defer to your brother” – “Forgive the one that has offended you”.

Discipleship is very practical in that it moves us beyond the ideological and causes us to become the very hands and feet of Jesus to those around us.

If in your heart you are thinking, this doesn’t sound very appealing, I would encourage you to focus on the moment and the task at hand. Peter walked with Jesus for three and a half years before he received this call from Jesus. Jesus never calls us without equipping us, and He doesn’t equip us until He determines that we are ready. After the Day of Pentecost, Peter was called, he was prepared, and he was equipped. Then God used him mightily to establish the church.

I would like to call your attention to another attribute of discipleship that is sometimes misplaced. Discipleship is never intended to be drudgery. If you find following Jesus to be hard and toilsome, that is evidence that your love has not yet been perfected.

Jesus’ soul-piercing question to Peter was quite simple, “Do you love Me?” It was as if Jesus was testing Peter. [“I have a job for you, Peter, but a prerequisite for this job is your devoted love for Me.”] Discipleship is a love response to Jesus. Our love for Christ makes service a joy. Toil is pleasant and sacrifice is not a loss.

We can best understand this in the context of human relationships. If you are married and you truly love your husband or your wife, you do not even consider it a sacrifice to work for the mutual benefit of your marriage. In the same way, if we are truly in love with Jesus it is not considered toil to work for him. No sacrifice that we make for the kingdom of heaven is a loss.

I welcome you to join us as we explore the realities of discipleship. We will learn from Christ’s example of forgiveness. We will gain a greater understanding of what it means to walk by faith. Jesus taught us to not worry but to trust. He taught lessons on servant leadership and on cross bearing. There is so much to discover when we are walking with Jesus.

Expect to be changed. The teachings of Jesus are revolutionary in that they run counter to our human impulses. Purpose to allow the life of Christ to become your life and you will be amazed by what God will do for you.

Dette er den første i en serie artikler om «Disippelskap». I dag fortsetter Jesus å kalle menn og kvinner til å svare på den enkle oppfordringen: «Følg meg.» Jesus kaller hver enkelt av oss til personlig å «følge meg.» I denne serien skal vi utforske dybden i dette enkle budet fra Jesus. Som disiplene vil du finne deg selv dratt til å følge Jesus.

Du kan oppleve både begeistring og uro. Begeistring når din trosreise fører deg til kjærlighetens høyder som du aldri har kjent. Uro når din tro blir prøvet på nye og vanskelige måter.

Det er en tomhet i hvert menneskehjerte som bare Jesus kan fylle. Det er en renhet og skjønnhet i Jesu liv som resonnerer med hjertets lengsler. Etter hvert som vi går med Jesus, opplever vi å bli forvandlet. Det gamle går bort. Alt blir nytt. Hans liv blir vårt liv. Hans ønsker blir våre ønsker.

Disippelskap påligger den troende. Å tro på Jesus, omvende seg fra våre synder og ta imot Herre Jesus i vårt hjerte er de første skrittene inn i en livslang trosreise. Disippelskap er ikke et alternativt middel til frelse. Å følge Jesus er svaret fra en sjel som er satt fri. Å følge Jesus er ikke et kjødelig forsøk på å fortjene evig liv. Det er kjærlighetssvaret fra den som har funnet livets kilde.

Hvis du blir med oss på denne reisen, vil du oppdage at det å følge Jesus vil lede oss inn i beslutningens dal hvor vi blir tvunget til å velge mellom et liv i full overgivelse til Kristus eller et liv i synd og selvbehag.

Og Jesus, mens han gikk ved Genesarets sjø, så han to brødre, Simon som kalles Peter, og Andreas hans bror, som kastet garn i sjøen; for de var fiskere. Og han sier til dem: Følg meg, så vil jeg gjøre dere til menneskefiskere. Og de forlot straks garnene og fulgte ham. Og fra der gikk han videre og så to andre brødre, Jakob, Sebedeus’ sønn, og Johannes hans bror, i et skip sammen med Sebedeus deres far, som reparerte garnene; og han kalte dem. Og de forlot straks skipet og deres far og fulgte ham – Matteus 4:18-22.

Forestill deg at du er i et skip sammen med en av disse brødrene. Solen sto opp i østhimmelen. I forventning om enda en fiskedag på Genesarets blå vann, gjør du deg opptatt med daglige gjøremål. Fiske har vært ditt liv. Du er like hjemme på sjøen som i hytta di.

Enda en dag, enda en fangst av fisk, og du burde kunne holde kreditorene unna en uke til. Det er det eneste livet du noen gang har kjent. Faren din var fisker. Bestefaren din var fisker. Det er et behagelig liv. Det er et kjent liv.

Denne morgenen, mens bølgene mykt slo mot den sandete strandkanten, nærmer en mann seg. Han er ikke en total fremmed. Alle vet om Marias sønn. Alle har en mening om Marias sønn. Han forbløffer byens rabbi med sin kunnskap om Skriften. Hans karakter er feilfri; han er venn av alle og ukjent for ingen.

Denne mannen, Jesus (det er hans navn), nærmer seg skipet ditt. Idet han kommer nær, roper han med en ganske munter stemme: «Følg meg.»

Jakob ser på Johannes, og sammen ser de mot faren Sebedeus. Hans godkjennende nikk var alt de trengte. Sebedeus hadde arbeidet med sine to sønner i mange år. Kanskje håpet han at tid med Nasarenen ville mildne temperamentet i deres skarpe væremåte.

«Følg meg, så vil jeg gjøre dere til menneskefiskere.» Det var det han ropte til Peter og Andreas. De forlot sin lille båt full av garn, kanskje fortøyd til en stokk ved strandkanten. Hva var det ved denne mannen som kunne dra disipler etter seg med et enkelt «Følg meg»? Kanskje lå det en dyp lengsel i disiplene—et «håp» om at det å følge Jesus ville gi oppfyllelse.

Generasjoner av jødiske menn hadde ventet på Messias—Den lovede; han som ville bryte den romerske åket og gjenopprette Israel til sin tidligere frihet og herlighet. Jesus var den mest lovende revolusjonære utsikten i samtiden. Han ville trenge en følge. Han ville trenge deres hjelp. Lite visste de den dagen da de kastet garnene og fulgte Jesus hvor den reisen ville føre dem. Lite visste de at hvis de fulgte denne mannen, ville de aldri bli de samme.

Da Peter, Andreas, Jakob og Johannes sluttet seg til åtte andre for å følge Jesus, gikk de bort fra fiskerens velkjente, sikre liv. De kan ha trodd at det å følge Jesus ville bli et eventyr. De kan ha tenkt at etter en tjenestetid hos Nasarenen kunne de vende tilbake til fiskebåtene sine. Og faktisk var det hva de gjorde.

Etter Jesu korsfestelse og oppstandelse viste han seg flere ganger for disiplene. De hadde ennå ikke fått Den Hellige Ånd, og midt i denne store usikkerheten kunne de ikke motstå det kjente. De bestemte seg for å gå ut og fiske, men til sin forbauselse hadde de mistet takten. De fisket hele natten uten å få noe. Om morgenen stod Jesus på stranden. Han ba dem kaste på høyre side av skipet. De kastet og kunne ikke dra garnene opp på grunn av mengden fisk.

Simon Peter sier til dem: Jeg går og fisker. De sier til ham: Vi følger deg også. De gikk da ut og gikk straks i båten; og den natten fikk de ingenting. Men da morgenen var kommet, stod Jesus på stranden; men disiplene kjente ikke at det var Jesus. Da sier Jesus til dem: Barn, har dere noe mat? De svarte ham: Nei. Og han sier til dem: Kast garnet på høyre side av båten, så skal dere finne. De kastet altså, og nå klarte de ikke å dra det opp for fiskemengden – Johannes 21:3-6.

Har du noen gang funnet deg i en situasjon der du har prøvd og prøvd og alle dine anstrengelser ender i fiasko? Du vet hva det er å «nå enden av mine oppsparte krefter». Hvis det er der du befinner deg, er du i en posisjon til å erfare et mirakel. Gud viser seg sterk for dem som erkjenner sin svakhet.

Når du bestemmer deg for å følge Jesus, vil han føre deg inn i en slik fullstendig avhengighet av ham at du endelig ikke lenger stoler på deg selv. Å bli virkelig lik Jesus er å innse med Paulus …at i meg (det vil si i mitt kjød) bor intet godt… Paulus fortsetter så verset …for å ville er hos meg; men å utføre det gode finner jeg ikke – Romerne 7:18.

Disippelskap vil lede oss til en total overgivelse av oss selv til Kristus. Akkurat som disiplene ikke kunne fatte hvor det å følge Jesus ville føre dem, kan heller ikke vi det. Vi tar et trosvalg. Vi velger å følge. Vi overgir detaljene til vår Mester.

Hvis du vil være lik Jesus, kan du ikke se tilbake. Jesus sa: …Ingen som har lagt hånden til plogen og ser tilbake, er skikket for Guds rike – Lukas 9:62. Peter så tilbake. Han sa: «Jeg går og fisker». Desillusjonert etter korsfestelsen og den herlige oppstandelsen, valgte Peter å vende tilbake til den livsstilen som var kjent for ham. Han gikk tilbake til fisket, og Jakob og Johannes gikk med ham.

Da Jesus viste seg på stranden etter deres lange natt med ufruktbart slit, gjorde han opp en fiskemiddag for de trette disiplene. Mens Peter satt og småspiste en grillet fisk, vendte Jesus seg til ham og sa: «Peter, elsker du meg mer enn disse?» Hvor ømt gjennomborende var ikke Jesu ord.

Peter svarte: «Ja Herre, du vet at jeg elsker deg.» Jesus sa: «Fôr mine lam.» Vi vet ikke hvor mye tid som gikk, men Jesus vendte seg igjen til ham: «Peter…» (egentlig kalte han ham Simon) «elsker du meg?» Peter ga det samme faste svaret: «Ja Herre, du vet at jeg elsker deg.» Det var riktig svar, men Jesus ville ha mer enn bare et riktig svar, så han sa igjen til ham: «Simon, Jonas’ sønn, elsker du meg?»

Peter begynte endelig å føle at Jesus krevde noe mer av ham—noe som gjennomboret hans sjel på dypet. Han hadde begynt å følge Jesus med et ønske om å motta fra ham. Nå ba Jesus ham om å svare denne kjærligheten.

Scener fra Kajafas hus kom for hans indre syn. Han så Jesus bli mishandlet brutalt, falskt anklaget og spyttet på. Han hørte den rasende ropingen fra sannhetsrådet mens de krevde Jesu død. Og så var det den vedvarende unge piken som utfordret ham og sa at han var en av Jesu disipler. Han sa til henne: «Det er jeg ikke». Tre ganger hadde han fornektet å kjenne Jesus, og nå tre ganger utfordrer Jesus hans kjærlighet.

I hjerteskjærende kval ropte Peter: «Herre, du vet alt; du vet at jeg elsker deg.» Jesus sier til ham: «Fôr mine sauer.» Fra den dag var Peter en mann med en kall—ikke bare å kjenne Kristus for å motta fra ham, men også å etterligne ham. Disippelskap er mer enn å vite om Jesus. Disippelskap er å gå i hans fotspor og identifisere seg med Jesus i hans tjeneste og i hans lidelser—virkelig å kjenne ham.

Jesus spør deg i dag: «Elsker du meg?» Vi kjenner alle det riktige svaret: «Ja, selvfølgelig, jeg elsker Jesus.» Så «elsk din neste» – «tjener de trengende» – «ettergi din bror» – «tilgi den som har fornærmet deg».

Disippelskap er svært praktisk ved at det fører oss utover det ideologiske og gjør oss til Jesu hender og føtter for dem rundt oss.

Hvis du i ditt hjerte tenker, dette høres ikke særlig tiltalende ut, vil jeg oppmuntre deg til å fokusere på øyeblikket og oppgaven foran deg. Peter vandret med Jesus i tre og et halvt år før han mottok dette kall fra Jesus. Jesus kaller oss aldri uten å utruste oss, og han utruster oss ikke før han fastslår at vi er klare. Etter pinsedagen ble Peter kalt, forberedt og utrustet. Så brukte Gud ham mektig til å grunnlegge kirken.

Jeg vil gjerne rette din oppmerksomhet mot en annen egenskap ved disippelskap som noen ganger blir misforstått. Disippelskap er aldri ment å være trått arbeid. Hvis du finner det vanskelig og slitsomt å følge Jesus, er det bevis på at din kjærlighet ennå ikke er fullkomnet.

Jesu sjelsgjennomtrengende spørsmål til Peter var ganske enkelt: «Elsker du meg?» Det var som om Jesus testet Peter. [«Jeg har en oppgave til deg, Peter, men et krav for denne oppgaven er din hengivne kjærlighet til meg.»] Disippelskap er et kjærlighetssvar til Jesus. Vår kjærlighet til Kristus gjør tjenesten til glede. Arbeid er behagelig og offer er ikke et tap.

Vi forstår dette best i menneskelige relasjoner. Er du gift og virkelig elsker din mann eller din kone, betraktes det ikke engang som et offer å arbeide for ekteskapets gjensidige beste. På samme måte, hvis vi virkelig er forelsket i Jesus, anses det ikke som anstrengelse å tjene ham. Intet offer vi gir for himmelrikets rike er et tap.

Jeg ønsker deg velkommen til å bli med oss mens vi utforsker realitetene i disippelskap. Vi vil lære av Kristi eksempel på tilgivelse. Vi vil få en større forståelse av hva det betyr å gå ved tro. Jesus lærte oss å ikke bekymre oss, men å stole. Han underviste i tjenerlederskap og i å bære kors. Det er så mye å oppdage når vi går med Jesus.

Forvent å bli forandret. Jesu lære er revolusjonerende ved at den går imot våre menneskelige impulser. Bestem deg for å la Kristi liv bli ditt liv, og du vil bli forundret over hva Gud vil gjøre for deg.

When you, my friend, are standing on this earth
And gazing up into the firmament
Where stretches all of space, what do you see?
A great black blanket stretched o’er all the sky
With many a mystery light somewhere up there?
Or can you see the distances so great
Which stretch the mind almost to breaking point
And make you feel the size you really are?
In the still silence of the spacious sky,
The far-off planets seem almost in reach
Compared to the great distance to the stars.
The crescent moon is closer yet to you,
And yet it took man three whole days to reach
That tiny sphere so very close at hand.
But what you see while gazing up to heights
Which you cannot begin to comprehend
Is but a streak of all the vast expanse
Beyond the knowledge of this human race.
And so, my friend, I hope that you will feel
That greatness, vastness, emptiness of space
Which our Creator made for us so we
Can feel His greatness and His tender love
And humbly bow our heads and worship Him.

–by Daniel Kaufman

E olhando para o firmamento lá no alto
Onde todo o espaço se estende, o que vês?
Um grande manto negro estendido por todo o céu
Com muitos mistérios de luz em algum lugar lá em cima?
Ou consegues ver as distâncias tão grandes
Que esticam a mente quase até romper
E te fazem sentir o tamanho que realmente és?
No silêncio imóvel do amplo céu,
Os planetas distantes parecem quase ao alcance
Comparados com a imensa distância às estrelas.
A lua crescente está ainda mais próxima de ti,

Aquela pequena esfera tão perto à mão.

Que não podes começar a compreender
É apenas um rasgo de toda a vastidão
Além do conhecimento desta raça humana.
E assim, meu amigo, espero que sintas
Essa grandeza, vastidão, vazio do espaço
Que nosso Criador fez para nós, para que possamos
Sentir Sua grandeza e Seu terno amor
E humilde inclinar nossas cabeças e adorá-Lo.

The things that are bad will all be in hell.

When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

It’s been said that in the 1500s, after baptism, the Anabaptists lived an average of only 27 days. They were hunted and killed. They realized one thing—serving Christ would most certainly cost them everything. They forsook the comforts of easy living; they forsook it all. It could also have been a similar situation when Jesus walked on the earth, or shortly after He was killed.

…and he turned, and said unto them, If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple. For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish. Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple –Luke 14:25-33.

Jesus clearly asked His disciples to count the cost. And they must have counted the cost, for they faithfully gave all, including their lives, for Christ’s Kingdom. They realized they could have had the good things in this life; however, they also realized it would cost them the good things in the next.

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution –2 Timothy 3:12. If we look at the promises which Jesus gave us in His Word about persecution, and then compare them with the lives of Jesus’ followers today, we might be confused. And rightfully so.

He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked –1 John 2:6. Jesus says we should walk as He walked, He also tells us that we need to follow Him.

How did He walk? We know that Jesus had no place to lay His head—this was how He wanted it. We know that Jesus could have chosen to live where and how He wanted. He was, in fact, in control of the whole world, yet He was despised and rejected by the world and its system. When He spoke, people wanted to lay their hands on Him; they wanted to kill Him. He was not a popular person; He had few friends. In reality, He didn’t fit in, and He didn’t last long. Three years after His ministry began, He was killed. …He was numbered with the transgressors –Mark 15:28.

What about His followers today? Are they walking how He walked? And if not, why not?

We read about the children of Israel going through the wilderness. They fought and overtook the cities in their paths, killing all in the process. We read many accounts about how God instructed the children of Israel to kill all of the enemy, even the women and children. The following is one such account of many.

So the LORD our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining. And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many. And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city –Deuteronomy 3:3-6.

We read accounts like this in scripture, and it can cause us to cringe. It is almost as if life itself was not important. Even in the New Testament, death doesn’t seem to be that big of a deal. People lived and people died.

The first week after we moved to Haiti, I was driving through the city. Suddenly, right in front of me I saw a man lying in the street. Blood ran down the road and pooled in a low spot—he was dead. I was shocked. But what shocked me the most was that no one seemed to notice. People by the hundreds busily walked around him, not even looking at the man—no one cared.

Over the next six years we saw many dead or dying people—it became a normal scene.

If that was how it was back in the Bible times, and it is still how it is today in many countries of the world, maybe we are the ones that are out of the norm? Maybe we esteem life higher than God does. Maybe we are among those that Jesus spoke of when He said—He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal –John 12:25.

In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:19. We were created out of the dust, and after a few short years, we return to the very same dust.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –James 4:14. The Bible also calls our lives a vapor.

We all know what happens after that—the judgment, then eternity. So why do we care so much about this life? Maybe it is an American problem or a western problem.

It is obvious that Americans are looked upon as ‘more valuable’ than most other nationalities. If you are an American in a developing country, you are heralded as a king. If something happens to an American, it is quickly headline news. I once stood over the bodies of two murdered men. One of their close friends stood by, so I asked him how he was doing. He shrugged and said, “This is life”.

So why does life mean so much to us Americans? The answer is simple. We can obtain almost anything we want; money is easy to get, and we can live how we want. We can live in pleasure every day. We go to the store and buy what we want, when we want—we have it our way. This is just how it is; for most of us it is all we have ever known—the life of plenty. So how does this affect us?

This type of living makes it especially hard to ‘give all’ for Christ. It makes it difficult to obey Jesus’ command to …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15. It makes it difficult to say with the Apostle Paul, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. In reality, it makes it difficult to be a Christian.

When Jesus said… For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25, what did He mean? Could it mean literally just what it says: that when you fall in love with your own life, you cannot effectively follow Christ, so that in the end you will actually lose your life?

Can you go to the lost and forsake the comforts of this life if it’s those comforts that you love and live for? It’s not likely. What we have is “Americanized” Christians that will only go to the mission field if they can take their comforts with them. This produces rich, comfortable missionaries who, despite their best efforts, can’t win the lost, rather they make them jealous. Can we go into the cities and preach the gospel to the lost like so many before us have? Can we take time to teach and disciple the tens of thousands who are seeking? If we love our lives, we probably will not, since there is too much to lose and it’s a waste of good talent and opportunity. God help us.

When we are living to please the flesh and we have our lives figured out, it is hard for God to use us. We are puffed up. We tend to believe that God has blessed us because of all our possessions and our status in life; but isn’t this the prosperity gospel? What if that changed? Would we still consider ourselves to be blessed? Is it God or our own doing that causes us to be joyful? What if we found ourselves in John the Baptist’s shoes? Or the Apostle Paul’s? If we would be sitting in prison for doing nothing wrong, would our joy remain? It should if the Holy Spirit is living and working in our hearts. The Bible says that we can suffer joyfully!

Years ago, a coworker of mine was a happy fellow. He had a nice life. There was one problem—he did not believe there was a God. We would talk day after day. He would constantly tell me how happy he was and that one didn’t need to be a Christian to be happy. He would talk about his nice life, all that he possessed, his good job, his nice family. Interestingly enough, he truly did seem happy.

I would tell him that true happiness didn’t come from the things that we possess or the position that we find ourselves in, but he would just disagree. He also proclaimed that he lived a better life than most Christians that he knew. He also said he didn’t get angry like most Christians and could control himself. I tried to convince him that he was deceived. At times I would think I was getting somewhere with him, then later it would seem I was far from reaching him. One day he soberly admitted that I seemed to be different that most Christians he had known in the past, but that still wasn’t enough.

I left that job and lost contact with him. Recently, I ran into another one of my former coworkers. I quickly thought of my friend and asked how he was doing. He looked at me strangely and then shocked me to my core as he said, “He committed suicide”.

The devil wants us to love our life—it’s that simple. When we love our life, we focus on it, we cherish it. The last thing we want to do is lose our life, even if it is for something eternal.

When I was in the Marines, they would constantly remind us that our lives were not number one; our country was. There are many young men who put their country first. Many have gone and given their all; many have died.

In World War 2, the Japanese would try to sneak up to a fox hole housing soldiers and throw in a grenade. Many times, it didn’t end like the Japanese wanted, because someone would jump on the grenade, absorbing the explosion. Thousands gave their lives to save their friends and defend their country. But be sure, if their priorities were not in order (of country first before themselves), they would not have done so.

If someone today, in America, would risk their life for the sake of the gospel, he would be labeled as foolish, reckless, and immature. But what do we say about so many before us—the ones that gave their lives while standing for the same things that we say we believe today? And what about the thousands today who are putting their lives on the line in other countries—are they foolish? Let’s look at a very obvious example in Acts.

And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus. And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem. Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. –Acts 21:10-13.

What would we think of Paul’s actions today? Paul went to Jerusalem and was quickly taken, beaten, and put in prison. It was the beginning of the end for our dear brother. He was moved from prison to prison and eventually ended up in Rome where he was beheaded. What do you think the ones that tried to persuade him to not go to Jerusalem thought? Do you think they called him a fool? Did they shake their heads and say, “I told him not to go!”?

We cannot know for sure. However, I am sure that Paul was simply putting the kingdom of Christ first; his life did not matter. He was obeying God, and God had told him to go.

When we love our lives, it is very difficult to be an effective disciple of the Lord Jesus. We end up forsaking God’s calling and then we are stuck trying to live the Christian life alone, and without God—no spiritual help from above, causing us to fall way short of the mark.

It’s ironic that only when we forsake all, including our lives, will we find true peace and purpose for our lives. And when we love our lives, that is when we will lose them.

Rise up, O saints of God!
Have done with lesser things.
Give heart and soul and mind and strength
To serve the King of kings.

Rise up, O saints of God!
The kingdom tarries long.
Bring in the day of Christlike love
And end the night of wrong.

Lift high the cross of Christ!
Tread where His feet have trod.
Led onward by the Son of Man,
Rise up, O saints of God!

Let us rise up, as God’s people, and begin to be done with lesser things, with our gaze on things above, not on the things of this earth. Yes, we will stand out; we will be labeled fools and many other things. However, we will once again catch God’s attention and the fires of revival will once again burn!

Det har blitt sagt at på 1500-tallet levde anabaptistene i gjennomsnitt bare 27 dager etter dåpen. De ble jaktet på og drept. De innså én ting—å tjene Kristus ville med sikkerhet koste dem alt. De forlot bekvemmelighetene ved et lett liv; de forlot alt. Det kunne også ha vært en lignende situasjon da Jesus vandret på jorden, eller kort tid etter at Han ble drept.

…og han vendte seg, og sa til dem: Om noen kommer til meg og ikke hater sin far og mor og hustru og barn og brødre og søstre, ja, og sitt eget liv også, kan han ikke være min disippel. Og hver den som ikke tar sitt kors opp og følger etter meg, kan ikke være min disippel. For hvilken av dere, som vil bygge et tårn, sitter ikke først ned og regner kostnadene, om han har nok til å fullføre det? For at det ikke skal hende, at etter at han har lagt grunnmuren og ikke kan fullføre det, alle som ser det, begynner å håne ham og sier: Denne mannen begynte å bygge og kunne ikke fullføre. Eller hvilken konge, som går til krig mot en annen konge, sitter ikke først ned og rådfører seg om han med ti tusen kan møte ham som kommer mot ham med tyve tusen? Ellers, mens den andre ennå er langt borte, sender han ambassadører og krever fredsbetingelser. Slik også, hver den av dere som ikke forkaster alt han eier, kan ikke være min disippel –Lukas 14:25-33.

Jesus ba tydelig sine disipler om å regne kostnaden. Og de må ha regnet kostnaden, for de gav trofast alt, inkludert sine liv, for Kristi rike. De forsto at de kunne ha hatt livets gode ting; men de forsto også at det ville koste dem de gode tingene i det neste livet.

Ja, og alle som vil leve fromt i Kristus Jesus, skal lide forfølgelse –2 Timoteus 3:12. Hvis vi ser på de løftene Jesus ga oss i Hans Ord om forfølgelse, og så sammenligner dem med livet til Jesu etterfølgere i dag, kan vi bli forvirret. Og med rette.

Han som sier at han blir i ham, bør også selv vandre slik som han vandret –1 Johannes 2:6. Jesus sier at vi skal vandre slik Han vandret, Han sier også at vi må følge Ham.

Hvordan vandret Han? Vi vet at Jesus ikke hadde noe sted å legge hodet—slik ønsket Han det. Vi vet at Jesus kunne ha valgt å leve hvor og hvordan Han ville. Han var, faktisk, herre over hele verden, likevel ble Han foraktet og forkastet av verden og dens system. Når Han talte, ville folk gripe tak i Ham; de ville drepe Ham. Han var ikke en populær person; Han hadde få venner. I realiteten passet Han ikke inn, og Han var ikke lengevarende. Tre år etter at Hans tjeneste begynte, ble Han drept. …Han ble talt blant lovbrytere –Markus 15:28.

Hva med Hans etterfølgere i dag? Går de slik Han gikk? Og hvis ikke, hvorfor ikke?

Vi leser om Israels barn som drog gjennom ørkenen. De kjempet og inntok byene i sine veier, og drepte alle i prosessen. Vi leser mange fortellinger om hvordan Gud befalte Israels barn å drepe alle fiendene, til og med kvinner og barn. Følgende er en slik beretning blant mange.

Så gav Herren vår Gud oss også Og, kongen i Basan, og hele hans folk i vår hånd; og vi slo ham til ingen gjensto. Og vi tok alle hans byer på den tid; det var ikke en by blant dem som vi ikke tok, seksti byer, hele Argobs slette, Og kongedømme i Basan. Alle disse byene var omgitt av høye murer, porter og bommer; i tillegg mange ubefestede byer. Og vi utslettet dem fullstendig, slik vi gjorde med Sihon, kongen i Hesbon, ved å utslette mennene, kvinnene og barna i hver by –5 Mosebok 3:3-6.

Vi leser slike beretninger i Skriften, og det kan få oss til å krympe oss. Det er nesten som om livet selv ikke var viktig. Selv i Det nye testamente ser ikke døden ut til å være en så stor sak. Folk levde og folk døde.

Den første uken etter at vi flyttet til Haiti, kjørte jeg gjennom byen. Plutselig så jeg rett foran meg en mann liggende i gaten. Blod rant nedover veien og samlet seg i et lavt sted—han var død. Jeg var sjokkert. Men det som sjokkerte meg mest var at ingen så ut til å legge merke til det. Hundrevis av mennesker travet forbi ham i all hast, uten engang å se på mannen—ingen brydde seg.

I de neste seks årene så vi mange døde eller døende mennesker—det ble en vanlig scene.

Hvis det var slik tilbake i bibeltiden, og det fortsatt er slik i mange land i verden i dag, kanskje er det oss som er utenfor normen? Kanskje verdsetter vi livet høyere enn Gud gjør. Kanskje er vi blant dem Jesus talte om når Han sa—Den som elsker sitt liv, skal miste det; og den som hater sitt liv i denne verden, skal bevare det til evig liv –Johannes 12:25.

Med svett av ditt ansikt skal du spise brød, inntil du vender tilbake til jorden; for av den ble du tatt: for støv er du, og til støv skal du vende tilbake –1 Mosebok 3:19. Vi ble skapt av støv, og etter noen få korte år vender vi tilbake til nettopp det støvet.

Dere vet ikke hva morgendagen vil bringe. For hva er deres liv? Det er bare en forbigående damp som viser seg for en liten tid, og så forsvinner den –Jakobsbrev 4:14. Bibelen kaller også våre liv en damp.

Vi vet alle hva som skjer etter det—dommen, så evigheten. Så hvorfor bryr vi oss så mye om dette livet? Kanskje er det et amerikansk problem eller et vestlig problem.

Det er åpenbart at amerikanere blir sett på som «mer verdifulle» enn de fleste andre nasjonaliteter. Hvis du er amerikaner i et utviklingsland, blir du hyllet som en konge. Hvis noe skjer med en amerikaner, blir det raskt toppsak i nyhetene. Jeg sto en gang over likene av to myrdede menn. En av deres nære venner sto ved siden av, så jeg spurte ham hvordan han hadde det. Han trakk på skuldrene og sa: «Slik er livet».

Så hvorfor betyr livet så mye for oss amerikanere? Svaret er enkelt. Vi kan få nesten hva vi vil; penger er lett å skaffe, og vi kan leve slik vi ønsker. Vi kan leve i nytelse hver dag. Vi går i butikken og kjøper det vi vil, når vi vil—vi får det på vår måte. Slik er det bare; for de fleste av oss er det alt vi noen gang har kjent—et liv i overflod. Så hvordan påvirker dette oss?

Denne typen liv gjør det spesielt vanskelig å «gi alt» for Kristus. Det gjør det vanskelig å adlyde Jesu befaling om …Gå ut i all verden og forkynn evangeliet for all skapningen –Markus 16:15. Det gjør det vanskelig å si med apostelen Paulus, For meg er livet Kristus, og døden en vinning –Filipperne 1:21. I realiteten gjør det det vanskelig å være en kristen.

Når Jesus sa… For den som vil frelse sitt liv, skal miste det; og den som mister sitt liv for min skyld, skal finne det –Matteus 16:25, hva mente Han? Kunne det bety bokstavelig det det sier: at når du forelsker deg i ditt eget liv, kan du ikke effektivt følge Kristus, slik at du til slutt faktisk mister ditt liv?

Kan du gå til de fortapte og forlate denne livets bekvemmeligheter hvis det er disse bekvemmelighetene du elsker og lever for? Det er ikke sannsynlig. Det vi har er «amerikaniserte» kristne som bare vil dra til misjonsmarken hvis de kan ta med seg bekvemmelighetene sine. Dette produserer rike, komfortable misjonærer som, til tross for sine beste anstrengelser, ikke kan vinne de fortapte; snarere gjør de dem misunnelige. Kan vi gå inn i byene og forkynne evangeliet for de fortapte slik så mange før oss har gjort? Kan vi ta oss tid til å lære og disippelgjøre titusenvis som søker? Hvis vi elsker våre liv, vil vi sannsynligvis ikke gjøre det, for det er for mye å tape og det er en bortkastet god evne og mulighet. Gud hjelpe oss.

Når vi lever for å glede kjødet og vi har våre liv fullstendig ordnet, er det vanskelig for Gud å bruke oss. Vi blir oppblåste. Vi har en tendens til å tro at Gud har velsignet oss på grunn av alle eiendelene våre og vår status i livet; men er ikke dette velstandsevangeliet? Hva om det endret seg? Ville vi fortsatt anse oss som velsignet? Er det Gud eller vår egen innsats som får oss til å være glade? Hva om vi befant oss i Johannes Døperens sko? Eller apostelen Paulus’? Hvis vi satt i fengsel for ingen skyld, ville gleden vår bestå? Den burde det hvis Den Hellige Ånd bor og virker i våre hjerter. Bibelen sier at vi kan lide med glede!

For mange år siden var en arbeidkamerat av meg en glad fyr. Han hadde et fint liv. Det var ett problem—han trodde ikke at det fantes en Gud. Vi snakket dag etter dag. Han fortalte meg stadig hvor lykkelig han var og at man ikke trengte å være kristen for å være lykkelig. Han snakket om sitt fine liv, alt han eide, sin gode jobb, sin hyggelige familie. Interessant nok så det virkelig ut som om han var lykkelig.

Jeg sa til ham at sann lykke ikke kom fra tingene vi eier eller posisjonen vi befinner oss i, men han var bare uenig. Han proklamerte også at han levde et bedre liv enn de fleste kristne han kjente. Han sa også at han ikke ble sint slik mange kristne gjorde og at han kunne kontrollere seg. Jeg prøvde å overbevise ham om at han var villedet. Til tider trodde jeg at jeg kom et stykke fram, så senere virket det som om jeg var langt fra å nå ham. En dag erkjente han edruelig at jeg syntes annerledes enn de fleste kristne han hadde kjent, men det var likevel ikke nok.

Jeg sluttet i den jobben og mistet kontakten med ham. Nylig møtte jeg en annen av mine tidligere kolleger. Jeg tenkte raskt på vennen min og spurte hvordan det gikk med ham. Han så på meg underlig og sjokkerte meg til beinet da han sa: «Han begikk selvmord».

Djevelen vil at vi skal elske livet vårt—det er så enkelt. Når vi elsker livet vårt, fokuserer vi på det, vi skatter det. Det siste vi ønsker er å miste livet vårt, selv om det er for noe evig.

Da jeg var i marinen, minnet de oss stadig på at livene våre ikke var nummer én; landet vårt var. Det er mange unge menn som setter landet først. Mange har gått og gitt alt; mange har dødd.

I andre verdenskrig forsøkte japanerne å snike seg bort til en revne med soldater og kaste inn en granat. Mange ganger endte det ikke slik japanerne ønsket, for noen ville hoppe på granaten og absorbere eksplosjonen. Tusener ga sine liv for å redde sine venner og forsvare landet sitt. Men vær sikker: hvis deres prioriteringer ikke hadde vært i orden (landet først foran dem selv), ville de ikke ha gjort det.

Hvis noen i dag, i Amerika, ville risikere livet for evangeliets skyld, ville han bli kalt dum, hensynsløs og umoden. Men hva sier vi om så mange før oss—de som gav sine liv mens de sto for de samme tingene vi sier vi tror i dag? Og hva med de tusenvis i dag som setter livet på spill i andre land—er de dumme? La oss se på et veldig åpenbart eksempel i Apostlenes gjerninger.

Og mens vi var der noen dager, kom det ned fra Judea en profet ved navn Agabus. Og da han kom til oss, tok han Paulus’ belte og bandt sine egne hender og føtter og sa: Slik sier Den Hellige Ånd: Slik skal jødene i Jerusalem binde mannen hvis dette beltet er, og overgi ham i hedningenes hender. Og da vi hørte dette, bad både vi og de som var på det stedet ham om ikke å gå opp til Jerusalem. Men Paulus svarte: Hva vil dere, at dere skal gråte og knuse mitt hjerte? For jeg er rede ikke bare til å bli bundet, men også til å dø i Jerusalem for Herrens Jesu navn. –Apostlenes gjerninger 21:10-13.

Hva ville vi ha tenkt om Paulus’ handlinger i dag? Paulus dro til Jerusalem og ble raskt tatt, slått og kastet i fengsel. Det var begynnelsen på slutten for vår kjære bror. Han ble flyttet fra fengsel til fengsel og endte til slutt i Roma hvor han ble halshugget. Hva tror du de som forsøkte å overtale ham til ikke å dra til Jerusalem tenkte? Tror du de kalte ham en tosk? Ristet de på hodet og sa: «Jeg sa ham at han ikke skulle dra!»?

Vi kan ikke være sikre. Men jeg er sikker på at Paulus enkelt og greit satte Kristi rike først; hans liv spilte ingen rolle. Han adlød Gud, og Gud hadde sagt til ham å gå.

Når vi elsker våre liv, er det veldig vanskelig å være en effektiv disippel for Herren Jesus. Vi ender opp med å forakte Guds kall og så sitter vi fast i å forsøke å leve kristenlivet alene og uten Gud—uten åndelig hjelp ovenfra, noe som gjør at vi faller langt kort for målet.

Det er ironisk at først når vi forkaster alt, inkludert våre liv, finner vi sann fred og livet formål. Og når vi elsker våre liv, er det da vi vil miste dem.

Stå opp, o helgener av Gud!
Gjør slutt på de mindre ting.
Gi hjerte og sjel og sinn og styrke
Til å tjene Kongenes Konge.

Stå opp, o helgener av Gud!
Riket venter lenge.
Bring inn dagen med Kristuslik kjærlighet
Og end nattens urett.

Løft høyt Kristi kors!
Trå der Hans føtter har trådt.
Ledet frem av Menneskesønnen,
Stå opp, o helgener av Gud!

La oss stå opp, som Guds folk, og begynne å gjøre slutt på de mindre tingene, med blikket vendt mot det som er der oppe, ikke mot jordiske ting. Ja, vi vil skille oss ut; vi vil bli kalt tåper og mye annet. Likevel vil vi igjen fange Guds oppmerksomhet og vekkelsens ild vil igjen brenne!

There is coming a day when all will be well.
The things that are bad will all be in hell.
But we must not forget that day has not come.
We are in a battle; we must still overcome.
The enemy rages, his time here is short.
He spreads all his lies, the truth to distort.
Sin in our lives, it is his great goal.
For he knows very well it will cost us our soul.
It need not be big; a small sin will do.
He’ll trick and deceive, each soul to pursue.
The darts of the wicked come from all sides.
When faced with God’s power, that devil—he hides!
When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

Ellie edged her chair closer to the grown-ups who were visiting in the kitchen. Grandpa, Grandma, and Aunt Lily had stopped by for a visit, and although she didn’t always understand the conversation, she loved to listen. She found that she learned a lot of things that way.

The topic this evening was about something related to church and that got her mind to thinking about singing during Sunday morning worship services. Although Ellie was only five years old, she very much loved to sing. She thought about the fact that her dear Grandpa was a song leader in their church and how much she liked when he led a song.

At Ellie’s church the song leaders all sat around a table near the center of the church. They took turns choosing a song and then leading it for the congregation. Ellie didn’t always know the songs that were chosen. They sang out of a little black hymnbook that had lots of songs with hard words and tunes she didn’t recognize. However, in the back of this little songbook was a section called “The Appendix” and here were hymns that were familiar to her and she was always pleased when a song was announced from that part of the book. Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight. When that particular song number was announced on a Sunday morning, she always felt a twinge of excitement. She would be able to help along with this song!

I wish we would sing that song again, thought Ellie. It’s been a long time since we have.

Then a sudden thought struck her. Why couldn’t she ask Grandpa to choose that song next Sunday?

Yes, I will ask him and see what he says about that idea, she smiled to herself. She decided to wait until her grandparents were ready to leave. She followed Grandpa out the door and as he walked across the porch, she quickly stepped up next to him. “Grandpa,” she asked. “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!” She felt suddenly shy at having asked such a question, and she ducked back toward the doorway of the house.

Grandpa smiled down at her. “I think I can do that. Is that a song you like?” His eyes twinkled at Ellie. “I’ll be happy to lead that one just for you.”

Ellie could scarcely wait for church the following Sunday. She would get to sing “her” song. Grandpa said he would choose it and she had no doubt he would do as he said.

Sunday morning, she waited eagerly for the song service to begin. The first and second songs were ones that were not familiar to her. Then came time for the third one. “Let’s sing number 8 in the Appendix,” announced the song leader. Ellie’s heart sang. They were going to sing her favorite song. Her grandpa had honored her request. Her eyes shone as she joined in the singing of the beautiful song. It was a lovely hymn that spoke of Jesus’ care as a Shepherd and a Friend, and how He would always keep His children close to Himself.

Later, after church was over and they were on their way home, Ellie remarked to her mother, “Grandpa chose that one song, just like I asked him to!”

Ellie’s mom looked a bit startled. “You asked him to lead a song today? When did you ask him?”

“Yes, I did. The other evening when they visited, I asked him if he could lead it today and he said he would. And he did!” Ellie said with delight.

Mom had a strange look on her face, and she was quiet for a moment.

“Did you know that Grandpas weren’t there today? At the last minute they decided to visit elsewhere this morning for church.” Mom smiled tenderly at her little daughter. “It seems that God knew what a little girl’s heart was desiring and He led another brother to choose the song you like so much. That’s so amazing, isn’t it?” Ellie nodded. To think that Grandpa wasn’t even at church today, and still they sang her favorite song anyway! It gave her such a special feeling to know that Jesus cared for her that much.

Today, Ellie is a grown-up woman and now has children of her own. Whenever she thinks about how Jesus cares for all His children, she especially remembers how God cared about one little, five-year-old girl and the song she loved so much. As her mother said, and still does, “Of course God cares. He loves all the little children of the world!”

Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us

Much we need Thy tender care.
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
For our use Thy folds prepare:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

We are Thine, do Thou befriend us,
Be the guardian of our way.
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
Seek us when we go astray:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

Thou hast promised to receive us,
Poor and sinful though we be.
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,

Ellie skjøv stolen sin nærmere de voksne som var på besøk på kjøkkenet. Bestefar, bestemor og tante Lily hadde kommet innom, og selv om hun ikke alltid forsto samtalen, elsket hun å lytte. Hun oppdaget at hun lærte mange ting på den måten.

Temaet denne kvelden handlet om noe som hadde med kirken å gjøre, og det fikk henne til å tenke på sang under søndagsgudstjenestene. Selv om Ellie bare var fem år gammel, elsket hun å synge. Hun tenkte på at kjære bestefar var sangleder i kirken deres, og hvor godt hun likte når han ledet en sang.

I Ellies kirke satt sanglederne alltid rundt et bord nær midten av kirkerommet. De valgte på tur en sang og ledet den for menigheten. Ellie visste ikke alltid hvilke sanger som ble valgt. De sang fra en liten svart salmebok som hadde mange sanger med vanskelige ord og melodier hun ikke kjente igjen. Men bakerst i denne lille sangboken var det en del kalt «Tillegg», og der var det salmer som var kjente for henne, og hun ble alltid glad når en sang ble kunngjort fra den delen av boken. Hennes favorittsang var «Frelser, lik en hyrde led oss», og selv om hun ennå ikke kunne lese, visste hun at den var nummer åtte. Når akkurat det sangnummeret ble kunngjort en søndagsmorgen, kjente hun alltid et stikk av begeistring. Hun ville kunne være med og hjelpe til med denne sangen!

Jeg skulle ønske vi sang den sangen igjen, tenkte Ellie. Det er lenge siden vi har gjort det.

Så slo en plutselig tanke henne. Hvorfor kunne hun ikke spørre bestefar om han kunne velge den sangen neste søndag?

Ja, jeg skal spørre ham og se hva han sier om den ideen, smilte hun for seg selv. Hun bestemte seg for å vente til besteforeldrene var klare til å dra. Hun fulgte etter bestefar ut døren, og mens han gikk over verandaen, trådte hun raskt opp ved siden av ham. «Bestefar,» spurte hun. «Tror du du kan lede sangen «Frelser, lik en hyrde led oss» neste søndag? Jeg skulle så gjerne likt å synge den igjen!» Hun ble plutselig sjenert etter å ha stilt et slikt spørsmål, og hun krympet seg tilbake mot husets døråpning.

Bestefar smilte ned til henne. «Jeg tror jeg kan gjøre det. Er det en sang du liker?» Øynene hans glitret mot Ellie. «Jeg stiller gjerne opp og leder den bare for deg.»

Ellie kunne knapt vente til kirken den påfølgende søndagen. Hun skulle få synge «sin» sang. Bestefar sa han ville velge den, og hun tvilte ikke på at han ville holde det han sa.

Søndagsmorgen ventet hun spent på at sangtjenesten skulle begynne. Den første og andre sangen var ikke kjente for henne. Så kom tiden for den tredje. «La oss synge nummer 8 i Tillegget,» kunngjorde sanglederen. Ellies hjerte sang. De skulle synge hennes favorittsang. Bestefar hadde innfridd hennes ønske. Øynene hennes lyste mens hun ble med i sangen av den vakre salmen. Det var en herlig salme som talte om Jesu omsorg som en hyrde og en venn, og hvordan Han alltid ville holde sine barn nær seg.

Senere, etter at kirken var over og de var på vei hjem, sa Ellie til moren sin: «Bestefar valgte den sangen, akkurat som jeg ba ham om!»

Ellies mor så noe overrasket ut. «Du ba ham lede en sang i dag? Når spurte du ham?»

«Ja, det gjorde jeg. Forleden kveld da de var på besøk, spurte jeg ham om han kunne lede den i dag, og han sa han ville. Og det gjorde han!» sa Ellie henrykt.

Moren hadde et underlig blikk i ansiktet, og hun var stille et øyeblikk.

«Visste du at besteforeldrene ikke var der i dag? I siste liten bestemte de seg for å besøke et annet sted denne morgenen for gudstjenesten.» Moren smilte ømt til sin lille datter. «Det ser ut til at Gud visste hva et lite jentes hjerte lengtet etter, og han ledet en annen bror til å velge sangen du liker så godt. Er ikke det helt forunderlig?» Ellie nikket. At bestefar ikke engang var i kirken i dag, og likevel sang de hennes favorittsang! Det ga henne en så spesiell følelse å vite at Jesus brydde seg så mye om henne.

I dag er Ellie en voksen kvinne og har nå egne barn. Når hun tenker på hvordan Jesus bryr seg om alle sine barn, husker hun spesielt hvordan Gud brydde seg om ei lita, fem år gammel jente og sangen hun elsket så høyt. Som moren hennes sa, og fortsatt sier, «Selvfølgelig bryr Gud seg. Han elsker alle verdens små barn!»

Hør, å hør oss når vi ber.

Du har lovet å ta imot oss,

Du har miskunn for å lindre oss,

Velsignede Jesus! velsignede Jesus!
La oss tidlig vende oss til deg.

La oss tidlig vende oss til deg.

La oss tidlig søke din gunst,

This is the first of a series of articles on “Discipleship.” Today, Jesus is continuing to call men and women to respond to the simple call, “Follow Me.” Jesus is calling each of us to personally “Follow Me.” In this series, we will explore the depth of this simple command of Jesus. Like the disciples, you will find yourself drawn to follow Jesus.

You may experience both exhilaration and apprehension. Exhilaration, as your journey of faith takes you to heights of love that you have never known. Apprehension, as your faith is tested in new and difficult ways.

There is an emptiness in every human heart that only Jesus can fill. There is a purity and beauty in the life of Jesus that resonates with those heart longings. As we walk with Jesus, we find ourselves being transformed. Old things pass away. All things become new. His life becomes our life. His desires become our desires.

Discipleship is incumbent on the believer. Believing in Jesus, repenting of our sins, and receiving the Lord Jesus into our heart are the first steps into a lifelong journey of faith. Discipleship is not an alternate means of salvation. Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free. Following Jesus is not a carnal attempt to merit eternal life. It is the love response of one who has discovered the source of life.

If you join us on this journey, you will discover that following Jesus will lead us into the valley of decision where we will find ourselves compelled to choose between a life of total surrender to Christ or a life of sin and pleasing self.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagine yourself in a ship with one of these brethren. The sun was rising on the eastern horizon. Anticipating another day of fishing the blue waters of the Galilee, you busy yourself with the daily tasks. Fishing has been your life. You are as much at home on the sea as you are in your cottage.

Another day, another catch of fish, and you should be able to keep the creditors at bay for another week. It’s the only life you have ever known. Your father was a fisherman. Your grandfather was a fisherman. It’s a comfortable life. It’s a familiar life.

This morning, as the waves are gently lapping the sandy shoreline, a man approaches. He’s not a total stranger. Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son. He astounds the local rabbi with his knowledge of the scriptures. His character is flawless; He is the friend of all and a stranger to none.

This man, Jesus (that is his name) is drawing near to your ship. As He draws near, He calls out in a rather cheerful voice, “Follow me.”

James looks at John, and together they look to their father Zebedee. His approving nod was all that they needed. Zebedee had worked with his two sons for many years. Perhaps he was hoping that time with the Nazarene would soften the temper of their abrasive characters.

“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” That’s what He called out to Peter and Andrew. They left their little boat full of nets, perhaps tethered to a stump by the shore. What was it about this Man that He could draw disciples after Him with a simple “Follow Me”? Maybe it was a deep longing in the heart of these disciples—a “hope” that following Jesus might fulfill.

Generations of Jewish men had been looking for The Messiah—The Promised One; He who would break the Roman yoke and restore Israel to her former freedom and glory. Jesus was the most promising revolutionary prospect of the day. He would need a following. He would need their help. Little did they realize that day as they dropped their nets and followed Jesus where that journey would lead them. Little did they know that if they followed this Man, they would never be the same.

As Peter, Andrew, James, and John joined with eight others to follow Jesus, they were walking away from the familiar, secure life of the fisherman. They may have thought that following Jesus would be an adventure. They may have thought that after a term of service to the Nazarene, they could return to their fishing boats. As a matter of fact, that is what they did.

After Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection, He made several appearances to His disciples. They had not yet received the Holy Spirit, and, in the midst of this great uncertainty, they could not resist the allure of the familiar. They decided to go fishing, but much to their consternation they had lost the touch. They fished all night and caught nothing. In the morning Jesus was standing on the shore. He told them to cast on the right side of the ship. They cast and were not able to pull in the nets due to the multitude of fish.

Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No. And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes –John 21:3-6.

Have you ever found yourself in a position where you have tried and tried and all your efforts are met with failure? You know what it is to “reach the end of my hoarded resources”. If that is where you find yourself, you are in a position to experience a miracle. God shows himself strong to those who acknowledge their weakness.

When you decide to follow Jesus, He will draw you into such an utter dependence upon Him that you will finally no longer trust in yourself. To become truly like Jesus is to realize with Paul …that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing…. Paul then continues the verse …for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not –Romans 7:18.

Discipleship will lead us into a total abandonment of ourselves to Christ. Just as the disciples could not have fathomed where following Jesus would lead them, neither can we. We make a faith choice. We choose to follow. We commit the details to our Master.

If you want to be like Jesus, you cannot look back. Jesus said: …No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62. Peter looked back. He said, “I go a fishing”. Disillusioned following the crucifixion and glorious resurrection, Peter chose to return to the lifestyle that was familiar to him. He went back to fishing and James and John went with him.

When Jesus appeared on the shore after their long night of fruitless toil, He prepared a fish fry for the weary disciples. As Peter sat munching on a charbroiled fish, Jesus turned to him and said, “Peter, do you love Me more than these?” How gently piercing are the words of Jesus.

Peter responded, “Yes Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.” We do not know how much time passed, but Jesus turned to him again, “Peter…” (actually He called him Simon) “Do you love Me?” Peter gave the same staid response. “Yes Lord, you know that I love you”. It was the right answer, but Jesus was interested in more than just a right answer, so He said to him again, “Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me?”

Peter finally began to feel that Jesus was asking for something more of him—something that pierced his soul through and through. He had begun following Jesus with the desire to receive from Him. Now Jesus is asking him to reciprocate that love.

Scenes of Caiaphas’ house came before him. He saw Jesus being brutally handled, falsely accused, and spat upon. He heard the angry shouting of the Sanhedrin as they called for Jesus’ death. And then there was that persistent young damsel that challenged him that he was one of Jesus’ disciples. He said to her, “I am not”. Three times he had denied knowing Jesus and now three times Jesus has challenged his love.

In anguish of heart Peter cried out, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee”. Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep”. From that day, Peter was a man with a calling, not only to know Christ for the purpose of receiving from him, but also to emulate him. Discipleship is more than merely knowing about Jesus. Discipleship is walking in his footsteps and identifying with Jesus in his ministry and in his sufferings—truly knowing Him.

Jesus is asking you today, “Do you love me?” We all know the right answer, “Yes, of course, I love Jesus.” Then “Love your neighbor” – “Serve the needy” – “Defer to your brother” – “Forgive the one that has offended you”.

Discipleship is very practical in that it moves us beyond the ideological and causes us to become the very hands and feet of Jesus to those around us.

If in your heart you are thinking, this doesn’t sound very appealing, I would encourage you to focus on the moment and the task at hand. Peter walked with Jesus for three and a half years before he received this call from Jesus. Jesus never calls us without equipping us, and He doesn’t equip us until He determines that we are ready. After the Day of Pentecost, Peter was called, he was prepared, and he was equipped. Then God used him mightily to establish the church.

I would like to call your attention to another attribute of discipleship that is sometimes misplaced. Discipleship is never intended to be drudgery. If you find following Jesus to be hard and toilsome, that is evidence that your love has not yet been perfected.

Jesus’ soul-piercing question to Peter was quite simple, “Do you love Me?” It was as if Jesus was testing Peter. [“I have a job for you, Peter, but a prerequisite for this job is your devoted love for Me.”] Discipleship is a love response to Jesus. Our love for Christ makes service a joy. Toil is pleasant and sacrifice is not a loss.

We can best understand this in the context of human relationships. If you are married and you truly love your husband or your wife, you do not even consider it a sacrifice to work for the mutual benefit of your marriage. In the same way, if we are truly in love with Jesus it is not considered toil to work for him. No sacrifice that we make for the kingdom of heaven is a loss.

I welcome you to join us as we explore the realities of discipleship. We will learn from Christ’s example of forgiveness. We will gain a greater understanding of what it means to walk by faith. Jesus taught us to not worry but to trust. He taught lessons on servant leadership and on cross bearing. There is so much to discover when we are walking with Jesus.

Expect to be changed. The teachings of Jesus are revolutionary in that they run counter to our human impulses. Purpose to allow the life of Christ to become your life and you will be amazed by what God will do for you.
