Dit is het eerste van een reeks artikelen over “discipelschap.” Vandaag roept Jezus nog steeds mannen en vrouwen op om te reageren op de eenvoudige oproep: “Volg Mij.” Jezus roept ieder van ons persoonlijk: “Volg Mij.” In deze reeks zullen we de diepte van dit eenvoudige gebod van Jezus onderzoeken. Net als de discipelen zul je je aangetrokken voelen om Jezus te volgen.

Je kunt zowel opwinding als bezorgdheid ervaren. Opwinding, omdat je geloofsreis je naar liefdeshoogten brengt die je nooit eerder gekend hebt. Bezorgdheid, omdat je geloof op nieuwe en moeilijke manieren wordt beproefd.

In elk menselijk hart is er een leegte die alleen Jezus kan vullen. Er is een zuiverheid en schoonheid in het leven van Jezus die resoneren met die hartverlangens. Terwijl we met Jezus wandelen, vinden we dat we worden getransformeerd. Oude dingen gaan voorbij. Alle dingen worden nieuw. Zijn leven wordt ons leven. Zijn verlangens worden onze verlangens.

Discipelschap is een plicht voor de gelovige. Geloven in Jezus, berouw over onze zonden en de Heere Jezus in ons hart ontvangen zijn de eerste stappen op een levenslange geloofsreis. Discipelschap is geen alternatief middel tot redding. Jezus volgen is de reactie van een ziel die vrij is gesteld. Jezus volgen is geen vleselijke poging om het eeuwige leven te verdienen. Het is de liefdesreactie van iemand die de bron van het leven heeft ontdekt.

Als je met ons meegaat op deze reis, zul je ontdekken dat Jezus volgen ons zal leiden naar het dal van besluit waarin we ons gedwongen zullen voelen te kiezen tussen een leven van totale overgave aan Christus of een leven van zonde en het behagen van zichzelf.

En Jezus, wandelende langs de zee van Galilea, zag twee broeders, Simon, genoemd Petrus, en Andreas, zijn broeder, die een net in de zee wierpen; want zij waren vissers. En Hij zegt tegen hen: Volg Mij, en Ik zal u vissers van mensen maken. En zij lieten meteen hun netten en volgden Hem. En van daar gaande zag Hij andere twee broeders, Jakobus, de zoon van Zebedeüs, en Johannes, zijn broeder, in een boot met hun vader Zebedeüs, die hun netten herstelden; en Hij riep hen. En zij lieten onmiddellijk de boot en hun vader en volgden Hem –Mattheüs 4:18-22.

Stel je voor dat je in een boot zit met een van deze broeders. De zon rees aan de oostelijke horizon. Verwachtend een nieuwe dag vissen op het blauwe water van de Galilea, houd je je bezig met de dagelijkse taken. Vissen is je leven geweest. Je voelt je op zee even thuis als in je huisje.

Weer een dag, weer een vangst, en je zou de schuldeisers nog een week op afstand moeten kunnen houden. Het is het enige leven dat je ooit hebt gekend. Je vader was visser. Je grootvader was visser. Het is een comfortabel leven. Het is een vertrouwd leven.

Die ochtend, terwijl de golven zachtjes tegen het zandige strand klotsten, naderde een man. Hij is geen totale vreemdeling. Iedereen kent de zoon van Maria. Iedereen heeft een mening over de zoon van Maria. Hij verbaast de plaatselijke rabbijnen met zijn kennis van de Schriften. Zijn karakter is onberispelijk; Hij is ieders vriend en voor niemand een vreemde.

Deze man, Jezus (dat is zijn naam) nadert je boot. Terwijl Hij nadert, roept Hij in een tamelijk opgewekte stem: “Volg Mij.”

Jakobus kijkt naar Johannes, en samen kijken zij naar hun vader Zebedeüs. Zijn instemmende knikje was alles wat zij nodig hadden. Zebedeüs had vele jaren met zijn twee zonen gewerkt. Misschien hoopte hij dat tijd met de Nazarener het temperament van hun schurende karakters zou verzachten.

“Volg Mij, en Ik zal u vissers van mensen maken.” Dat riep Hij naar Petrus en Andreas. Zij lieten hun kleine boot vol netten achter, misschien vastgemaakt aan een boomstronk bij de oever. Wat was het toch met deze Man dat Hij discipelen achter Zich aan kon trekken met een eenvoudig “Volg Mij”? Misschien was het een diepe hunkering in het hart van deze discipelen—een “hoop” dat Jezus volgen mogelijk zou vervullen.

Generaties Joodse mannen hadden naar De Messias gezocht—De Beloofde; Degene die het Romeinse juk zou breken en Israël zou herstellen tot haar vroegere vrijheid en glorie. Jezus was het meest veelbelovende revolutionaire vooruitzicht van die tijd. Hij zou een gevolg nodig hebben. Hij zou hun hulp nodig hebben. Weinigen realiseerden zich die dag toen zij hun netten neerlegden en Jezus volgden waar die reis hen zou brengen. Ze hadden geen idee dat als ze deze Man zouden volgen, ze nooit meer hetzelfde zouden zijn.

Toen Petrus, Andreas, Jakobus en Johannes zich met acht anderen voegden om Jezus te volgen, liepen zij weg van het vertrouwde, veilige leven van de visser. Zij dachten misschien dat Jezus volgen een avontuur zou zijn. Zij dachten misschien dat zij na een termijn van dienst aan de Nazarener konden terugkeren naar hun vissersboten. In feite is dat wat zij deden.

Na Jezus’ kruisiging en opstanding maakte Hij meerdere verschijningen aan Zijn discipelen. Zij hadden de Heilige Geest nog niet ontvangen en, temidden van deze grote onzekerheid, konden zij de verleiding van het vertrouwde niet weerstaan. Zij besloten weer te gaan vissen, maar tot hun grote ontsteltenis waren zij de greep kwijtgeraakt. Zij visten de hele nacht en vingen niets. In de morgen stond Jezus op de oever. Hij zei hun aan de rechterzijde van de boot uit te werpen. Zij wierpen uit en konden de netten niet binnenhalen vanwege de hoeveelheid vis.

Simon Petrus zegt tegen hen: Ik ga vissen. Zij zeggen tegen hem: Wij gaan ook met u mee. Zij gingen uit en gingen onmiddellijk in de boot; en die nacht vingen zij niets. Maar toen het morgen was gekomen, stond Jezus op de oever; maar de discipelen wisten niet dat het Jezus was. Toen zegt Jezus tegen hen: Kinderen, hebt gij geen spijs? Zij antwoordden Hem: Nee. En Hij zei tot hen: Werpt het net aan de rechterzijde van de boot en gij zult vinden. Zij wierpen daarom uit en nu konden zij het niet binnenhalen vanwege de menigte vissen –Johannes 21:3-6.

Heb je je ooit in een situatie bevonden waarin je en blijf proberen en al je inspanningen op mislukking stuiten? Je weet wat het is om “het einde van mijn opgespaarde middelen te bereiken”. Als dat is waar je jezelf bevindt, ben je in een positie om een wonder te ervaren. God toont Zich sterk aan hen die hun zwakheid erkennen.

Wanneer je besluit Jezus te volgen, zal Hij je in zo’n volledige afhankelijkheid van Hem trekken dat je uiteindelijk niet langer op jezelf zult vertrouwen. Waarlijk Jezus gelijk worden is met Paulus te beseffen …dat in mij (dat is, in mijn vlees) geen goed woont… Paulus vervolgt vervolgens de verzen met: …want het goede te willen is bij mij aanwezig; hoe het goede te volbrengen vind ik echter niet –Romeinen 7:18.

Discipelschap zal ons leiden tot een totale prijsgeving van onszelf aan Christus. Net zoals de discipelen zich niet konden voorstellen waar Jezus volgen hen zou brengen, zo ook wij niet. Wij maken een geloofskeuze. Wij kiezen om te volgen. Wij vertrouwen de details aan onze Meester toe.

Als je op Jezus wilt lijken, kun je niet achterom kijken. Jezus zei: …Niemand die zijn hand aan de ploeg slaat en ziet achterom is geschikt voor het Koninkrijk van God –Lucas 9:62. Petrus keek achterom. Hij zei: “Ik ga vissen”. Teleurgesteld na de kruisiging en glorieuze opstanding, koos Petrus terug te keren naar de levensstijl die hem vertrouwd was. Hij ging terug naar het vissen en Jakobus en Johannes gingen met hem mee.

Toen Jezus aan de oever verscheen na hun lange nacht van vruchteloze arbeid, bereidde Hij een vismaaltijd voor de vermoeide discipelen. Terwijl Petrus zat te knagen aan een geroosterde vis, wendde Jezus Zich tot hem en zei: “Petrus, houd je meer van Mij dan deze?” Hoe zacht en tegelijk doordringend zijn de woorden van Jezus.

Petrus antwoordde: “Ja Heer, Gij weet dat ik U liefheb.” Jezus zei: “Weid Mijn lammeren.” We weten niet hoeveel tijd er verstreek, maar Jezus wendde Zich opnieuw tot hem: “Petrus…” (eigenlijk noemde Hij hem Simon) “Houdt gij Mij lief?” Petrus gaf hetzelfde keurige antwoord: “Ja Heer, Gij weet dat ik U liefheb.” Het was het juiste antwoord, maar Jezus was geïnteresseerd in meer dan alleen een juist antwoord, dus Hij zei opnieuw: “Simon, zoon van Jonas, hebt gij Mij lief?”

Petrus begon eindelijk te voelen dat Jezus iets meer van hem vroeg—iets dat zijn ziel door en door doorboorde. Hij was Jezus gaan volgen met het verlangen iets van Hem te ontvangen. Nu vraagt Jezus hem die liefde te beantwoorden.

Tafereeltjes van het huis van Kajafas kwamen voor zijn geest. Hij zag hoe Jezus ruw werd behandeld, onterecht beschuldigd en bespuugd. Hij hoorde het boze geschreeuw van het Sanhedrin toen zij om Jezus’ dood riepen. En toen was daar dat volhardende jonge meisje dat hem uitdaagde dat hij een van Jezus’ discipelen was. Hij zei tegen haar: “Ik ken Hem niet.” Drie keer had hij ontkend Jezus te kennen en nu had Jezus hem driemaal uitgedaagd over zijn liefde.

In diepe smart riep Petrus uit: “Heer, Gij weet alles; Gij weet dat ik U liefheb.” Jezus zei tegen hem: “Weid Mijn schapen.” Vanaf die dag was Petrus een man met een roeping, niet alleen om Christus te kennen met het doel iets van Hem te ontvangen, maar ook om Hem na te bootsen. Discipelschap is meer dan slechts weten over Jezus. Discipelschap is wandelen in Zijn voetstappen en je identificeren met Jezus in Zijn bediening en in Zijn lijden—Hem werkelijk kennen.

Jezus vraagt jou vandaag: “Houdt gij van Mij?” We kennen allemaal het juiste antwoord: “Ja, natuurlijk, ik houd van Jezus.” Dan “Heb uw naaste lief” – “Dien de behoeftigen” – “Geef voorrang aan uw broeder” – “Vergeef degene die u heeft beledigd.”

Discipelschap is zeer praktisch in die zin dat het ons voorbij het ideologische brengt en ons de handen en voeten van Jezus maakt voor de mensen om ons heen.

Als je in je hart denkt, dit klinkt niet erg aantrekkelijk, zou ik je willen aanmoedigen je te richten op het moment en de taak die voor je ligt. Petrus liep drieënhalf jaar met Jezus voordat hij deze oproep van Jezus ontving. Jezus roept ons nooit zonder ons uit te rusten, en Hij rust ons niet uit totdat Hij bepaalt dat wij er klaar voor zijn. Na de dag van Pinksteren werd Petrus geroepen, voorbereid en toegerust. Toen gebruikte God hem machtiglijk om de kerk te stichten.

Ik wil je attent maken op nog een kenmerk van discipelschap dat soms verkeerd wordt geplaatst. Discipelschap is nooit bedoeld als sleur. Als je merkt dat Jezus volgen zwaar en moeizaam is, is dat een bewijs dat je liefde nog niet volmaakt is.

Jezus’ ziel-doorborende vraag aan Petrus was heel eenvoudig: “Houdt gij van Mij?” Het was alsof Jezus Petrus testte. [“Ik heb een taak voor u, Petrus, maar een vereiste voor deze taak is uw toegewijde liefde voor Mij.”] Discipelschap is een liefdesreactie op Jezus. Onze liefde voor Christus maakt dienst een vreugde. Arbeid is aangenaam en opoffering is geen verlies.

We kunnen dit het beste begrijpen in de context van menselijke relaties. Als je getrouwd bent en je houdt echt van je man of vrouw, overweeg je het niet eens als een offer om te werken voor het wederzijds welzijn van je huwelijk. Op dezelfde manier, als wij echt verliefd zijn op Jezus, wordt het niet als arbeid gezien om voor Hem te werken. Geen enkele opoffering die wij brengen voor het koninkrijk der hemelen is een verlies.

Ik nodig je uit met ons mee te gaan terwijl we de realiteiten van discipelschap onderzoeken. We zullen leren van Christus’ voorbeeld van vergeving. We zullen een groter begrip verkrijgen van wat het betekent te wandelen door geloof. Jezus leerde ons niet te zorgen maar te vertrouwen. Hij gaf lessen over dienend leiderschap en over het dragen van het kruis. Er valt zoveel te ontdekken wanneer we met Jezus wandelen.

Verwacht veranderd te worden. De leer van Jezus is revolutionair omdat zij ingaat tegen onze menselijke impulsen. Stel je ten doel het leven van Christus jouw leven te laten worden en je zult verbaasd zijn over wat God voor je zal doen.

There is coming a day when all will be well.
The things that are bad will all be in hell.
But we must not forget that day has not come.
We are in a battle; we must still overcome.
The enemy rages, his time here is short.
He spreads all his lies, the truth to distort.
Sin in our lives, it is his great goal.
For he knows very well it will cost us our soul.
It need not be big; a small sin will do.
He’ll trick and deceive, each soul to pursue.
The darts of the wicked come from all sides.
When faced with God’s power, that devil—he hides!
When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

Virá um dia em que tudo estará bem.
As coisas más ficarão todas no inferno.
Mas não devemos esquecer que esse dia não veio ainda.
Estamos numa batalha; ainda precisamos vencer.
O inimigo enfurece-se, seu tempo aqui é curto.
Espalha todas as suas mentiras, para distorcer a verdade.
O pecado em nossas vidas é o seu grande alvo.
Pois sabe muito bem que isso nos custará a alma.
Não precisa ser grande; um pequeno pecado basta.
Ele enganará e iludirá, perseguindo cada alma.
As setas dos ímpios vêm de todos os lados.
Quando defronte ao poder de Deus, esse diabo—ele se põe a ocultar!
Quando Deus está conosco, ele não pode avançar!
Quando Deus está conosco, o pecado não tem chance!
Pois os olhos do Senhor procuram de um lado ao outro,
Para encontrar um perfeito, Seu poder então mostrará!
Cessemos as coisas menores e olhemos muito além.
Tomemos o poder de Deus! É tempo de responder!

It’s been said that in the 1500s, after baptism, the Anabaptists lived an average of only 27 days. They were hunted and killed. They realized one thing—serving Christ would most certainly cost them everything. They forsook the comforts of easy living; they forsook it all. It could also have been a similar situation when Jesus walked on the earth, or shortly after He was killed.

…and he turned, and said unto them, If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple. For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish. Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple –Luke 14:25-33.

Jesus clearly asked His disciples to count the cost. And they must have counted the cost, for they faithfully gave all, including their lives, for Christ’s Kingdom. They realized they could have had the good things in this life; however, they also realized it would cost them the good things in the next.

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution –2 Timothy 3:12. If we look at the promises which Jesus gave us in His Word about persecution, and then compare them with the lives of Jesus’ followers today, we might be confused. And rightfully so.

He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked –1 John 2:6. Jesus says we should walk as He walked, He also tells us that we need to follow Him.

How did He walk? We know that Jesus had no place to lay His head—this was how He wanted it. We know that Jesus could have chosen to live where and how He wanted. He was, in fact, in control of the whole world, yet He was despised and rejected by the world and its system. When He spoke, people wanted to lay their hands on Him; they wanted to kill Him. He was not a popular person; He had few friends. In reality, He didn’t fit in, and He didn’t last long. Three years after His ministry began, He was killed. …He was numbered with the transgressors –Mark 15:28.

What about His followers today? Are they walking how He walked? And if not, why not?

We read about the children of Israel going through the wilderness. They fought and overtook the cities in their paths, killing all in the process. We read many accounts about how God instructed the children of Israel to kill all of the enemy, even the women and children. The following is one such account of many.

So the LORD our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining. And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many. And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city –Deuteronomy 3:3-6.

We read accounts like this in scripture, and it can cause us to cringe. It is almost as if life itself was not important. Even in the New Testament, death doesn’t seem to be that big of a deal. People lived and people died.

The first week after we moved to Haiti, I was driving through the city. Suddenly, right in front of me I saw a man lying in the street. Blood ran down the road and pooled in a low spot—he was dead. I was shocked. But what shocked me the most was that no one seemed to notice. People by the hundreds busily walked around him, not even looking at the man—no one cared.

Over the next six years we saw many dead or dying people—it became a normal scene.

If that was how it was back in the Bible times, and it is still how it is today in many countries of the world, maybe we are the ones that are out of the norm? Maybe we esteem life higher than God does. Maybe we are among those that Jesus spoke of when He said—He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal –John 12:25.

In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:19. We were created out of the dust, and after a few short years, we return to the very same dust.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –James 4:14. The Bible also calls our lives a vapor.

We all know what happens after that—the judgment, then eternity. So why do we care so much about this life? Maybe it is an American problem or a western problem.

It is obvious that Americans are looked upon as ‘more valuable’ than most other nationalities. If you are an American in a developing country, you are heralded as a king. If something happens to an American, it is quickly headline news. I once stood over the bodies of two murdered men. One of their close friends stood by, so I asked him how he was doing. He shrugged and said, “This is life”.

So why does life mean so much to us Americans? The answer is simple. We can obtain almost anything we want; money is easy to get, and we can live how we want. We can live in pleasure every day. We go to the store and buy what we want, when we want—we have it our way. This is just how it is; for most of us it is all we have ever known—the life of plenty. So how does this affect us?

This type of living makes it especially hard to ‘give all’ for Christ. It makes it difficult to obey Jesus’ command to …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15. It makes it difficult to say with the Apostle Paul, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. In reality, it makes it difficult to be a Christian.

When Jesus said… For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25, what did He mean? Could it mean literally just what it says: that when you fall in love with your own life, you cannot effectively follow Christ, so that in the end you will actually lose your life?

Can you go to the lost and forsake the comforts of this life if it’s those comforts that you love and live for? It’s not likely. What we have is “Americanized” Christians that will only go to the mission field if they can take their comforts with them. This produces rich, comfortable missionaries who, despite their best efforts, can’t win the lost, rather they make them jealous. Can we go into the cities and preach the gospel to the lost like so many before us have? Can we take time to teach and disciple the tens of thousands who are seeking? If we love our lives, we probably will not, since there is too much to lose and it’s a waste of good talent and opportunity. God help us.

When we are living to please the flesh and we have our lives figured out, it is hard for God to use us. We are puffed up. We tend to believe that God has blessed us because of all our possessions and our status in life; but isn’t this the prosperity gospel? What if that changed? Would we still consider ourselves to be blessed? Is it God or our own doing that causes us to be joyful? What if we found ourselves in John the Baptist’s shoes? Or the Apostle Paul’s? If we would be sitting in prison for doing nothing wrong, would our joy remain? It should if the Holy Spirit is living and working in our hearts. The Bible says that we can suffer joyfully!

Years ago, a coworker of mine was a happy fellow. He had a nice life. There was one problem—he did not believe there was a God. We would talk day after day. He would constantly tell me how happy he was and that one didn’t need to be a Christian to be happy. He would talk about his nice life, all that he possessed, his good job, his nice family. Interestingly enough, he truly did seem happy.

I would tell him that true happiness didn’t come from the things that we possess or the position that we find ourselves in, but he would just disagree. He also proclaimed that he lived a better life than most Christians that he knew. He also said he didn’t get angry like most Christians and could control himself. I tried to convince him that he was deceived. At times I would think I was getting somewhere with him, then later it would seem I was far from reaching him. One day he soberly admitted that I seemed to be different that most Christians he had known in the past, but that still wasn’t enough.

I left that job and lost contact with him. Recently, I ran into another one of my former coworkers. I quickly thought of my friend and asked how he was doing. He looked at me strangely and then shocked me to my core as he said, “He committed suicide”.

The devil wants us to love our life—it’s that simple. When we love our life, we focus on it, we cherish it. The last thing we want to do is lose our life, even if it is for something eternal.

When I was in the Marines, they would constantly remind us that our lives were not number one; our country was. There are many young men who put their country first. Many have gone and given their all; many have died.

In World War 2, the Japanese would try to sneak up to a fox hole housing soldiers and throw in a grenade. Many times, it didn’t end like the Japanese wanted, because someone would jump on the grenade, absorbing the explosion. Thousands gave their lives to save their friends and defend their country. But be sure, if their priorities were not in order (of country first before themselves), they would not have done so.

If someone today, in America, would risk their life for the sake of the gospel, he would be labeled as foolish, reckless, and immature. But what do we say about so many before us—the ones that gave their lives while standing for the same things that we say we believe today? And what about the thousands today who are putting their lives on the line in other countries—are they foolish? Let’s look at a very obvious example in Acts.

And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus. And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem. Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. –Acts 21:10-13.

What would we think of Paul’s actions today? Paul went to Jerusalem and was quickly taken, beaten, and put in prison. It was the beginning of the end for our dear brother. He was moved from prison to prison and eventually ended up in Rome where he was beheaded. What do you think the ones that tried to persuade him to not go to Jerusalem thought? Do you think they called him a fool? Did they shake their heads and say, “I told him not to go!”?

We cannot know for sure. However, I am sure that Paul was simply putting the kingdom of Christ first; his life did not matter. He was obeying God, and God had told him to go.

When we love our lives, it is very difficult to be an effective disciple of the Lord Jesus. We end up forsaking God’s calling and then we are stuck trying to live the Christian life alone, and without God—no spiritual help from above, causing us to fall way short of the mark.

It’s ironic that only when we forsake all, including our lives, will we find true peace and purpose for our lives. And when we love our lives, that is when we will lose them.

Rise up, O saints of God!
Have done with lesser things.
Give heart and soul and mind and strength
To serve the King of kings.

Rise up, O saints of God!
The kingdom tarries long.
Bring in the day of Christlike love
And end the night of wrong.

Lift high the cross of Christ!
Tread where His feet have trod.
Led onward by the Son of Man,
Rise up, O saints of God!

Let us rise up, as God’s people, and begin to be done with lesser things, with our gaze on things above, not on the things of this earth. Yes, we will stand out; we will be labeled fools and many other things. However, we will once again catch God’s attention and the fires of revival will once again burn!

1500년대에 침례를 받은 후 아나뱁티스트들이 평균 겨우 27일만 살았다고도 한다. 그들은 사냥당해 죽임을 당했다. 그들은 한 가지를 깨달았다—그리스도를 섬기는 일은 분명히 그들에게 모든 것을 요구할 것이라는 사실을. 그들은 편안한 안락함을 버렸다; 그들은 모든 것을 버렸다. 예수께서 이 땅에 계실 때나 그가 죽임을 당한 직후에 비슷한 상황이었을 수도 있다.

…그리고 예수께서 돌아서서 그들에게 이르시되 누구든지 나를 따라오려거든 아버지와 어머니와 아내와 자녀와 형제와 자매까지도, 심지어 자기 목숨까지도 미워하지 아니하면 능히 내 제자가 되지 못하리라. 또 누구든지 자기 십자가를 지고 나를 따르지 아니하면 능히 내 제자가 되지 못하리라. 어느 사람이 탑을 세우려 할진대 앉아서 먼저 그 비용을 헤아리지 아니하겠느냐 곧 그가 마무리할 능력이 있나 보려 함이라. 혹시 기초를 놓고 능히 마무리하지 못하면 보는 사람들이 다 비웃어 이르되 이 사람이 건축을 시작하고 능히 마치지 못하였다 하리라. 혹은 어떤 임금이 다른 임금과 싸우려 할진대 만일 만 명으로 와서 그가 이만 명과 당할 수 있는가 앉아 상의하지 아니하겠느냐. 또는 저 임금이 아직 멀리 있을 때 사신을 보내어 평화의 조건을 구하리라. 이와 같이 너희 중에 누구든지 자기가 가진 것을 다 버리지 아니하면 능히 내 제자가 되지 못하리라 –누가복음 14:25-33.

예수님은 분명히 그의 제자들에게 대가를 계산해 보라고 요청하셨다. 그리고 그들은 분명 대가를 계산했을 것이다. 왜냐하면 그들은 성실하게 모든 것, 심지어 자신의 목숨까지도 그리스도의 왕국을 위해 바쳤기 때문이다. 그들은 이 생에서 좋은 것들을 가질 수 있었음을 알았지만, 동시에 다음 생에서 좋은 것들을 잃게 될 것임을 알았다.

그리스도 예수 안에서 경건하게 살고자 하는 자는 다 핍박을 받으리라 –디모데후서 3:12. 예수께서 그의 말씀에서 우리에게 핍박에 대해 주신 약속들을 살펴보고, 그것을 오늘날 예수의 추종자들의 삶과 비교하면 우리는 혼란스러울 수 있다. 그리고 그럴 만도 하다.

자기 자신이 그 안에 거한다고 말하는 자는 또 자기 자신도 그가 행한 것 같이 행할지니라 –요한일서 2:6. 예수님은 우리가 그가 행하신 것과 같이 행해야 한다고 말씀하시며, 또한 우리에게 그를 따르라고 말씀하신다.

그는 어떻게 걸으셨는가? 우리는 예수께서 누일 곳이 없으셨다는 것을 안다—그것이 그가 원하신 방식이었다. 우리는 예수께서 원하시면 어디에서든 어떻게든 살 수 있었음을 안다. 사실 그는 온 세상을 다스리실 수 있었지만, 그는 세상과 그 체제에게 경멸과 거절을 당하셨다. 그가 말씀하실 때 사람들은 그를 붙잡아 죽이려고 했다. 그는 인기 많은 사람이 아니었다; 친구도 적었다. 실상 그는 어울리지 못했고 오래 머무르지 못했다. 그의 사역이 시작된 지 삼 년 만에 그는 죽임을 당했다. …그가 죄인들과 함께 수를 헤아림을 받았더라 –마가복음 15:28.

오늘 그의 추종자들은 어떠한가? 그들은 그가 걸으신 대로 걷고 있는가? 그렇지 않다면 왜 그렇지 않은가?

우리는 이스라엘 자손들이 광야를 지나는 이야기를 읽는다. 그들은 길에 있는 성들을 싸워 점령하며 그 과정에서 모두를 죽였다. 우리는 하나님께서 이스라엘 자손들에게 적의 남자와 여자와 어린아이까지 다 죽이라고 지시하신 많은 기록을 읽는다. 다음은 그러한 많은 기록 중 하나이다.

여호와 우리 하나님이 또 바산 왕 옥과 그의 모든 백성을 우리 손에 넘기셨으니 우리가 그를 물리쳐 조금도 남기지 아니하였더라 그 때에 우리가 그의 모든 성읍을 취하였으니 우리가 취하지 아니한 성읍이 없었으니 육십 성읍이요 온 아르고브 지방, 바산의 옥의 나라의 모든 성들이었더라 이 모든 성들이 높은 성벽과 문 및 성문방으로 둘러쌓였고 성 밖에는 성읍들이 매우 많았더라 우리가 그들을 실로 왕 헤스본의 싯온에게 행한 것같이 그 성읍마다 사람과 여자와 아이를 쓸어 멸하였더라 –신명기 3:3-6.

우리는 성경에서 이러한 기록들을 읽고 몸서리를 칠 수 있다. 마치 생명 자체가 중요하지 않은 것처럼 보이기도 한다. 신약에서도 죽음은 그리 큰 문제가 아닌 것처럼 보인다. 사람이 살고 사람이 죽었다.

내가 아이티로 이사한 첫 주에 도시를 운전하고 있었다. 갑자기 내 앞에 한 남자가 길바닥에 누워 있는 것을 보았다. 피가 길에 흘러 저지대에 고여 있었다—그는 죽어 있었다. 나는 충격을 받았다. 그러나 나를 가장 놀라게 한 것은 아무도 신경 쓰지 않는 듯 보였다는 것이다. 수백 명의 사람들이 바쁘게 그를 둘러 지나가며 한 번도 그 남자를 쳐다보지 않았다—아무도 개의치 않았다.

그 후 6년 동안 우리는 많은 죽거나 죽어가는 사람들을 보았다—그것은 일상이 되었다.

만약 성경 시대에 그런 식이었고 오늘날에도 세계의 많은 나라에서 여전하다면, 어쩌면 우리가 정상에서 벗어난 존재일지도 모른다? 어쩌면 우리는 하나님보다 생명을 더 귀히 여기는지도 모른다. 어쩌면 우리는 예수께서 말씀하신 그들 중 하나일 것이다—자기 목숨을 사랑하는 자는 잃을 것이요 이 세상에서 자기 목숨을 미워하는 자는 영생을 보전하리라 –요한복음 12:25.

네가 수고한 댓가로 식물을 먹을 것이며 네 얼굴의 땀으로 너는 떡을 먹을 것이니 네가 흙으로 돌아갈 때까지니라 그가 거기서 취함을 입었으므로 흙이니 흙으로 돌아가리라 –창세기 3:19. 우리는 흙으로 창조되었고, 몇 년 후 우리는 같은 흙으로 돌아간다.

너희가 내일 일을 알지 못하니라 너희 생명이 무엇이냐 너희는 잠시까지 보이다가 없어지는 안개니라 –야고보서 4:14. 성경은 또한 우리의 생명을 안개라고 부른다.

우리는 모두 그 다음에 무슨 일이 일어나는지 안다—심판이 있고 그 다음에 영원이 있다. 그렇다면 왜 우리는 이 삶을 이토록 중요하게 여기는가? 아마도 이것은 미국의 문제이거나 서구의 문제일 것이다.

미국인들이 다른 대부분의 민족보다 ‘더 가치 있게’ 여겨지는 것은 분명하다. 개발도상국에서 미국인이라면 왕처럼 추대된다. 미국인에게 무슨 일이 생기면, 곧바로 헤드라인 뉴스가 된다. 한때 나는 두 명의 살해된 남자의 시신 위에 서 있었다. 그들의 친한 친구 한 명이 옆에 서 있기에 나는 그가 어떠냐고 물었다. 그는 어깨를 으쓱하며 말했다. “이게 삶입니다.”

그렇다면 왜 생명이 우리 미국인들에게 이토록 중요한가? 답은 간단하다. 우리는 거의 원하는 것을 무엇이든 얻을 수 있다; 돈을 벌기 쉽고 우리가 원하면 원하는 방식으로 살 수 있다. 우리는 매일 쾌락 속에서 살 수 있다. 우리는 가게에 가서 원할 때 원하는 것을 산다—우리는 우리 방식대로 산다. 대부분의 우리에게 이것이 전부였다—풍요의 삶. 이것이 우리에게 어떤 영향을 미치는가?

이러한 삶은 그리스도를 위해 ‘모든 것을 바치는 것’을 특히 어렵게 만든다. 이것은 예수의 명령인 …너희는 온 천하에 다니며 만민에게 복음을 전파하라 –마가복음 16:15.를 순종하기 어렵게 한다. 또한 사도 바울처럼 말하기 어렵게 한다—내게 사는 것이 그리스도요 죽는 것은 유익하니라 –빌립보서 1:21. 실제로 이것은 기독교인이 되기 어렵게 만든다.

예수께서 말씀하시되… 자기 목숨을 구하는 자는 잃을 것이요 내 목숨을 위하여 잃는 자는 얻으리라 –마태복음 16:25 하셨을 때, 무슨 뜻이었는가? 글자 그대로 그 말만을 뜻할 수 있는가: 자기 자신의 삶을 사랑하게 되면 효과적으로 그리스도를 따를 수 없으므로 결국 실제로 그의 삶을 잃게 된다는 것인가?

잃어버린 자들에게 가서 이 생의 안락함을 버릴 수 있는가, 만약 그 안락함이 당신이 사랑하고 사는 것이라면? 그럴 가능성은 낮다. 우리가 가진 것은 “미국화된” 기독교인들인데, 그들은 자기 편안함을 함께 가져갈 수 있을 때만 선교지에 갈 것이다. 이것은 부유하고 안락한 선교사들을 낳는데, 그들은 최선의 노력에도 불구하고 잃은 자를 얻지 못하고 오히려 그들을 질투하게 만든다. 우리는 많은 선배들처럼 도시로 가서 잃은 자들에게 복음을 전할 수 있는가? 수만 명의 구직자들에게 가르치고 제자 삼을 시간을 낼 수 있는가? 만약 우리가 우리의 삶을 사랑한다면, 아마도 그러지 못할 것이다. 잃을 것이 너무 많고 그것은 좋은 재능과 기회를 낭비하는 것처럼 보이기 때문이다. 하나님이여 도우소서.

육체를 기쁘게 하며 삶을 계획해 놓고 살 때 하나님이 우리를 사용하시기 어렵다. 우리는 교만해진다. 우리는 하나님께서 모든 소유와 사회적 지위 때문에 우리를 축복하셨다고 믿는 경향이 있다; 그러나 이것이 번영 복음이 아닌가? 만약 그것이 바뀐다면 우리는 여전히 우리를 복되다고 여길 것인가? 우리를 기쁘게 하는 것이 하나님인가 아니면 우리의 처지인가? 만약 우리가 세례 요한의 처지에 놓이거나 사도 바울의 처지에 놓인다면 어떠할까? 잘못한 일도 없이 옥에 갇힐 상황이 온다면 우리의 기쁨은 유지될 것인가? 성령께서 우리의 마음 안에서 살아 역사하신다면 그래야 마땅하다. 성경은 우리가 기쁘게 고난을 당할 수 있다고 말한다!

수년 전, 내 직장 동료 중 한 사람은 행복한 사람이었다. 그는 좋은 삶을 살았다. 단 하나의 문제가 있었으니—그는 하나님이 없다고 믿었다. 우리는 날마다 이야기했다. 그는 끊임없이 자신이 얼마나 행복한지, 행복하기 위해 기독교인이 될 필요가 없다고 말하곤 했다. 그는 자신의 좋은 삶, 가진 것들, 좋은 직장, 좋은 가정에 대해 이야기했다. 흥미롭게도 그는 정말로 행복해 보였다.

나는 참된 행복이 우리가 소유한 것이나 우리가 처한 지위에서 오지 않는다고 말하곤 했지만, 그는 동의하지 않았다. 그는 또한 자신이 아는 대부분의 기독교인보다 더 나은 삶을 살고 있다고 주장했다. 그는 또한 자신은 대부분의 기독교인들처럼 화를 내지 않으며 자신을 제어할 수 있다고 말했다. 나는 그가 속아 있다고 설득하려 애썼다. 때때로 나는 그에게 다가가는 것 같았지만, 나중에는 그에게서 멀어진 것처럼 보였다. 어느 날 그는 진지하게 인정하되 내가 과거에 알고 있던 대부분의 기독교인들과 달라 보였지만 그럼에도 그것만으로는 충분치 않다고 말했다.

나는 그 직장을 떠나 연락이 끊겼다. 최근에 나는 다른 전 동료를 우연히 만났다. 나는 그 친구가 생각나 그가 어떻게 지내는지 물었다. 그는 나를 이상하게 쳐다보다가 내 가슴을 철렁 내려앉게 하며 말했다. “그가 자살했어요.”

마귀는 우리가 삶을 사랑하도록 원한다—그것이 단순한 진리이다. 우리가 삶을 사랑할 때 우리는 삶에 초점을 맞추고, 그것을 소중히 여긴다. 우리가 잃고 싶어 하지 않는 것이 마지막일 것이다, 심지어 그것이 영원한 무언가를 위한 것일지라도.

내가 해병대에 있을 때, 그들은 끊임없이 우리에게 우리의 생명이 최우선이 아니라고 상기시켰다; 나라가 최우선이라고. 많은 젊은이들이 나라를 먼저 생각한다. 많은 이들이 가서 그들의 전부를 바쳤고; 많은 이들이 죽었다.

제2차 세계대전에서 일본군은 종종 군인들이 있는 참호에 몰래 다가가 수류탄을 던지려 했다. 많은 경우 일본군이 원하던 대로 끝나지 않았는데, 누군가가 수류탄 위로 뛰어들어 폭발을 흡수했기 때문이다. 수천 명이 친구를 구하고 나라를 방어하기 위해 자신의 목숨을 바쳤다. 그러나 분명히 그들의 우선순위가 올바르지 않았다면(자기 자신보다 나라를 먼저 두지 않았다면) 그들은 그렇게 하지 않았을 것이다.

오늘날 미국에서 누군가가 복음을 위해 목숨을 걸면 그는 어리석고 무모하며 미성숙하다는 낙인이 찍힐 것이다. 그러나 우리보다 앞서 그 자리에서 자신들의 목숨을 바친 수많은 이들에 대해 우리는 무엇이라 말할 것인가—오늘 우리가 믿는다고 말하는 같은 것들을 위해 서서 그들의 목숨을 바친 이들 말이다? 그리고 다른 나라들에서 목숨을 걸고 있는 수천 명의 오늘의 이들은 어리석은가? 사도행전의 아주 분명한 예를 보자.

우리가 거기 여러 날 머물러 있을 때에 유대에서 한 선지자 아가보라 하는 자가 내려왔더니 그가 와서 바울의 띠를 가져다가 자기 손과 발을 동이고 말하기를 성령이 이르시되 예루살렘에 있는 유대인들이 이 띠 가진 사람을 이와 같이 동이고 이방인들에게 넘기리라 하더라 우리가 이 말을 듣고 우리와 그 곳에 있는 사람들이 다 그에게 올라가지 말라 간청하였더니 바울이 가로되 너희가 어찌하여 울며 내 마음을 아프게 하느냐 나는 결박만을 받으려 하지 아니하고 또한 주 예수의 이름을 위하여 예루살렘에서 죽기를 준비하였노라 –사도행전 21:10-13.

오늘날 우리가 바울의 행동을 어떻게 생각하겠는가? 바울은 예루살렘에 갔고 급히 잡혀 매를 맞고 감옥에 갇혔다. 그것은 우리 사랑하는 형제에게 시작에 불과했다. 그는 감옥에서 감옥으로 옮겨졌고 결국 참수되어 로마에서 생을 마쳤다. 그를 올라가지 말라고 설득하려 했던 사람들은 무엇이라 생각했을까? 그들은 그를 어리석다 불렀을까? 그들은 고개를 저으며 “내가 가지 말라 했지!”라고 말했을까?

우리는 확실히 알 수 없다. 그러나 나는 바울이 단순히 그리스도의 왕국을 먼저 두었을 뿐임을 확신한다; 그의 생명은 중요하지 않았다. 그는 하나님께 순종하고 있었고 하나님은 그에게 가라 하셨다.

우리가 우리 삶을 사랑할 때, 주 예수의 효과적인 제자가 되기 매우 어렵다. 우리는 하나님의 부르심을 버리고 결국 혼자서, 하나님의 도움 없이 기독교 생활을 하려다 표적에서 크게 빗나가게 된다.

우리가 모든 것, 심지어 우리의 삶까지도 버릴 때에만 진정한 평안과 삶의 목적을 발견하게 된다는 것은 아이러니하다. 그리고 우리가 우리의 생명을 사랑할 때, 바로 그때 우리가 그것을 잃으리라.

일어나라, 하나님의 성도들이여!
더 낮은 것들로부터 벗어나라.
마음과 영혼과 뜻과 힘을 다하여
왕 중의 왕을 섬기라.

일어나라, 하나님의 성도들이여!
그 나라가 더디 이루어진다.
그리스도를 닮은 사랑의 날을 가져오라
잘못의 밤을 끝내라.

그리스도의 십자가를 높이 들라!
그분의 발이 밟으신 길을 밟으라.
인자의 인도하심을 따라 나아가라,
일어나라, 하나님의 성도들이여!

하나님의 백성으로서 일어나 더 낮은 것들을 끊고 하늘의 것을 바라보기 시작하자, 이 땅의 것이 아니라. 그렇다, 우리는 눈에 띄게 될 것이다; 우리는 어리석은 자라 불리고 다른 많은 꼬리표를 붙을 것이다. 그러나 우리는 다시 하나님의 주목을 받을 것이며, 회개의 불길이 다시 타오를 것이다!

Around the world, but particularly in the United States, people seem to value rugged individualism. People who demonstrate this character quality make their own way through life, asking nothing from others and expecting nothing.

I suppose that this idea relates back to the pioneers. These were men and women who trekked across the various new countries looking for a place where they could settle down and call home. There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.

While this may sound like a scenario that demonstrates strength, the truth is somewhat different these days. These days people use technology to deliberately create bubbles of isolation around themselves.

Many older people have found themselves increasingly isolated from friends and family. COVID certainly made this worse, but there were seeds of this seclusion that had been sowed long before COVID was ever heard of.

Isolation is Not a Natural State

Looking back to the Garden of Eden we can see that Adam was created before Eve. While there were lots of animals around, there was no true companionship for Adam. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him … And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him –Genesis 2:18-20.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man –Genesis 2:21-22. Of course, this was the beginning of marriage, but the more important thing to see here is that it is not a normal state for humans to be alone. We desire companionship and not just the companionship of a pet dog or cat.

Isolation can lead to Despair

Perhaps there is no story that demonstrates so clearly the dangers of isolation as the story of Elijah. We know from the biblical book of I Kings, that Elijah was a fiery prophet of God.

He brought word from God to Ahab that there would be no rain and there was terrible drought for the next three and a half years. During that time, Elijah spent time in the wilderness and then with a widow in Zarephath.

The whole time, he was miraculously fed through God’s power, first by ravens and then through God’s provision of flour and oil to a widow, with whom he lived. Through God’s power, he raised the widow’s son to life.

Then came a time when he challenged the prophets of Baal to a match on Mt. Carmel and won a decisive victory for God. Miraculous fire descended from heaven in answer to his prayer. Truly, God was working great things in his life.

Very soon though, Elijah was running for his life into the desert. Jezebel had threatened his life and rather than trusting God, he fled to Mt. Horeb where he heard the voice of God.

When God asked him what he was doing there, Elijah replied, …I have been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away –1 Kings 19:10.

We can see here a big reason for Elijah’s weakness. He felt completely alone. God corrected Elijah’s incorrect assumption when He stated: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him –1 Kings 19:18.

The fact that those men and women existed in Israel did Elijah little good since he didn’t spend time with them. Elijah’s isolation led him to weakness and despair.

The story of Paul comes to mind as well. The Apostle Paul was a man who seemed to have nearly limitless amounts of energy and an unquenchable zeal for the things of God, but his last letter to Timothy from prison revealed a man who felt very alone. Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee… –2 Timothy 4:9-11.

The Apostle was not abandoned. Other than Demas, they had not fled because they were afraid or ashamed of his bonds. He had sent many of his friends away to strengthen the church in various parts of the Roman Empire. Yet, Paul was still feeling isolated and needed the good Christian brothers, Timothy and Mark, to come and encourage him as he faced a martyr’s death.

Isolation is Physically Harmful

Studies have showed that isolation is linked to higher rates of high blood pressure, heart disease, anxiety, and depression. Older people who are isolated often show signs of mental decline and can experience worsening dementia.

Many times, as people age, they experience the deaths of loved ones. The loss of a spouse can lead older people to withdraw from others and to experience loneliness and isolation. This in turn often leads to rapid progression of the aging process.

Science does not fully understand it, but loneliness leads to increased inflammation and poorer immune function. This in turn can lead to lonely people getting worse infections and struggling to recover after such an infection.

While we think of these problems as those that primarily affect elderly people, they can affect younger people as well. In younger people, often loneliness doesn’t lead to memory issues, but it certainly can lead to things like depression, and it can make chronic inflammatory diseases much worse.

The Opposite of Isolation

If asked what the opposite of isolation is most people would probably answer “Companionship” or maybe even “Friendship”. There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.

The Greek word translated fellowship in the New Testament is “Koinonia” and in the Bible it speaks of relationships that are founded on a shared love for God and for the church—a unity of belief and desire. Christian fellowship includes concepts like praying together, encouraging one another, and even suffering together.

I am afraid that many today find themselves in one of two dangerous situations. First, they may not be a member of any church congregation. While this may be unavoidable in certain mission outreach situations, it is not ideal, and most certainly it should not be a normal situation. At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed. We need fellowship, both to encourage us and to keep us accountable.

The second dangerous situation is that many believers, while members of a church, isolate themselves within that church. If you are a member of a large church congregation, it is easy to blend in and not develop relationships with others. This is just as harmful as not being a member of a church body. Too many people feel lonely, even when there are lots of people around.

Scripture makes it clear that we need a church body. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching –Hebrews 10:25.

There are many people who have lives that are full of friends and acquaintances, but if they do not have a place where they receive fellowship, they are missing out.

When I see people in my office who are struggling with depression there are two things I always tell them to do for themselves.

First is to start exercising. There have been several studies that compared exercise to antidepressants and found that it had similar effectiveness to many of the commonly prescribed antidepressant medications. This doesn’t have to be really vigorous exercise, but it does need to be aerobic (enough to raise the heart rate) and consistent.

The second is to become active in a church congregation; it is not enough to just attend church. Having brothers and sisters to pray for someone who is struggling, to listen to the discouraging situations, and to encourage that person to a more vibrant walk with God is really helpful.

Unfortunately, when someone is struggling with depression, the last thing they seem to want to do is make the effort to be around other people, which contrary to their feelings, is counterproductive to changing the problem.

As we consider this, it should move us to reach out to those who we know are struggling with isolation.

When someone loses a spouse, they often have a lot of encouragement for the first several weeks, but we need to make certain that they continue to have an active presence in their lives in the months that follow.

For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:5, should not give us excuse to not obey God’s command to Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2. The family of God is given no time limit on bearing burdens. There is only a mandate that as we see our brother or sister struggling, we are to help them, as we are able.

The blessing is that someday, when we are struggling, we will have men and women of faith around us to encourage us and to pray for us. We cannot carry these burdens alone. Together, we will reach the Celestial City.

Isolation comes for many reasons. Sometimes it seems to be a chosen way of life, as is the natural tendency of introverted people. Sometimes it is foisted upon a person due to deaths of loved ones or other significant losses. Either way, it is not a healthy place to live.

As we find ourselves in these situations, we need to reach out for fellowship. The family of God is there for us if we only reach out.

As we see others who are struggling, we need to extend to them the right arm of fellowship. As we do so, we may, through our small efforts, help someone emotionally, physically, and spiritually, simply by being a friend in a time of isolation.

Во всем мире, но особенно в Соединенных Штатах, кажется, ценят жёсткий индивидуализм. Люди, демонстрирующие это качество характера, пробиваются через жизнь сами, ни о чем не прося и ни на что не рассчитывая.

Полагаю, что эта идея восходит к пионерам. Это были мужчины и женщины, которые пересекали разные новые земли в поисках места, где могли бы осесть и назвать домом. Там было мало лавок общего назначения, и по возможности они жили настолько самодостаточно, насколько могли.

Хотя это может звучать как проявление силы, правда сегодня несколько иная. В наши дни люди с помощью технологий сознательно создают вокруг себя пузыри изоляции.

Многие пожилые люди оказались всё более изолированными от друзей и семьи. COVID, безусловно, усугубил это, но семена такого уединения были посеяны задолго до того, как о COVID вообще стали слышать.

Изоляция — не естественное состояние

Оглядываясь в Сад Эдемский, мы видим, что Адам был создан раньше Евы. Хотя вокруг было много животных, для Адама не было настоящего соучастия. И сказал Господь Бог: не хорошо быть человеку одному; сотворю ему помощника, соответственного ему… И нарёк Адам имена всем скотам и птицам небесным и всем зверям полевым; а для Адама не нашлось помощника, соответственного ему — Бытие 2:18–20.

И повелел Господь Бог глубокий сон на Адама, и уснул он; и взял одну из ребр его, и закрыл место её плотию. И из ребра, которое Господь Бог взял у человека, сотворил он жену и привёл её к человеку — Бытие 2:21–22. Конечно, это было начало брака, но более важное здесь то, что быть одному для человека — не нормальное состояние. Мы желаем общения, и не только общения с питомцем.

Изоляция может привести к отчаянию

Возможно, нет истории, которая так наглядно демонстрирует опасности изоляции, как история Илии. Из книги Царств мы знаем, что Илия был пламенным пророком Божьим.

Он провозвестил царю Ахаву слово от Бога, что не будет дождя, и наступил страшный засушливый период в течение последующих трёх с половиной лет. В это время Илия находился в пустыне, а затем у вдовы в Зарефате.

Все это время он чудесным образом питался по Божьей силе: сначала воронами, затем по Божьему обеспечению — мукой и маслом у вдовы, у которой он жил. По силе Божьей он воскресил сына вдовы.

Затем наступил момент, когда он бросил вызов пророкам Ваала на горе Кармил и одержал решительную победу для Бога. Чудесный огонь с неба сошёл в ответ на его молитву. Истинно, Бог совершал в его жизни великие дела.

Однако очень скоро Илия бежал в пустыню, спасаясь бегством. Иезавель угрожала ему смертью, и вместо того чтобы уповать на Бога, он бежал на гору Хорив, где услышал голос Божий.

Когда Бог спросил его, что он там делает, Илия ответил: …я ревновал очень о Господе Саваофе: ибо оставили Израиль завет твой, свергли жертвенники твои, и погубили пророков твоих мечом; и я один остался, и ищут души моей, чтобы отнять её — 3-я книга Царств 19:10.

Здесь мы видим большую причину слабости Илии. Он чувствовал себя совершенно одиноким. Бог исправил неверное предположение Илии, когда сказал: И ещё оставил Мне семь тысяч в Израиле — все колени, не поклонившиеся Ваалу, и все устá, не поцеловавшие его — 3-я книга Царств 19:18.

Тот факт, что такие мужчины и женщины существовали в Израиле, мало утешил Илию, потому что он не проводил с ними времени. Изоляция привела Илию к слабости и отчаянию.

Также приходит на ум история Павла. Апостол Павел был человеком, казалось бы, с практически неиссякаемой энергией и неутолимой ревностью к делам Божьим, но его последнее письмо к Тимофею из темницы открыло человека, который чувствовал себя очень одиноким. Приди к мне скорее; ибо Димас оставил меня, возлюбив настоящий век, и отошёл в Фессалонику; Крискен — в Галатию; Тит — в Далмацию. Только Лукий со мною. Возьми Марка и приведи с собою… — 2 Тимофею 4:9–11.

Апостол не был оставлен полностью. За исключением Демаса, они не бежали из страха или стыда за его узы. Многие из его друзей он посылал укреплять церкви в разных частях Римской империи. Тем не менее Павел всё равно ощущал изоляцию и нуждался в приближении добрых христианских братьев Тимофея и Марка, чтобы ободрить его перед лицом мученической смерти.

Изоляция вредна для здоровья

Исследования показали, что изоляция связана с повышенным уровнем артериального давления, сердечными заболеваниями, тревожностью и депрессией. Пожилые люди, находящиеся в изоляции, часто демонстрируют признаки умственного упадка и могут испытывать ухудшение деменции.

Многие с возрастом переживают смерти близких. Потеря супруга может привести к тому, что пожилые люди отстраняются от других и переживают одиночество и изоляцию. Это, в свою очередь, часто ускоряет процесс старения.

Наука пока полностью этого не понимает, но одиночество ведёт к увеличению воспаления и снижению иммунной функции. Это, в свою очередь, может привести к тому, что одинокие люди получают более тяжёлые инфекции и труднее восстанавливаются после них.

Хотя мы считаем эти проблемы прежде всего болезнями пожилых, они могут затрагивать и молодых. У молодых однообразно одиночество редко приводит к проблемам памяти, но оно безусловно может вызывать такие явления, как депрессия, и усугублять хронические воспалительные заболевания.

Противоположность изоляции

Если спросить, какова противоположность изоляции, большинство, вероятно, ответит «общение» или даже «дружба». Существует и другое слово с христианским оттенком, которое ещё лучше. Это слово — общение.

Греческое слово, переводимое в Новом Завете как общение, — «koinonia», и в Библии оно означает отношения, основанные на общей любви к Богу и церкви — единство веры и стремлений. Христо́вское общение включает такие понятия, как совместная молитва, ободрение друг друга и даже совместные испытания.

Боюсь, что многие сегодня оказываются в одной из двух опасных ситуаций. Во-первых, они могут не состоять ни в каком церковном собрании. Хотя это может быть неизбежно в некоторых миссионерских ситуациях, это не идеально и, безусловно, не должно быть нормой. По крайней мере, это может создавать чувство изоляции, а в худшем случае препятствовать исполнению многих повелений «друг другу» из Писания. Нам нужно общение — чтобы ободрять друг друга и чтобы иметь ответственность.

Вторая опасность в том, что многие верующие, будучи членами церкви, изолируют себя внутри этой церкви. Если вы являетесь членом большой общины, легко слиться с толпой и не завести отношений с другими. Это столь же вредно, как и не быть членом церковного тела. Слишком много людей чувствуют себя одиноко, даже когда вокруг множество людей.

Писание ясно указывает, что нам нужно церковное тело. Не оставляя собрания своего, как у некоторых; но увещевая друг друга; и тем более, чем более усматриваете близость того дня — Евреям 10:25.

Есть много людей, у которых жизнь полна друзей и знакомых, но если у них нет места, где они получают настоящее общение, они многое теряют.

Когда ко мне в кабинет приходят люди, страдающие депрессией, я всегда говорю им сделать две вещи для себя.

Первая — начать заниматься физическими упражнениями. Было несколько исследований, сравнивавших упражнения с антидепрессантами, и показавших, что упражнения имели схожую эффективность с многими часто назначаемыми антидепрессантами. Это не обязательно должны быть очень интенсивные занятия, но они должны быть аэробными (достаточно, чтобы учащать сердцебиение) и регулярными.

Вторая — стать активным в церковном собрании; недостаточно просто посещать церковь. Наличие братьев и сестёр, которые молятся за того, кто переживает трудности, выслушивают угнетающие ситуации и побуждают человека к более живой жизни с Богом, действительно помогает.

К сожалению, когда кто-то борется с депрессией, последнее, чего он обычно хочет, — это прилагать усилия, чтобы быть рядом с другими, что, вопреки его чувствам, контрпродуктивно для изменения ситуации.

Размышляя об этом, мы должны быть побуждены протянуть руку тем, кого знаем, что они страдают от изоляции.

Когда кто-то теряет супруга, первые несколько недель ему часто оказывают много поддержки, но нужно позаботиться о том, чтобы в последующие месяцы в его жизни сохранялось активное присутствие близких.

Ибо каждый понесёт свою ношу — Галатам 6:5, не должно давать нам оправдания не повиноваться Божьей заповеди: Носите бремена друг друга, и так исполните закон Христов — Галатам 6:2. Семье Божьей не дано ограничение по времени в ношении бремён. Есть только повеление: когда видим страдающего брата или сестру, мы помогаем им, чем можем.

Благо в том, что однажды, когда мы сами будем бороться, у нас будут верующие мужчины и женщины вокруг, которые нас ободрят и помолятся за нас. Мы не в силах нести эти бремена в одиночку. Вместе мы достигнем Небесного Града.

Изоляция наступает по разным причинам. Иногда это кажется выбранным образом жизни, как естественная тенденция интровертов. Иногда она навязывается человеку из-за смерти близких или других значительных потерь. В любом случае это нездоровое состояние для жизни.

Оказавшись в таких ситуациях, нам нужно стремиться к общению. Семья Божья рядом с нами, если мы только протянем руку.

Увидев других, кто страдает, мы должны протянуть им правую руку общения. Делая это, мы, благодаря нашим небольшим усилиям, можем помочь кому‑то эмоционально, физически и духовно, просто будучи другом в время изоляции.

This is the first of a series of articles on “Discipleship.” Today, Jesus is continuing to call men and women to respond to the simple call, “Follow Me.” Jesus is calling each of us to personally “Follow Me.” In this series, we will explore the depth of this simple command of Jesus. Like the disciples, you will find yourself drawn to follow Jesus.

You may experience both exhilaration and apprehension. Exhilaration, as your journey of faith takes you to heights of love that you have never known. Apprehension, as your faith is tested in new and difficult ways.

There is an emptiness in every human heart that only Jesus can fill. There is a purity and beauty in the life of Jesus that resonates with those heart longings. As we walk with Jesus, we find ourselves being transformed. Old things pass away. All things become new. His life becomes our life. His desires become our desires.

Discipleship is incumbent on the believer. Believing in Jesus, repenting of our sins, and receiving the Lord Jesus into our heart are the first steps into a lifelong journey of faith. Discipleship is not an alternate means of salvation. Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free. Following Jesus is not a carnal attempt to merit eternal life. It is the love response of one who has discovered the source of life.

If you join us on this journey, you will discover that following Jesus will lead us into the valley of decision where we will find ourselves compelled to choose between a life of total surrender to Christ or a life of sin and pleasing self.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagine yourself in a ship with one of these brethren. The sun was rising on the eastern horizon. Anticipating another day of fishing the blue waters of the Galilee, you busy yourself with the daily tasks. Fishing has been your life. You are as much at home on the sea as you are in your cottage.

Another day, another catch of fish, and you should be able to keep the creditors at bay for another week. It’s the only life you have ever known. Your father was a fisherman. Your grandfather was a fisherman. It’s a comfortable life. It’s a familiar life.

This morning, as the waves are gently lapping the sandy shoreline, a man approaches. He’s not a total stranger. Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son. He astounds the local rabbi with his knowledge of the scriptures. His character is flawless; He is the friend of all and a stranger to none.

This man, Jesus (that is his name) is drawing near to your ship. As He draws near, He calls out in a rather cheerful voice, “Follow me.”

James looks at John, and together they look to their father Zebedee. His approving nod was all that they needed. Zebedee had worked with his two sons for many years. Perhaps he was hoping that time with the Nazarene would soften the temper of their abrasive characters.

“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” That’s what He called out to Peter and Andrew. They left their little boat full of nets, perhaps tethered to a stump by the shore. What was it about this Man that He could draw disciples after Him with a simple “Follow Me”? Maybe it was a deep longing in the heart of these disciples—a “hope” that following Jesus might fulfill.

Generations of Jewish men had been looking for The Messiah—The Promised One; He who would break the Roman yoke and restore Israel to her former freedom and glory. Jesus was the most promising revolutionary prospect of the day. He would need a following. He would need their help. Little did they realize that day as they dropped their nets and followed Jesus where that journey would lead them. Little did they know that if they followed this Man, they would never be the same.

As Peter, Andrew, James, and John joined with eight others to follow Jesus, they were walking away from the familiar, secure life of the fisherman. They may have thought that following Jesus would be an adventure. They may have thought that after a term of service to the Nazarene, they could return to their fishing boats. As a matter of fact, that is what they did.

After Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection, He made several appearances to His disciples. They had not yet received the Holy Spirit, and, in the midst of this great uncertainty, they could not resist the allure of the familiar. They decided to go fishing, but much to their consternation they had lost the touch. They fished all night and caught nothing. In the morning Jesus was standing on the shore. He told them to cast on the right side of the ship. They cast and were not able to pull in the nets due to the multitude of fish.

Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No. And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes –John 21:3-6.

Have you ever found yourself in a position where you have tried and tried and all your efforts are met with failure? You know what it is to “reach the end of my hoarded resources”. If that is where you find yourself, you are in a position to experience a miracle. God shows himself strong to those who acknowledge their weakness.

When you decide to follow Jesus, He will draw you into such an utter dependence upon Him that you will finally no longer trust in yourself. To become truly like Jesus is to realize with Paul …that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing…. Paul then continues the verse …for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not –Romans 7:18.

Discipleship will lead us into a total abandonment of ourselves to Christ. Just as the disciples could not have fathomed where following Jesus would lead them, neither can we. We make a faith choice. We choose to follow. We commit the details to our Master.

If you want to be like Jesus, you cannot look back. Jesus said: …No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62. Peter looked back. He said, “I go a fishing”. Disillusioned following the crucifixion and glorious resurrection, Peter chose to return to the lifestyle that was familiar to him. He went back to fishing and James and John went with him.

When Jesus appeared on the shore after their long night of fruitless toil, He prepared a fish fry for the weary disciples. As Peter sat munching on a charbroiled fish, Jesus turned to him and said, “Peter, do you love Me more than these?” How gently piercing are the words of Jesus.

Peter responded, “Yes Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.” We do not know how much time passed, but Jesus turned to him again, “Peter…” (actually He called him Simon) “Do you love Me?” Peter gave the same staid response. “Yes Lord, you know that I love you”. It was the right answer, but Jesus was interested in more than just a right answer, so He said to him again, “Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me?”

Peter finally began to feel that Jesus was asking for something more of him—something that pierced his soul through and through. He had begun following Jesus with the desire to receive from Him. Now Jesus is asking him to reciprocate that love.

Scenes of Caiaphas’ house came before him. He saw Jesus being brutally handled, falsely accused, and spat upon. He heard the angry shouting of the Sanhedrin as they called for Jesus’ death. And then there was that persistent young damsel that challenged him that he was one of Jesus’ disciples. He said to her, “I am not”. Three times he had denied knowing Jesus and now three times Jesus has challenged his love.

In anguish of heart Peter cried out, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee”. Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep”. From that day, Peter was a man with a calling, not only to know Christ for the purpose of receiving from him, but also to emulate him. Discipleship is more than merely knowing about Jesus. Discipleship is walking in his footsteps and identifying with Jesus in his ministry and in his sufferings—truly knowing Him.

Jesus is asking you today, “Do you love me?” We all know the right answer, “Yes, of course, I love Jesus.” Then “Love your neighbor” – “Serve the needy” – “Defer to your brother” – “Forgive the one that has offended you”.

Discipleship is very practical in that it moves us beyond the ideological and causes us to become the very hands and feet of Jesus to those around us.

If in your heart you are thinking, this doesn’t sound very appealing, I would encourage you to focus on the moment and the task at hand. Peter walked with Jesus for three and a half years before he received this call from Jesus. Jesus never calls us without equipping us, and He doesn’t equip us until He determines that we are ready. After the Day of Pentecost, Peter was called, he was prepared, and he was equipped. Then God used him mightily to establish the church.

I would like to call your attention to another attribute of discipleship that is sometimes misplaced. Discipleship is never intended to be drudgery. If you find following Jesus to be hard and toilsome, that is evidence that your love has not yet been perfected.

Jesus’ soul-piercing question to Peter was quite simple, “Do you love Me?” It was as if Jesus was testing Peter. [“I have a job for you, Peter, but a prerequisite for this job is your devoted love for Me.”] Discipleship is a love response to Jesus. Our love for Christ makes service a joy. Toil is pleasant and sacrifice is not a loss.

We can best understand this in the context of human relationships. If you are married and you truly love your husband or your wife, you do not even consider it a sacrifice to work for the mutual benefit of your marriage. In the same way, if we are truly in love with Jesus it is not considered toil to work for him. No sacrifice that we make for the kingdom of heaven is a loss.

I welcome you to join us as we explore the realities of discipleship. We will learn from Christ’s example of forgiveness. We will gain a greater understanding of what it means to walk by faith. Jesus taught us to not worry but to trust. He taught lessons on servant leadership and on cross bearing. There is so much to discover when we are walking with Jesus.

Expect to be changed. The teachings of Jesus are revolutionary in that they run counter to our human impulses. Purpose to allow the life of Christ to become your life and you will be amazed by what God will do for you.

Este es el primero de una serie de artículos sobre “Discipulado”. Hoy, Jesús continúa llamando a hombres y mujeres a responder al simple llamado: “Sígueme”. Jesús está llamando a cada uno de nosotros a “seguirle” personalmente. En esta serie exploraremos la profundidad de este simple mandato de Jesús. Como los discípulos, te sentirás atraído a seguir a Jesús.

Puedes experimentar tanto exaltación como aprensión. Exaltación, cuando tu camino de fe te lleva a alturas de amor que nunca habías conocido. Aprensión, cuando tu fe es probada de maneras nuevas y difíciles.

Hay un vacío en todo corazón humano que sólo Jesús puede llenar. Hay una pureza y belleza en la vida de Jesús que resuena con esos anhelos del corazón. Al caminar con Jesús, nos hallamos siendo transformados. Lo viejo pasa. Todas las cosas se hacen nuevas. Su vida se convierte en nuestra vida. Sus deseos se convierten en nuestros deseos.

El discipulado incumbe al creyente. Creer en Jesús, arrepentirse de nuestros pecados y recibir al Señor Jesús en nuestro corazón son los primeros pasos hacia un viaje de fe de toda la vida. El discipulado no es un medio alternativo de salvación. Seguir a Jesús es la respuesta de un alma liberada. Seguir a Jesús no es un intento carnal de merecer la vida eterna. Es la respuesta de amor de quien ha descubierto la fuente de la vida.

Si te unes a nosotros en este camino, descubrirás que seguir a Jesús nos conducirá al valle de la decisión donde nos veremos compelidos a escoger entre una vida de entrega total a Cristo o una vida de pecado y complacencia propia.

Y Jesús, andando junto al mar de Galilea, vio a dos hermanos, Simón que se llama Pedro, y Andrés su hermano, echando la red en el mar; porque eran pescadores. Y les dice: Venid en pos de mí, y haré que seáis pescadores de hombres. Y ellos, luego, dejando las redes, le siguieron. Y yendo de allí, vio a otros dos hermanos, Jacobo hijo de Zebedeo, y Juan su hermano, en la barca con Zebedeo su padre, remendando las redes; y los llamó. Y luego ellos, dejando la barca y a su padre, le siguieron –Mateo 4:18-22.

Imagínate en una barca con uno de esos hermanos. El sol se levantaba en el horizonte oriental. Anticipando otro día de pesca en las azules aguas de la Galilea, te ocupas en las tareas diarias. La pesca ha sido tu vida. Estás tan a gusto en el mar como en tu cabaña.

Otro día, otra captura de peces, y deberías poder mantener a raya a los acreedores por otra semana. Es la única vida que has conocido. Tu padre fue pescador. Tu abuelo fue pescador. Es una vida cómoda. Es una vida familiar.

Esta mañana, mientras las olas acarician suavemente la orilla arenosa, se acerca un hombre. No es un completo desconocido. Todos saben del hijo de María. Todos tienen una opinión sobre el hijo de María. Asombra al rabino local con su conocimiento de las Escrituras. Su carácter es impecable; es amigo de todos y extraño para ninguno.

Este hombre, Jesús (ese es su nombre) se aproxima a tu barca. Al acercarse, llama en una voz bastante alegre: “Sígueme”.

Jacobo mira a Juan, y juntos miran a su padre Zebedeo. Su asentimiento aprobatorio fue todo lo que necesitaban. Zebedeo había trabajado con sus dos hijos por muchos años. Quizás esperaba que el tiempo con el nazareno ablandara el temperamento de sus caracteres ásperos.

“Sígueme, y yo os haré pescadores de hombres.” Eso fue lo que gritó a Pedro y a Andrés. Ellos dejaron su pequeña barca llena de redes, quizás atada a un tronco en la orilla. ¿Qué había en este Hombre que podía atraer discípulos tras Él con un simple “Sígueme”? Tal vez fue un anhelo profundo en el corazón de estos discípulos—una “esperanza” de que seguir a Jesús podría cumplirla.

Generaciones de hombres judíos habían esperado al Mesías—Al Prometido; Aquel que rompería el yugo romano y restauraría a Israel a su antigua libertad y gloria. Jesús era la perspectiva revolucionaria más prometedora del día. Necesitaría seguidores. Necesitaría su ayuda. Poco se daban cuenta aquel día, al dejar sus redes y seguir a Jesús, adónde los llevaría ese camino. Poco imaginaban que si seguían a este Hombre, nunca serían los mismos.

Cuando Pedro, Andrés, Jacobo y Juan se unieron con otros ocho para seguir a Jesús, estaban abandonando la vida conocida y segura del pescador. Podían pensar que seguir a Jesús sería una aventura. Podían pensar que después de un periodo de servicio al nazareno, podrían regresar a sus barcas de pesca. De hecho, eso fue lo que hicieron.

Después de la crucifixión y resurrección de Jesús, Él se manifestó varias veces a sus discípulos. Aún no habían recibido el Espíritu Santo y, en medio de esa gran incertidumbre, no pudieron resistir el atractivo de lo familiar. Decidieron ir a pescar, pero para su consternación habían perdido la mano. Pescaron toda la noche y no atraparon nada. Por la mañana Jesús estaba de pie en la orilla. Les dijo que arrojaran la red al lado derecho de la barca. La arrojaron y no pudieron tirar de las redes por la multitud de peces.

Simón Pedro les dice: Voy a pescar. Le dicen: Vamos también nosotros contigo. Salieron y entraron en la barca inmediatamente, y aquella noche no cogieron nada. Pero cuando ya amanecía, se presentó Jesús en la playa; mas los discípulos no sabían que era Jesús. Entonces Jesús les dijo: Hijitos, ¿tenéis nada de comer? Le respondieron: No. Y él les dijo: Echad la red a la derecha de la barca, y hallaréis. Entonces la echaron, y ya no podían sacarla por la multitud de peces –Juan 21:3-6.

¿Te has encontrado alguna vez en una situación en la que lo intentas una y otra vez y todos tus esfuerzos se encuentran con el fracaso? Sabes lo que es “llegar al fin de mis recursos acumulados”. Si es ahí donde te hallas, estás en posición de experimentar un milagro. Dios se muestra fuerte a los que reconocen su debilidad.

Cuando decides seguir a Jesús, Él te atraerá a tal dependencia absoluta de Él que finalmente ya no confiarás en ti mismo. Llegar a ser verdaderamente como Jesús es darse cuenta, con Pablo, …que en mí (esto es, en mi carne) no mora el bien… Pablo continúa el versículo …porque el querer está en mí, pero el cómo efectuar lo bueno no lo hallo –Romanos 7:18.

El discipulado nos conducirá a un abandono total de nosotros mismos a Cristo. Así como los discípulos no pudieron concebir adónde los llevaría seguir a Jesús, tampoco nosotros podemos. Tomamos una decisión de fe. Elegimos seguir. Confiamos los detalles a nuestro Maestro.

Si quieres ser como Jesús, no puedes mirar atrás. Jesús dijo: …Ninguno que puso la mano en el arado y mira atrás, es apto para el reino de Dios –Lucas 9:62. Pedro miró atrás. Dijo: “Voy a pescar”. Desilusionado tras la crucifixión y la gloriosa resurrección, Pedro escogió volver al estilo de vida que le era familiar. Volvió a pescar y Jacobo y Juan fueron con él.

Cuando Jesús apareció en la orilla después de su larga noche de trabajo infructuoso, preparó una fritura de pescado para los discípulos cansados. Mientras Pedro masticaba un pescado asado, Jesús se volvió hacia él y dijo: “Pedro, ¿me amas más que éstos?” Qué palabras tan suavemente penetrantes las de Jesús.

Pedro respondió: “Sí, Señor, tú sabes que te amo.” Jesús dijo: “Apacienta mis corderos.” No sabemos cuánto tiempo pasó, pero Jesús se volvió a él otra vez, “Pedro…” (en realidad lo llamó Simón) “¿me amas?” Pedro dio la misma respuesta acostumbrada. “Sí, Señor, tú sabes que te amo”. Era la respuesta correcta, pero a Jesús le interesaba más que una respuesta correcta, así que le dijo de nuevo: “Simón, hijo de Jonás, ¿me amas?”

Pedro finalmente empezó a sentir que Jesús le pedía algo más—algo que le atravesaba el alma de parte a parte. Había comenzado a seguir a Jesús con el deseo de recibir de Él. Ahora Jesús le está pidiendo que corresponda ese amor.

Se le aparecieron escenas de la casa de Caifás. Vio a Jesús siendo tratado brutalmente, acusado falsamente y escupido. Oyó los gritos airados del Sanedrín pidiendo la muerte de Jesús. Y luego estuvo aquella joven persistente que lo desafió diciendo que él era uno de los discípulos de Jesús. Él le dijo: “No lo soy”. Tres veces negó conocer a Jesús y ahora tres veces Jesús ha desafiado su amor.

En angustia de corazón Pedro clamó: “Señor, tú lo sabes todo; tú sabes que te amo”. Jesús le dijo: “Apacienta mis ovejas”. Desde ese día, Pedro fue un hombre con un llamado, no sólo a conocer a Cristo con el propósito de recibir de él, sino también a emularlo. El discipulado es más que simplemente saber acerca de Jesús. El discipulado es andar en sus pasos e identificarse con Jesús en su ministerio y en sus sufrimientos—conocerle verdaderamente.

Jesús te está preguntando hoy: “¿Me amas?” Todos sabemos la respuesta correcta: “Sí, por supuesto, amo a Jesús.” Entonces “Ama a tu prójimo” – “Sirve a los necesitados” – “Cede a tu hermano” – “Perdona a quien te ha ofendido”.

El discipulado es muy práctico en cuanto nos mueve más allá de lo ideológico y nos hace ser las mismas manos y pies de Jesús para los que nos rodean.

Si en tu corazón piensas, esto no suena muy atractivo, te animaría a que te concentres en el momento y en la tarea presente. Pedro caminó con Jesús durante tres años y medio antes de recibir este llamado de Jesús. Jesús nunca nos llama sin equiparnos, y no nos equipa hasta que determina que estamos listos. Después del día de Pentecostés, Pedro fue llamado, preparado y equipado. Entonces Dios lo usó poderosamente para establecer la iglesia.

Me gustaría llamar tu atención hacia otro atributo del discipulado que a veces se malinterpreta. El discipulado nunca pretende ser tedioso. Si encuentras que seguir a Jesús es duro y trabajoso, eso es evidencia de que tu amor aún no ha sido perfeccionado.

La pregunta que traspasó el alma de Jesús a Pedro fue bastante simple: “¿Me amas?” Era como si Jesús estuviera probando a Pedro. [“Tengo un trabajo para ti, Pedro, pero un requisito previo para este trabajo es tu amor devoto por mí.”] El discipulado es una respuesta de amor a Jesús. Nuestro amor por Cristo hace que el servicio sea una alegría. El trabajo es placentero y el sacrificio no es una pérdida.

Podemos entender esto mejor en el contexto de las relaciones humanas. Si estás casado y realmente amas a tu esposo o a tu esposa, ni siquiera consideras un sacrificio trabajar para el beneficio mutuo de tu matrimonio. De la misma manera, si realmente estamos enamorados de Jesús, no se considera trabajo esforzarse por él. Ningún sacrificio que hagamos por el reino de los cielos es una pérdida.

Te invito a unirte a nosotros mientras exploramos las realidades del discipulado. Aprenderemos del ejemplo de perdón de Cristo. Gozaremos de una mayor comprensión de lo que significa caminar por fe. Jesús nos enseñó a no preocuparnos sino a confiar. Dio lecciones sobre liderazgo servicial y sobre llevar la cruz. Hay tanto que descubrir cuando caminamos con Jesús.

Espera ser cambiado. Las enseñanzas de Jesús son revolucionarias en tanto que van en contra de nuestros impulsos humanos. Decide permitir que la vida de Cristo se convierta en tu vida y te sorprenderás de lo que Dios hará por ti.

Ellie edged her chair closer to the grown-ups who were visiting in the kitchen. Grandpa, Grandma, and Aunt Lily had stopped by for a visit, and although she didn’t always understand the conversation, she loved to listen. She found that she learned a lot of things that way.

The topic this evening was about something related to church and that got her mind to thinking about singing during Sunday morning worship services. Although Ellie was only five years old, she very much loved to sing. She thought about the fact that her dear Grandpa was a song leader in their church and how much she liked when he led a song.

At Ellie’s church the song leaders all sat around a table near the center of the church. They took turns choosing a song and then leading it for the congregation. Ellie didn’t always know the songs that were chosen. They sang out of a little black hymnbook that had lots of songs with hard words and tunes she didn’t recognize. However, in the back of this little songbook was a section called “The Appendix” and here were hymns that were familiar to her and she was always pleased when a song was announced from that part of the book. Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight. When that particular song number was announced on a Sunday morning, she always felt a twinge of excitement. She would be able to help along with this song!

I wish we would sing that song again, thought Ellie. It’s been a long time since we have.

Then a sudden thought struck her. Why couldn’t she ask Grandpa to choose that song next Sunday?

Yes, I will ask him and see what he says about that idea, she smiled to herself. She decided to wait until her grandparents were ready to leave. She followed Grandpa out the door and as he walked across the porch, she quickly stepped up next to him. “Grandpa,” she asked. “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!” She felt suddenly shy at having asked such a question, and she ducked back toward the doorway of the house.

Grandpa smiled down at her. “I think I can do that. Is that a song you like?” His eyes twinkled at Ellie. “I’ll be happy to lead that one just for you.”

Ellie could scarcely wait for church the following Sunday. She would get to sing “her” song. Grandpa said he would choose it and she had no doubt he would do as he said.

Sunday morning, she waited eagerly for the song service to begin. The first and second songs were ones that were not familiar to her. Then came time for the third one. “Let’s sing number 8 in the Appendix,” announced the song leader. Ellie’s heart sang. They were going to sing her favorite song. Her grandpa had honored her request. Her eyes shone as she joined in the singing of the beautiful song. It was a lovely hymn that spoke of Jesus’ care as a Shepherd and a Friend, and how He would always keep His children close to Himself.

Later, after church was over and they were on their way home, Ellie remarked to her mother, “Grandpa chose that one song, just like I asked him to!”

Ellie’s mom looked a bit startled. “You asked him to lead a song today? When did you ask him?”

“Yes, I did. The other evening when they visited, I asked him if he could lead it today and he said he would. And he did!” Ellie said with delight.

Mom had a strange look on her face, and she was quiet for a moment.

“Did you know that Grandpas weren’t there today? At the last minute they decided to visit elsewhere this morning for church.” Mom smiled tenderly at her little daughter. “It seems that God knew what a little girl’s heart was desiring and He led another brother to choose the song you like so much.
